Sports.title: Washington Spirit provide hope and joy in a city that badly needs it
Sports.content:
In the moments after the Washington Spirit’s 2-1 semi-final victory over the Utah Royals last weekend, all of Audi Field was in rapture. In the stands, around 20,000 Spirit supporters had filled the stadium to capacity, the sixth time they’d done so in 2026. They filled the place with the type of wondrous noise that’s become alien in DC sports in recent years, the type of gleeful adoration reserved for the city’s rare winners. The Spirit will return to their home stadium to face the Kansas City Current in the NWSL championship this Saturday.

In short order, the Spirit’s players made their way to the north end of the stadium, taking their celebrations into the crowd with their supporters. Perhaps no player has done more to push the Spirit into not only local but national relevance than US women’s national team forward Trinity Rodman, and Rodman herself grabbed a flag from a fan, jubilantly waving it above the crowd. Moments later, she bolted back onto the field and track down the club’s owner, Michele Kang, cajoling the businesswoman into a celebratory dance.

In the echo of all of this, many media members covering the match in the press box received an email from DC United, the local Major League Soccer club that operates and rents out Audi Field to the Spirit. It was a press release announcing the dismissal of their head coach, René Weiler. As the Spirit celebrated a third consecutive championship appearance on the pitch below, some unfortunate soul in a nearby office was tasked with sending that notice, the final nail in yet another dreadful season. While the women have thrived, the local men’s team has not made the playoffs in nearly a decade.

The Spirit, who share not only United’s stadium but also their training facility, are not asking to be compared to them. In reality no NWSL team is, as the audiences for men’s and women’s teams in the same city frequently prove to be quite different. Yet the differing fortunes of the two clubs and the stark difference in atmosphere at their games makes it nearly impossible not to do so. Once-mighty United, four-time MLS Cup champions, have become a laughingstock. That has not stopped the club’s ownership from seeking hundreds of millions of dollars from the DC government to renovate their eight-year-old stadium. While they lobby for that assistance, their matches have become borderline funerary affairs.

The Spirit? The club has become a beacon of hope and joy in a city that badly needs it. The District is a wildly diverse, deeply progressive place and its residents have struggled at times to come to terms with the political realities of hosting the current presidential administration. Thousands of National Guard troops roam the streets, more than a year into an anti-crime deployment that many believe hasn’t helped the city at all. In the shadow of all of this, Spirit matches have become a refuge. And while much of that relief comes from soccer the club plays – technical, entertaining – much of it comes from a deeper place.

View image in fullscreen Washington Spirit owner, Michele Kang, alongside Washington Commanders minority co- owner, Magic Johnson. The teams’ strong ties could lead to a change of home venue for the former.

Photograph: Brad Mills/USA Today Sports

“I think it’s the way that we bring the fans into everything that we do,” Rodman told the Guardian. “I think the way we interact with them after games, it’s not just a meet and greet. We truly do have conversations, and it feels like they’re our friends in a way. I think that’s amazing. The way that we celebrate, we’re always celebrating and interacting with them in the stadium - I feel like it’s a very safe, inclusive environment.

“There is always new people coming to each and every game and what I’ve heard is that everybody feels comfortable when they come to a game, there’s so many friends made. The comfort in it, the safety, the inclusivity of it at all.”

The Spirit have been mentioned as potential benefactors of United’s push for renovations at Audi Field, but Spirit ownership has long harbored bigger ambitions. The club have strong ties to the NFL’s Washington Commanders, who are moving into a new 65,000-seat home as part of a $4bn deal in the coming years, and “opportunities for women’s soccer” made up part of the pitch for that stadium’s public funding. Kang has spoken about aspirations of constructing a standalone training facility and moving the club out of the one it shares with United, a glorified collection of shipping containers in exurban Loudoun county, Virginia.

“I’m hoping in the future we do have that,” said Rodman. “Especially with how great we’ve done and how this organization is as a whole, that would be the cherry on top. Sharing facilities isn’t the greatest for anybody; to be able to have our own facilities with our own logos on it, our own space, not worried about timing would be great and I’m hoping it happens soon.”

All of it feels plausible. Should the Spirit remain competitive, and continue to endear to the District’s residents, it almost feels probable.

Sports.title: Huge crowd gathers for funeral of Irish boxer Lee Reeves after he passed away following knockout in the ring and three-month coma
Sports.content:
Huge crowds have gathered today for the funeral of Irish boxer Lee Reeves who died this week.

The 31-year-old died in hospital on Monday after being placed in a medically induced coma following a fight in August.

After being knocked down twice in the 10th round, the Irish southpaw was carried from the ring on a stretcher following his defeat to fellow countryman Gary Cully and taken to hospital.

His promoters, Queensberry, later revealed he was in a 'critical but stable' condition before undergoing surgery.

Reeves was then placed in an induced coma, where he remained until his death three months later, surrounded by his family.

Along with being a professional boxer, Reeves was a serving member of the 12th Infantry Battalion out of Sarsfield Barracks, an ambassador for Limerick Treaty Suicide Prevention and a model.

A large crowd gathered at the Church of Our Lady, Queen of Peace for the funeral mass in Roxboro, Limerick, on Friday, with thousands also tuning in to a livestream of the service.

Dreams by The Cranberries played in the church as the coffin carrying Reeves' body, draped in the Irish tricolour, was carried inside.

Irish boxer Lee Reeves died on Monday after spending three months in a medically-induced coma

Family members accompanied the hearse carrying the coffin of boxer Lee Reeves arriving at Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, for his funeral with full military honours on Friday

Members of the Irish Defence Forces carry the coffin of boxer Reeves out of Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, on Friday

It had been brought to the church on an adapted gun carriage, as part of the military honours for the service.

His Defence Forces cap was also placed on the coffin.

Reeves' boxing gloves and belt, his Bible, and a pizza box were among items placed at the altar to represent his interests including his love of his religion – along with photographs of the Limerick-born boxer.

The mass heard tributes from some of his four sisters: Louise, Shannon, Jodie and Jessie, who described him as 'one of the greatest men on this earth' and 'an inspiration to everyone he met'.

Jodie told the funeral mass that Reeves was a family man who 'did everything' for his sisters.

'He was my mother's whole life, and she was his. He dedicated every fight to her, and no doubt made her proud.

'She was his number one supporter from day one.

'You were a father to us all, and that even includes Dad.'

She added: 'Nothing is going to be the same without you around, but I promise you'll never be forgotten.'

Jodie, also reading a tribute from Reeves' father, said: 'You had a heart and a presence that touched so many lives.'

Continuing that tribute, she added: 'God knows how much we will miss you, and how much of a piece of our hearts will go with you. Rest easy, son.'

Reeves had been carried out of the ring on a stretcher after his defeat to his countryman Gary Cully and taken to hospital (Source: Instagram/Lee Reeves)

A car is pictured following the funeral cortege of Reeves as it leaves Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, after his funeral mass on Friday

Wreaths and tributes are seen on display before the funeral of boxer Lee Reeves at Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick,on Friday

Shannon said: 'I will miss you every day that I'm on this earth.'

She added: 'You never deserved this, brother, but it's not the end.

'Your story will live on, and your legacy will live on.'

Outside, a large screen and several framed photographs depicted images of Reeves and his loved ones as well as his boxing gloves.

The images carried captions such as 'brother', 'son', 'nephew', 'uncle' and 'pride of Limerick'.

Attendees included Mayor of Limerick John Horan as well as Defence Forces colleagues including the General Officer Commanding 1 Brigade, Brigadier General Caimin Keogh and Officer Commanding 12th Infantry Battalion, Lieutenant Colonel Ian Harrington.

Reeves was placed in a medically-induced coma and had emergency surgery after a junior welterweight fight in Dublin on August 1.

He had won 16 of his 18 bouts after turning professional in 2018, with several of his fights in Canada and Colombia.

The hearse is pictured carrying the coffin of boxer Lee Reeves arriving at Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, for his funeral with full military honours, on Friday

Family members stand behind as soldiers from the Irish Defence Forces place the coffin of boxer and serving soldier Reeves on an adapted gun carriage at Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, on Friday

Reeves' August clash with final opponent Gary Cully saw the 31-year-old knocked down twice in the 10th round

He was also a contestant on BBC reality show, Survivor, in 2023.

Defence Forces head chaplain Fr Paschal Hanrahan said Reeves showed physical courage in the boxing ring but also moral, courage and integrity in his mental health advocacy.

'We hold in our prayers today his colleagues serving overseas at this time with the 128th Infantry Battalion in Unifil, along with their chaplain Fr Piotr, who I know are gathered at this very moment in prayer for Lee.

'With all the agility and dexterity of a professional boxer, Lee moves seamlessly from being a model to being a role model in the Defence Forces.

'And those who served with him in Sarsfield Barracks saw our Defence Forces values in the way that he lived.'

He added: 'They saw his respect in the way he treated people, his loyalty in the way he stood by his comrades, and his selflessness in the time he gave to those who needed encouragement.'

Reeves, who was nicknamed 'El Champo', had won 16 of his 18 professional bouts since turning professional in 2018, and had been challenging Cully for the vacant BUI Celtic light-welterweight title.

He had been knocked down twice in the 10th round against Cully before being taken out of the ring, and in his tribute message for his opponent, Cully admitted that he was still in shock at how their match had ended.

Members of the Irish Defence Forces walked in procession alongside the coffin of boxer and soldier Reeves on an adapted gun carriage at Our Lady Queen Of Peace Church, Limerick, on Friday

'I still remember the stadium days when I used to watch Lee in the nationals, the weight above me, and (I would) always be impressed by his fights and his flashy gear,' Cully wrote.

'What a character and a gent. It's never been nothing but love between us champ, can't really believe I'm writing this but RIP brother.'

Sports.title: Josh Hazlewood hints at abrupt exit if Pat Cummins is ousted - and breaks ranks to defend his captain as Sandpapergate claims escalate
Sports.content:
Josh Hazlewood hints at abrupt exit if Pat Cummins is ousted - and breaks ranks to defend his captain as Sandpapergate claims escalate

Cricketer Josh Hazlewood has spoken out in defence of Pat Cummins amid suggestions his captaincy might not survive the Sandpapergate saga.

Cricket Australia is set to publicly back Pat Cummins to remain Test captain this weekend, despite claims by Usman Khawaja, Chadd Sayers and Cameron Bancroft that other members of the Australian team knew about the alleged sandpaper plot in South Africa eight years ago.

Hazlewood, 35, has warned that removing Cummins would divide the squad and described how there had been a 'bit of a pile on the last few days from different people'.

The comments were made in an interview with Code Sports on Saturday, during which the fast bowler was asked if he would consider leaving the team in protest if Cummins were removed.

'I think I'd have to be put in that position to make a decision, but you'd have to think about it,' Hazlewood said.

'I want to back Pat and everything he said in his press conference last week, everything he's done for the last five or six years in particular as captain.

Cricket Australia is set to publicly back Pat Cummins to remain Test captain this weekend, despite claims by Usman Khawaja, Chadd Sayers and Cameron Bancroft that other members of the Australian team knew about the sandpaper plot in South Africa eight years ago

Josh Hazlewood (pictured with wife Cherina Murphy-Christian) has spoken out in defence of Cummins

'To get the group where it is now and in a position where something like that is never going to happen again, I think is just a remarkable job. He's a great leader. If you went around and asked everyone in the team, you'd hear the same response.'

Hazlewood warned that, if Australia turned up for the first Test and Cummins wasn't the captain, that there could be fractures among teammates, saying: 'Honestly, I don't know how that would go.'

He also denied knowledge of the sandpaper plan but said he sympathised with Bancroft, David Warner and Steve Smith, who were sanctioned over the plan.

'Was I an architect in the plan to tamper with the ball with sandpaper? And was I aware sandpaper or foreign substances being used on the field? The answer is no,' he said.

'When it boils down to it I think those two points are crucial.

'Assuming everyone knows and actually knowing everyone knows, that gap is huge... That's a big chasm.'

On Friday, former Australian fast bowler Mitchell Johnson suggested Cummins's 'personal brand' and role as skipper may not survive the scrutiny he has faced.

'I believe Bancroft's account. It comes across as real and I could feel the words as he was saying them,' he wrote in the West Australian.

The ball-tampering plot came to light following the 2018 Cape Town Test

The debate over the scandal was reignited after Usman Khawaja suggested in his newly released book Sabr that the entire team may have known about the use of sandpaper

'The pressure on Cummins is now immense. I think he will still try to stand by what he has said. But I think the public pressure for Cummins to stand down as Test captain now will be too much.

'I just can't see how his captaincy and personal brand survives this.'

The debate reignited after Khawaja suggested in his newly released book Sabr that the entire team may have known about the ball-tampering plot rather than just those officially sanctioned by Cricket Australia following the 2018 Cape Town Test.

Khawaja claimed a player experimented with sandpaper on a ball in the Port Elizabeth dressing room. 'Everyone… was laughing their heads off,' he wrote, adding that Bancroft then volunteered to do it.

Cummins has repeatedly denied having prior knowledge of the plan to alter the condition of the ball during the 2018 Cape Town Test.

When he fronted the media on November 13, Cummins also directly challenged Khawaja's claim that the team knew.

'When he says "We all knew", if by that he means that we knew sandpaper was going out in the field, he's 100 per cent wrong,' Cummins said.

But just days later, in a more than 4,000-word essay, Bancroft claimed he used sandpaper nearly every over in the final session and continued using it for the rest of the Test.

Khawaja claimed a player experimented with sandpaper on a ball in the Port Elizabeth dressing room

'I recall conversations with all the fast bowlers - Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Marsh - about whether it was reverse swinging enough,' he wrote in The West Australian.

Bancroft said he also sought feedback from wicketkeeper Tim Paine. As the wickets fell, he recalled teammates telling him: 'Great work Bang. Keep it up.'

He claimed his use of sandpaper was discussed in front of the group the following morning and that he received encouragement from members of the playing and coaching staff.

Cummins, Hazlewood, Starc and Nathan Lyon had previously addressed what they knew during the Cape Town Test in a joint statement issued on May 18, 2021.

The four said they 'did not know a foreign substance was taken onto the field to alter the condition of the ball' until they saw the images on the big screen at Newlands.

Following Bancroft's lengthy essay, Cummins' manager Neil Maxwell said on Thursday that the Australian captain remained firm in his position, which he has maintained since the 2018 ball-tampering scandal.

Maxwell said Cummins had never wavered in his account of events over the past eight years.

He acknowledged that Cummins felt sympathy for Bancroft, who had endured significant difficulties in the aftermath of the scandal.

Cricket Australia said on Wednesday night it would take time to examine Bancroft's claims before making any further comment.

Maxwell also encouraged people to revisit Cummins' previous interview transcript, insisting the Test skipper had already addressed every question put to him, including those raised by Bancroft's latest comments.

He credited Cummins with helping transform Australian cricket, saying the young player who made a commitment to turn things around in Cape Town had spent the subsequent eight years working towards that goal.

Former Australia coach Darren Lehmann, who was in charge during the scandal, has also promised to address the allegations in the coming days.

Cricket Australia said on Wednesday night it would take time to examine Bancroft's claims before making any further comment.

In a statement, the governing body said it respected Bancroft's decision to share his account and recognised there could be different perspectives on the events of 2018.

It pointed to the independent forum it had established, which will give players and staff involved in the tour a confidential opportunity to provide their own accounts.

Cricket Australia will determine what information can eventually be released publicly after seeking independent advice, with Bancroft indicating he is willing to participate.

Sports.title: Harry Kane's Bayern blow: England captain set to be ruled out for MONTHS after tearing ankle ligaments - and star could need surgery
Sports.content:
Harry Kane's Bayern blow: England captain set to be ruled out for MONTHS after tearing ankle ligaments - and star could need surgery

Bayern Munich fear Harry Kane will be ruled out for months after suffering an ankle injury in their Bundesliga draw against Cologne.

Kane was forced off just 20 minutes into the match at the Allianz Arena following a challenge from Joel Schmied.

The defender had won the ball but caught Kane with his follow through on his ankle.

Kane had initially tried to play on after treatment, before eventually needing to be replaced.

Speaking post-match, Bayern sporting director Max Eberl revealed that Kane has suffered ligament damage.

A Bayern club statement confirmed the blow, reading: 'Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga home match against 1. FC Köln on Friday evening.

Harry Kane was forced off during Bayern Munich's draw against Cologne on Friday night

Bayern confirmed the England captain is set to be out for months following the injury

'This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich’s medical department.

'The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months. Get well soon Harry.'

Kane's absence will be a major blow for Bayern, with the Ballon d'Or winner having scored ten goals in 16 matches so far this season.

Bayern, who are already without Luis Diaz, Saibari and Serge Gnabry, also saw Michael Olise come off at half-time.

The German giants later confirmed Olise had suffered a 'contusion of the forefoot', with the Frenchman set to undergo treatment in the coming days.

It remains to be seen whether Kane - who became England's most-capped player last week when making his 126th appearance in the 2-1 win over Croatia - is at risk of missing the Nations League quarter-final against Norway in March.

Vincent Kompany, who was back in the dugout for the first time since his collapse last month, admitted other players will have to step up for Bayern in the absence of star names such as Kane.

'These are world-class players, you can't replace them, but we have the mentality and we have to bring that now,' Kompany said, as per Bild.

'We need incredible performances from players who may not yet be used to this pressure at FC Bayern.

Bayern were held to a 1-1 draw by Cologne on Vincent Kompany's return to the touchline

'We will all try together to make this situation a positive one for ourselves. FC Bayern does this time and time again, and that's what we want to do now too.'

Bayern were ultimately held to a 1-1 draw by Cologne, with Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore giving the visitors a shock first half lead at the Allianz Arena.

Nathaniel Brown drew Bayern level before half-time, but the hosts were unable to find a winner on Kompany's return.

The draw gives Borussia Dortmund the chance to move to the top of the Bundesliga table on Saturday.

Sports.title: Chelsea slapped with huge £150,000 fine after 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' fan chants in last season's FA Cup tie at Charlton
Sports.content:
Chelsea slapped with huge £150,000 fine after 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' fan chants in last season's FA Cup tie at Charlton

Chelsea have been slapped with a significant £150,000 fine by the Football Association for their fans’ behaviour during an FA Cup away tie at Charlton Athletic more than ten months ago.

It was alleged that in the 56th minute, the visiting supporters at the Valley sang ‘f*** the Pope and the IRA’. A charge followed, and Chelsea were hit with their fine, along with being given an action plan to follow and a formal warning as to their future conduct.

Chelsea tried to appeal being fined £150,000 for the sectarian chanting. They wanted it either removed completely, or at least substantially reduced.

The club attempted to argue that it was excessive despite admitting that approximately 2,500 of their fans may have taken part in the offensive singing. They also noted how Millwall were previously not fined for the same chant occurring.

Their appeal was dismissed and the full scale of their punishment was upheld.

In a statement, Chelsea said of the chanting: ‘We unequivocally condemn this behaviour. Sectarian abuse – chanting that creates division targeted towards a particular religious or political group – and discriminatory language of any kind has no place in our football club.

Chelsea have been hit with a £150,000 fine for their fans’ behaviour during an FA Cup away tie at Charlton Athletic back in January

ALONSO REJECTS 'SOFT' LABEL Xabi Alonso insists his Chelsea stars will show they are not 'soft' after Leeds United rubbed in how often they have bullied their opponents in a video uploaded to their social media. Leeds produced a compilation of clips of their players leaving crunching challenges in on their Chelsea counterparts and capitalising on mistakes made down the years. Daniel Farke's side have won more duels than any other club in the Premier League this season, and Alonso's team crumbled when visiting Sunderland before the international break. That was a game in which Levi Colwill and Co were bullied by Brian Brobbey. Colwill was hooked at half-time in that 1-0 loss at the Stadium of Light. Dominic Calvert-Lewin may now be relishing testing Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, but Alonso said when asked about being seen as weak: 'We focus on not being soft and being competitive. That's our goal. We have played once this year (a 6-3 win for Chelsea in the Carabao Cup). We will play twice more (in the league). We are ready for that. I like that. We will show that.' Calvert-Lewin shares similar attributes to Brobbey in that he is a traditional centre forward who will challenge Chelsea's centre backs. 'It¿s quite common in the Premier League that they have a good No 9,' Alonso said. 'Calvert-Lewin is doing well. He played with England. But it is up to us, how we defend, how we compete in those situations, how we attack the last line, how we attack their defenders. The preparation has, as always, we think been good. We are ready.' Asked if defenders have forgotten how to face such strikers, Alonso added: 'Forgotten? No, no, no, I don't think forgotten. But it's demanding to play against No 9s. They have good movement in the box, out the box. This is the demand. You can ask the full-backs, they have to play against great wingers in one v one situations. But I don't think it's been forgotten. But it's good they are back, these type of players.' Only Tottenham have made more changes to their line-up than Chelsea this season, adding to the suggestion that Alonso is still searching for his preferred style of play. Some have been forced on the Spaniard because of their habit for picking up injuries despite playing only once a week. 'Once you have the whole menu, you can select what you like and I know what I like from the menu,' Alonso said. 'I would like to have more options with the whole squad available but that's something that's difficult to have during the season. I am sure we will get close to that. 'It (the injuries) is a concern. Sometimes you can analyse them and find a reason but sometimes it is difficult to find a reason.'

‘Such behaviour only serves to cause hurt to others and does not represent the values we hold as a club. We want to create a safe and inclusive environment for all, and we have a shared responsibility in delivering this.’

They added: ‘We understand that further incidents risk additional sanctions against the club and are doing everything we can to inform and educate supporters, as well as develop our existing initiatives to prevent, detect and respond to discrimination in future. We know Chelsea fans do not want to see any form of discrimination in our game, and we ask for their support in fostering a welcoming environment at Chelsea matches going forward.’

On the pitch, Chelsea will go into their Saturday clash against Leeds United without star striker Joao Pedro, who has yet to return to training.

Since the Brazilian was sidelined, Chelsea have won only one of their three Premier League games played, beating a beleaguered Manchester United under Michael Carrick. Otherwise, they have lost to Tottenham Hotspur and Sunderland without scoring.

Joao Pedro is still nursing a thigh problem, and has not yet made it outside with his team-mates as Leeds visit Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Chelsea will, however, have Moises Caicedo available after his injury scare during the international break with Ecuador.

‘He's not fit yet to train with the team, so we need to wait a bit longer,’ Alonso confirmed on Joao Pedro. He’s not going to be available for Leeds. We need to see game by game how he's feeling. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.’

Chelsea will have Emiliano Martinez available after recovering from his broken jaw suffered at Everton on October 17. The goalkeeper required surgery following his collision with Jarrad Branthwaite. Alonso confirmed he no longer needs to wear a mask, having been training without it, and the 34-year-old Argentinian could be in line for his first club appearance since his injury.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish's Everton olive branch: Star IS available to return to first team after being axed for skipping training without permission in 'breach of club discipline'
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish has been offered an olive branch by Everton boss David Moyes and said the sanctioned star is available for selection this weekend.

The Manchester City loanee was punished by the club for failing to report to training sessions and missed several matches. He has not featured for four games: one because of illness, then a ‘breach of club discipline’ and a lack of fitness thereafter.

But Grealish will be considered for the squad when the in-form Toffees travel to Brentford on Monday night.

Moyes said: ‘He has served his punishment and we will treat him as we were treating him before.

‘We will get on with things. The team is going really well at the moment and what I don’t want to do is turn it into a Jack story because it shouldn’t be.’

Pushed if that suggests he will not play on Monday night, Moyes replied: ‘He could easily. He is back in the squad, he is a good player. Who knows?’

Jack Grealish is available for Everton again after serving his punishment and regaining fitness

Everton have won their last three games and go into Monday’s match sixth in the table.

Asked what Grealish can offer, the boss added: ‘Jack can offer us a lot. I want more from him, I want him to show more than he has done. I want him to give me more assists, goals.

‘But there's lots of things about him which we need and he's good at retaining the ball, giving us good possession, carrying. So we hope that he can get back to those levels and give us what we need.

‘I think this time last year he was probably sitting on five or six assists so we're hoping to get that.’

Grealish's social media apology came after he featured in a behind-closed-doors match during the international break.

'Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training!' Grealish wrote. 'I want to apologise to the fans (and) everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.

A presentation from Blues past and present. 🤝



Leon Osman and James Tarkowski surprise David Moyes with a memento as he sets a new record for games managed for Everton Football Club (593). 💙 pic.twitter.com/tzFuGeUhFW — Everton (@Everton) November 20, 2026

'I love playing for this club (and) can't wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt.

'See you all soon (blue heart)'.

At the start of his press conference Moyes was presented with a framed memento of his time in charge by defender James Tarkowski and former player Leon Osman after he set a new club record of 593 games in the hotseat.

Moyes said: 'It’s something that I’m really thrilled about but, if I’m being honest, it’s not something I really think about. I understand I’ve suddenly become the manager who’s had more games at Everton than anybody before and that’s a real honour and privilege to be put in that position.'

Sports.title: A footballer who loves getting cards! Tottenham star Tosin Adarabioyo opens up on his passion for collecting as he launches trading card shop in London with Chelsea's Reece James and Levi Colwill
Sports.content:
Tottenham star Tosin Adarabioyo has joined forces with former Chelsea team-mates Reece James and Levi Colwill to launch a trading card shop in London.

Card Cop, opening in Borough Market on Thursday, will sell cards from a variety of sports as well as other collections such as Pokemon and Marvel.

Adarabioyo began collecting as a child and returned to the hobby in 2020. His collection, which he shares on social media, spans a variety of sports and he also has several of Brazilian icon Neymar.

'I’ve been collecting for years, and it’s great to see the hobby continue to grow,' said the 29-year-old, who left Chelsea for Spurs last summer.

'I love collecting. It’s a great way for supporters to connect with their favourite players. I’ve always felt that collectors are some of the most passionate fans.

'I’ve got to know so many collectors through the hobby. Talking about our collections is an instant icebreaker, and I know those conversations can mean a lot. I want to bring more players into the hobby and recreate those moments.

Tosin Adarabioyo, like many footballers, has a passion for collecting trading cards

The new shop is set to open in London's Borough Market next week

Adarabioyo enjoyes collecting cards of former PSG star Neymar, who won 130 caps for Brazil

'Neymar is criminally underrated to me, and I think his cards are too. Some of the images take me straight back to performances I’ve watched over the years. It’s hard to describe, but it’s like bottling up that feeling forever. Football purists will know what I mean.'

West Ham defender Kyle Walker-Peters, who played with Tosin at England youth level, is among backers along with James and Colwill.

Adarabioyo already has an online retail business, The Huddle, with guests such as Dominic Solanke, Robert Sanchez and Adam Wharton all featuring on live streams, opening boxes as fans watch.

Recent figures valued the global sports trading card market at $13.75billion (£10.5bn) in 2025, with that projected to grow to $27.52bn (£21bn) by 2034.

Formula One star Lewis Hamilton got in on the act earlier this year, launching his own venture and a shop in Frankfurt.

The seven-time world champion was already an ambassador for Topps - who also have the licence for Premier League cards - and said: 'I’ve loved collecting cards since I was a kid — Pokemon, football, anything I could get my hands on.

'To now play a role in shaping the future of the category is incredible. We have a significant opportunity to tap into the culture in a way no one has before.'

Sports.title: Houston Rockets' Tari Eason says influencer ex stole his $40K watch and $15K Louis Vuitton duffel bag
Sports.content:
A roughly $40,000 Rolex and a $15,000 Louis Vuitton duffel bag were among the items allegedly stolen from Houston Rockets forward Tari Eason by his glamorous influencer ex-girlfriend, according to a court filing obtained by The Daily Mail.

As was first reported in July, the 25-year-old Eason sought a temporary restraining order against Marilyn Maritza Melo Rodriguez, 32, over accusations of abuse and alleged threats. At the time, Eason blamed Rodriguez for more than $92,000 in damaged and stolen property after she allegedly poured liquid bleach on his clothes valued at $35,000.

Now, as first reported by TMZ, Eason has filed a complaint over the $92,000 in luxury goods he claims he lost in a June 11 confrontation. In total, Eason is seeking nearly $300,000 in damages and other payments under California law, as well as attorneys' fees.

'The defendant submitted to the restraining order until July of 2027,' Eason's attorney Ronald Richards told The Daily Mail in a statement. 'The DV petition referenced property damage and withholding of my client’s personal property. The complaint in simplest terms seeks a civil remedy for theft under California law which provides for treble damages and attorney’s fees.

'We had requested to resolve this portion of our client's claim while we're resolving the DV petition,' Richards continued. 'The defendant [Rodriguez] chose not to resolve it at that time so in order to seek a return of our client’s property and the related property damage, we filed this action for that purpose.

'Mr. Eason does not deserve to have his property damaged nor his personal items taken from him. We will resolve this matter through the court system and hopefully the defendant will cooperate with the return of these items to mitigate her exposure here.'

Tari Eason first filed for a restraining order against Marilyn Maritza Melo Rodriguez in July

Known as Marilyn Melo, Rodriguez is now being sued for nearly $300,000 in damages

The Daily Mail has sought comment from Rodriguez's attorney as well. Previously, a source close to Rodriguez told TMZ that Eason's account of the June 11 altercation was false and misleading.

The ugly accusations against Rodriguez first surfaced over the summer, when Eason filed for a restraining order over his claim that she punched him in the face on June 11 and later had a friend call to threaten him.

'[Rodriguez] had a friend of hers call me to tell me that she would "break both of my legs" and "kill me,"' Eason claimed in his request for a restraining order. 'The person said they would ruin my career. I am a professional basketball player. The person said they were calling for [Rodriguez]. The threats were real and very concerning. I have fear for my life.'

The dispute began when Rodriguez's mother called Eason over to her house, claiming Rodriguez was going to 'hurt herself,' according to the temporary restraining order request, which was granted by an LA County judge.

When Eason got there, he claimed in his filing, Rodriguez confronted him with accusations about another woman.

'I was with [Rodriguez] in front of her mother's house on the steps,' Eason claimed in the July filing. 'I asked her why is she mentioning another woman's name to me over and over again. I told her the other woman only cares about me and is grateful to be with me. [Rodriguez] was upset over that comment and then repeatedly struck me in the face with a closed fist. The blows were violent and physical. My face hurt as a result.'

Later, Eason claimed, Rodriguez went to his rental property where she 'committed felony vandalism and burglary.' Rodriguez was never charged with any crime over the claims.

What went unnoticed in the media at the time were further details about that June 11 altercation. Specifically, Eason's claim that he was robbed of the Louis Vuitton bag, a watch and $2,000 worth of personal items.

Rodriguez, the 32-year-old who goes by Marilyn Melo online, is a model and influencer with more than 700,000 followers on Instagram PHOTO CREDIT: Instagram/@marilyn_melo

Eason was originally selected by the Rockets with the 17th overall pick in the 2022 NBA Draft out of LSU, where he earned First-Team All-SEC honors and was named the conference's Sixth Man of the Year.

The 6ft 8in forward quickly established himself as a core defensive pillar and high-energy spark plug in Houston, earning an NBA All-Rookie Second Team selection during his debut season after playing in all 82 games.

Eason recently solidified his long-term future in Houston after agreeing to a five-year, $81.5 million contract extension with the Rockets.

This season, Eason is averaging 10.6 points and 6.1 rebounds a game, although he has struggled to shoot from the perimeter, making just 26.7 percent of his 3-point attempts for the 12-4 Rockets.

Rodriguez, who goes by Marilyn Melo online, is a model and influencer with more than 700,000 followers on Instagram. She also has her own clothing line, Melo, which doesn't appear to have any affiliation with former NBA star Carmelo 'Melo' Anthony.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi defends Mykhailo Mudryk after on-loan star angered Spurs fans with interview gaffes - including admitting he wanted to join Arsenal
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi defends Mykhailo Mudryk after on-loan star angered Spurs fans with interview gaffes - including admitting he wanted to join Arsenal

Mykhailo Mudryk is still two weeks away from a Tottenham return after a suffering setback to his recovery from an ankle injury.

Mudryk, who has played only 16 minutes since joining on loan from Chelsea, clashed with the Ukrainian FA this week when he blamed them for his positive drug test which ruled him out of football for almost two years.

He also risked the wrath of Spurs fans by admitting he only made the move across London to recover his fitness before returning to Stamford Bridge where Blues boss Xabi Alonso was 'counting on him'.

And he managed to annoy both Chelsea and Spurs fans by revealing, during the same YouTube interview, that he wanted to sign for Arsenal when he moved to the Premier League in January 2023 but his agent forced through the move with the best commission.

'I can understand the fans, but Mudryk is a good guy,' said Spurs boss De Zerbi, who worked with the Ukraine international at Shakhtar Dontetsk and convinced him to resist interest from Brentford and Coventry and be reunited in North London.

'He's a good player. He suffered a lot for the situation in the last couple of years. He has just one thing to do, show on the pitch his qualities, show on the pitch that now he's playing for Tottenham. Tottenham is a big club, like the other clubs, not less at all.'

Mykhailo Mudryk admitted he joined Tottenham to regain fitness before returning to Chelsea, while also stating he had wanted to sign for Arsenal in 2023 before his transfer to the Blues

Roberto De Zerbi acknowledged Tottenham fans' views on Mudryk's comments, but insisted the winger has 'suffered a lot' following his doping ban

Chelsea paid £86million for Mudryk but he made little impression before he was hit with a four-year ban in 2024, which was wiped out this summer enabling him to return to competition.

'He has no responsibility in this part,' said De Zerbi. 'Now his focus is just on the ball or just on the football. He has a big chance to play with us because Tottenham is a big club. He knows very well the coach, he knows very well the style of play.

'He knows I give him total confidence to show what he is. So to move the focus in the right direction, in a good direction. But I think he's working hard to recover and to play earlier.'

Mudryk made his Spurs debut as a sub at Nottingham Forest in September but injured an ankle in training a few days later. He was initially expected to be out for two months with Saturday's game against Ipswich his target to return.

'The plan was to be available for Ipswich or Sunderland,' said De Zerbi, who will serve a touchline ban against Ipswich for three yellow cards. 'Then he felt not pain but he was not comfortable last week. And they take two weeks more, and step by step we're going to see the situation.'

James Maddison's limited involvement for Tottenham relates to a niggling hip injury dating back to pre-season.

Maddison has been an unused sub in two Spurs games since limping off when the problem flared up at Chelsea, on his second start of the season and his second start in six days.

Roberto De Zerbi confirmed ahead of Saturday's game against Ipswich that it had been the same problem which dogged Maddison through the summer as he fought back from a serious knee injury.

The Spurs boss revealed how his physical condition had suffered from not training regularly and reminded the 29-year-old England midfielder he could only make an impact in the Premier League in peak condition.

De Zerbi confirmed James Maddison is available to face Ipswich but stressed the midfielder needs to push himself to reach his peak physical condition

'It is not a big injury, but he was not able to work,' explained De Zerbi. 'He had a problem with his hip. The same as preseason. It's not a big problem but if you don't work consistently you lose the physical condition and to play in this level of competition you have to stay in the top physical condition.'

Maddison, who turns 30 on Monday, missed most of last season with a cruciate knee injury and has played only 195 minutes this season. His return was further complicated by a shoulder injury after coming on at Brentford on the opening game of the season.

'He is still young, 29 years is not old,' said De Zerbi. 'He has to push and demand of himself the top in terms of physical condition, because if he is 80 or 90 per cent of his physical condition he makes the difference for us, he changes the games.'

Maddison and Destiny Udogie have both trained fully through the international break and are available to face Ipswich.

'He worked very well from the Wednesday after Leeds,' said De Zerbi. 'From Chelsea to the Leeds game, he worked just three times on the pitch at the training ground.

'If you don't work during the week you risk injury and lose the normal physical condition you need to play Premier League. The same for Udogie. When they work and are fit to work, they have many chances to play, especially Maddison because a special player.'

Maddison's first start of the season came against Coventry when he scored the opener and inspired Spurs to their first win. He barely trained but started again in the win at Chelsea five days later, where he broke down early in the second half and was replaced by Conor Gallagher.

De Zerbi made it clear there were no problems connected to Maddison being pictured out at a pub in Coventry after the defeat at Leeds. It was the last game before the international break and the first of three days off.

'I am angry because next time he has to invite me,' joked the Spurs boss and he added: 'I am happy. I know when my players work well. If they are serious on the pitch, off the pitch they can do what they want. I'm not a policeman.

'James is top professional, top guy, top player. The private life is not our problem if they work well and they are serious, and give their best for the club, the shirt and the fans, and he is perfect when it comes to that.'

Sports.title: Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi responds to Mykhailo Mudryk's Arsenal transfer admission
Sports.content:
Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi responds to Mykhailo Mudryk's Arsenal transfer admission

Mykhailo Mudryk has not endeared himself to Tottenham fans by admitting that rivals Arsenal were his dream club when he moved to Chelsea in January 2023 for a huge fee

View 2 Images Mykhailo Mudryk has caused a stir with his comments (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

Roberto De Zerbi has defended Mykhailo Mudryk after he angered Tottenham fans by admitting he has dreamed of joining Arsenal.

‌



‌



Mudryk joined Spurs on a season-long loan from Chelsea on transfer deadline day in September. The Ukraine international is looking to get his career back on track after spending 20 months on the sidelines while banned for failing a drugs test.

‌



The 25-year-old has played just 16 minutes for Spurs since his move due to an ankle injury. And his comments in a controversial interview on the Guest of Gordon podcast did not endear Mudryk to his new club's fanbase.

‌



Speaking about the fact he nearly joined Arsenal instead of Chelsea a deal worth a potential £88million in January 2023, Mudryk described the Gunners as "the club I wanted to play for" and said "moving to the Emirates Stadium was my dream".

"Yes, I can understand the fans but Mudryk is a good guy and is a good player," De Zerbi said in a press conference ahead of Tottenham's home game against Ipswich on Saturday.

‌



"He suffered a lot for the situation in the last couple of years. He has just one thing to do. Show on the pitch his qualities and show on the pitch that now he is playing for Tottenham. And Tottenham is a big club like the other clubs, not less at all.

"Now his focus is just on football and he has a big chance to play with us because Tottenham is a big club, he knows very well the coach, he knows very well the style of play and he knows I give him total confidence to show what he is.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 2 Images Roberto De Zerbi defended Mykhailo Mudryk (Image: Hayters TV)

‌



"So, he has to move the focus in the right direction, in a good direction, but I think he is working hard to recover and to play earlier."

Spurs have the option to make Mudryk's move permanent for £75m, but that is currently looking very unlikely. He is still a few weeks away from returning to training and De Zerbi was asked whether the club could cancel his loan in January.

Article continues below

"It is not my part, no?" he replied. "I am a coach and now we have to help him to recover in the best way because I think and I believe he can be very important for us for the specific characteristics he has and for the level of the player."

It is understood that Spurs were not aware of Mudryk's interview, in which he also sparked a row with the Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF) by alleging they were to blame for him testing positive for the banned substance meldonium.

Sports.title: Man Utd CEO Omar Berrada breaks silence on Man City charges with firm message
Sports.content:
Man Utd CEO Omar Berrada breaks silence on Man City charges with firm message

Omar Berrada's time at Manchester City covered most of the years in which the Premier League club have now been found to have committed serious financial breaches

View 2 Images Omar Berrada has spoken publicly about Manchester City's charges for the first time (Image: Sky Sports)

Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada insists that he is "not concerned" about being caught up in the case against former employers Manchester City.

‌



‌



An independent commission recently found City guilty of breaching more than 100 of the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018, having artificially inflated their revenues by £830million using 'sham' commercial agreements. The club deny any wrongdoing and have appealed the verdict.

‌



Berrada joined City in 2011 and worked in the club's commercial and international business departments. He was then appointed chief operating officer in 2016 and worked closely with City CEO Ferran Soriano.

‌



Having moved to United in 2024, one year after the charges were brought against City, Berrada has now spoken about the case in public for the first time. "I'm not concerned," he told Sky Sports.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"I want to be very clear about this: I wasn't involved in any wrongdoings. I wasn't involved in the proceedings. There are no allegations against me. In that sense, there will be no surprises."

It was put to Berrada that should City fail in their appeal, he could lead United in a compensation claim against his old club. "I don't want to comment on that because right now, it's an ongoing process," the 48-year-old added.

‌



"When it runs its course, then we'll take a view of what is our position as Manchester United."

Across town at the Etihad Stadium, City manager Enzo Maresca says that his club are 'convinced' they'll be successful in their appeal. "The reason why I joined this club is I completely trust 100 per cent, the owner, the sporting director, the CEO - all the organisation. I have no doubt about that," Maresca affirmed last month.

‌



View 2 Images Omar Berrada left Manchester City to join United in 2024 (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

"I spoke with the club for sure. Probably the right moment to speak about that is when we're going to win this appeal."

‌



Soriano has also told supporters: "The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began.

"There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies."

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino sends immediate January transfer plea to Man Utd chiefs
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino sends immediate January transfer plea to Man Utd chiefs

Mauricio Pochettino addressed the media for the first time since being appointed Manchester United's new manager, as he previewed Sunday's Premier League game away to Liverpool

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino wants assurances from Manchester United's owners (Image: MUTV)

Mauricio Pochettino has told the Manchester United hierarchy that he wants to be involved in any transfer decisions and reminded his bosses that they work for a 'football club'. Pochettino, 54, outlined his stance in an effort to avoid running into the same problems as his predecessors.

‌



‌



Former manager Erik ten Hag recently bemoaned how Scott McTominay was sold without his approval, while ex-boss Louis van Gaal once labelled United as a 'commercial club, not a football club'. In his first press conference ahead of Sunday's game against Liverpool, Pochettino was asked to define his role and how much of a say he'll have.

‌



"I was in all my career a coach, head coach, manager. It does not change too much," the Argentine replied. "I know as head coach I am the guy who tomorrow will decide the squad for Sunday, pick the 11, make the changes.

‌



"I know in the future, I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that affect the squad. At the end of the day, Manchester United is a football club."

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Pochettino's comments come little over a month before the January transfer window is due to open and after United CEO Omar Berrada told Sky Sports: "When we find the right opportunity, we will spend, but we won't spend for the sake of it."

Michael Carrick suffered the consequences of a lacklustre summer winner and was sacked earlier this month, having overseen just one win from the Red Devils' first 10 Premier League games this season. Pochettino, who's signed a two-and-a-half-year contract, is tasked with turning things around and restoring confidence in the squad that he's inheritated.

‌



"It is normal when you don't win games that the confidence starts to go down," the former USA manager acknowledged. "I think the players need to feel from us that you believe and trust in them, and show that you know what you are doing. That is important.

Will Manchester United beat Liverpool? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images The Glazers have entrusted Sir Jim Ratcliffe with Manchester United's football operations (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

"With the schedule we have ahead we have to settle on our principles. The players are intelligent, they have quality. Sometimes it is unlocking some things that didn't appear for different reasons."

‌



Pochettino flew into Manchester on a private jet from Cincinnati on Wednesday and has had a busy week, starting Friday's press conference only a few minutes after finishing training. "My first target is to sleep, but I cannot sleep," the ex-Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea boss admitted.

"The target is to know the people, the staff, all the people at the club, the players, and to try from the beginning to have an impact. We try to be positive.

Article continues below

"Our most important job is to get the best from the players. We have talented players in the squad. That is our main focus."

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola insists Man Utd have advantage despite Liverpool watching drone training footage
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola insists Man Utd have advantage despite Liverpool watching drone training footage

Liverpool host Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday for Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge after his training session was spied on by a rogue drone operator

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola gave his take on Manchester United's drone incident

Andoni Iraola has insisted that it is Liverpool who will be at a disadvantage when they face Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday.

‌



‌



United come into the weekend 18th in the Premier League table with one win from their 10 matches so far. It will be Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge since jetting in from his previous job in the United States on Wednesday.

‌



Pochettino is facing a huge task to turn around his struggling side and matters weren't helped when a rogue drone operator filmed his first training session on Thursday and uploaded the footage to YouTube. The 12-minute clip has since been deleted, but it appeared to reveal details of Pochettino's tactical work on the training pitch.

‌



Iraola has admitted that he was sent the video and, while he said he felt sorry for Pochettino, he rejected the idea that United had been put at a disadvantage by the drone.

"They sent me yesterday the footage," Iraola said in his pre-match press conference. "But I think the important part is that it shouldn't be legal. It happened to United but it could happen today to me in training you know.

‌



"Yesterday you had access to our training, the cameras in the corridors for 15 or 20 minutes, I don't know how much. You know who's training with us, who didn't train. We know the same (with United).

"But it's not [about] the matter of the advantage, it's about the fact that someone can do this... I think there's a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things that you have to respect and I don't think it's nice for any club, honestly."

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 3 Images Mauricio Pochettino has only had a few days to work before the Liverpool game (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



Iraola even feels that because Pochettino is starting from a clean slate at United, his Liverpool analysis team have been unable to prepare as they would usually.

Asked about knowing Pochettino well, Iraola replied: "We've faced each other and obviously he has lots of Premier League games behind him that we can look at.

‌



"We can look at games from the US, but it's true that they have this small advantage that we don't have references to prepare. They can go different ways and, honestly, we don't know right now."

United have decided not to take legal action against the drone operator, who issued a grovelling apology on Friday morning. A statement read: "I would like to speak about yesterday's incident. A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.

‌



View 3 Images Mauricio Pochettino's first Manchester United training session was filmed by a drone (Image: YouTube)

"My aim was to picture Mauricio Pochettino in his United training kit for the supporters to see for the first time. I had wrongly presumed that with it being close to the start of the session that no meaningful training sessions would have started so would have been some harmless warming up shown.

Article continues below

"I also wrongly assumed that the training session would have been open to various media outlets. I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.

"I would also like to state that Liverpool Football Club or any other football club were not involved in my decision to film at Carrington yesterday. The video has been removed from my channel."
