Sports.title: Chris Eubank Jr in talks to fight Kell Brook in first bout since Conor Benn loss - with 'Special K' to come out of retirement
Sports.content:
Chris Eubank Jr in talks to fight Kell Brook in first bout since Conor Benn loss - with 'Special K' to come out of retirement

Chris Eubank Jr is in talks to fight Kell Brook in his return to the ring.

Brook, 40, has not fought since beating Amir Khan in 2022, but has emerged as a potential option to fight Eubank in his first fight since losing to Conor Benn late last year.

According to Elliott Amoakoh, the executive director of Eubank Jr's management team, Nova Sport LLC, any agreement is still a way away.

He told Sky Sports: 'Talks are ongoing but the date, purse and location are yet to be confirmed.'

Ben Shalom, however, who has represented both fighters in the past, told talkSPORT: 'It's a fight that we have been trying to make for a couple of months.

'They have pretty much agreed terms on both sides, there is just some final bits to go. It is one of the biggest fights in British boxing. I think you are right on February and in Manchester.'

Chris Eubank Jr (pictured) is in talks with Kell Brook to face off in his return to the ring

Brook (pictured) hasn't fought since 2022 and retired after beating long-term rival Amir Khan

Brook retired after beating long-time rival Khan in Manchester, having been linked with a fight with Eubank in the aftermath.

Brook has seemed almost certain to return to the ring, having revealed his return fight would be 'announced soon'.

He retired with 40 wins from 43 fights, and is a former International Boxing Federation welterweight champion.

Having debuted as a professional in 2004, he didn't lose until September 2016, when he was stopped in the fifth round by Gennady Golovkin.

Eubank Jr, meanwhile, had faced questions over retirement following his defeat by Benn but has refused to call it quits on his 15-year career.

He had claimed to have major fights scheduled for 2026, but has taken a whole year out of action.

Sports.title: English boxer, 18, banned from World Championships after extraordinary sex test mix-up: 'Broken' teenager reveals how his dream was shattered after team forgot to prove he was a man
Sports.content:
A teenage English boxer has said they have been left 'broken' after being denied the chance to compete at the World Championships due to officials failing to organise a sex verification test to prove he is male.

George Francis, 18, had been due to represent England at the Under-19 World Championships in Budva, Montenegro last month.

Francis was withdrawn from competition on the eve of the event after an administration error by England Boxing, with the governing body having failed to arrange the necessary sex verification test.

'They got me in a room and told me that I couldn't box because they didn't know if I was a boy or a girl, basically,' Francis told the BBC.

'The explanation was that they couldn't provide a blood sample for me in time. Everyone else was able to provide a blood sample, but they just forgot me.

'Somehow I wasn't on the system.

George Francis, 18, missed out on competing at the Under-19 World Championships after England Boxing failed to arrange a necessary sex verification test. Source: Instagram/georgefrancis_07

'It was the worst news I've ever had in my life.

'I wouldn't wish it on anyone, to be honest. I was just broken. They were speaking to me and I couldn't even really hear. I was devastated.

'I couldn't really talk. I literally couldn't feel anything. There was a hole left there.'

Francis's situation, first reported by The Times, followed the mandatory introduction of sex verification tests by the sport's governing body World Boxing.

World Boxing announced the move last year, with genetic sex testing initially introduced for female competitors aged 18 and above. The governing body stated the move was due to a 'duty of care to deliver safety and competitiveness fairness'.

It followed controversy at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games, where boxers Imane Khelif and Lin Yu-ting won gold.

Khelif and Lin had been disqualified from the previous year's World Championships, with boxing's former governing body – the International Boxing Association – claiming the pair had failed sex eligibility tests.

Earlier this year, Lin was cleared to compete in women's events following a review of her sex eligibility.

World Boxing's mandatory tests were extended to include male boxers earlier this year.

Francis had been required to undergo a test due to turning 18 four days before travelling to the World Championships.

Francis, a multiple national champion, had been required to undergo a mandatory test after turning 18 days before the World Championships. Source: Instagram/georgefrancis_07

World Boxing introduced sex testing last year amid the controversy surrounding Algerian boxer Imane Khelif's participation at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games

The multiple national and GB champion has claimed he is considering turning professional following the mix-up.

England Boxing reportedly contacted Francis's father to apologise for the 'administrative oversight', with the governing body stressing it will 'strengthen processes' to avoid a repeat incident.

'We maintained open communication with George and his family throughout, despite this, a resolution was not possible,' an England Boxing statement read.

'George remained a valued member of the England team, including representing the squad as flag bearer.

'England Boxing has no greater priority than the health and wellbeing of athletes on its performance pathway and are committed to learning from this experience and strengthening our processes to prevent a recurrence.'

World Boxing's policy requires boxers to undergo a once-in-a-lifetime PCR (polymerase chain reaction) test to determine their sex and their eligibility to compete in either the male or female category.

The PCR test is a laboratory technique used to detect specific genetic material, in this case the SRY gene, which reveals the presence of the Y chromosome that is an indicator of male biological sex.

A dozen boxers, representing five nations, were last year blocked from competing at the World Championships in Liverpool because deadlines for their sex tests were missed.

Under World Boxing rules, national federations are responsible for testing and will be required to confirm the sex of their athletes when entering them into World Boxing competitions

Sports.title: Viddal Riley opens up on why he stuck with his dad instead of moving to Las Vegas to train with a Mayweather as he eyes fighting Oleksandr Usyk
Sports.content:
Viddal Riley opens up on why he stuck with his dad instead of moving to Las Vegas to train with a Mayweather as he eyes fighting Oleksandr Usyk

Derrick Riley almost never speaks publicly. Ahead of his son's European title defence against Seydi Coupe at Wembley on Saturday, father and son sat down together to talk about trust, tough love, Joe and Enzo Calzaghe, and why Oleksandr Usyk returning to cruiserweight is 'a little bit greedy'.

But to understand where Viddal is going, you first have to understand the man in his corner.

Derrick Riley has been watching his son get punched since he was a little boy. He still can't put into words what it does to him.

'It's strange,' he exclusively tells Daily Mail Sport. 'I've been doing it for a long time. But you have to try and separate it. You have to shut off the emotion and the sentiment. If you let that sentiment in, I think that's a bad thing. That's your boy in there. He's getting hit and he's getting hurt. I would say it's not easy, and some people can't separate it.'

It's rare to hear Derrick say anything at all. He stays out of the spotlight, and he leaves the talking to his son. Sitting beside Viddal days before the biggest night of his career, when the unbeaten Londoner headlines OVO Arena Wembley against Frenchman Coupe, you quickly see how their relationship works.

'Only my dad would be able to speak to me the way he does,' Viddal says. 'But it comes from a place of genuine care. It's not a job. Someone can only care so much when it's a job. It's like being an employee at a company and having your own business. It's a completely different mentality. This is my business, so he cares and I care.'

WATCH THE EXCLUSIVE INTERVIEW ON THE DAILY MAIL BOXING YOUTUBE CHANNEL

Derrick Riley (R), the father and trainer of son Viddal Riley (L), almost never speaks publicly

Viddal is set to take on Seydi Coupe at Wembley on Saturday evening, headlining the event

Derrick added: 'Part of caring too is the fact it's the same brain you've got now that you're going to need after boxing. You can't go to the shop and buy a new one, so you need to protect it. That's why it's difficult to separate the two.'

Viddal grins and says: 'It's the same brain I need for the grandkids.'

The partnership was not always a given. At 21, Viddal went looking for something of his own.

'I was at a stage where I was trying to find some independence. That's the truth,' he says. 'I was presented with the opportunity to go to Vegas, train with a Mayweather and work with Jeff Mayweather. I was thinking, "Yeah, I'm doing this my way. I'm doing things differently."

'But the truth is, I knew my ceiling was getting lower. And I knew the only person who could push that ceiling higher, and continue to do so, was my dad.

'So when I came back to the UK, I said, "Dad, can you train me?" He was like, "Nah, I'm alright. I'm not doing it." And I was like, "Nah, I need you to do it, because that's the only way this dream we've been talking about is going to be fulfilled."

Derrick's refusal was not stubbornness. It was self-preservation.

When asked why he initially said no, Derrick admitted: 'I know what the game is about. I know what boxing involves, and I thought to myself, do I want that in my life? It's a good question when you're in your 50s. I've lived life. There are no rose-coloured glasses. I know what boxing is. But I had to think about it.'

Derrick Riley has been watching his son get punched since Viddal was a little boy

The irony was that he was already qualified for the job. 'By this point I already had a British Boxing Board of Control licence, because I was in the corner with Viddal in Dubai,' he laughs. 'So, funnily enough, I already had the licence.

'He looked at me with those puppy-dog eyes, and I thought, you know what? We've got to do this. But I did say to him, "It's not going to be easy, son. We're going to have to do this properly. You're going to get no ranking belts, no intercontinental belt, nothing like that. You're going to have to do it the old-school way, with the British, Commonwealth, European, and it's going to be hard." And we've done it, man.'

The record backs him up. Viddal is 14-0 with seven knockouts. He won the European title in April with a wide points win over the vastly experienced Pole Mateusz Masternak at The O2, a fight that also served as an IBF world title eliminator. Saturday is his first defence, and it's a mandatory one against a challenger who is also unbeaten in 14.

For a template of what father and son can achieve together, Derrick points to Wales.

'I appreciate Enzo [Calzaghe] more now than I did before,' he says. 'I've always appreciated him, but I appreciate him even more now because I'm doing it myself. People have no idea what it takes, and for him to do what he did with Joe was absolutely amazing. I take my hat off to him.

'Don't get me wrong, I had a boxing background. I wasn't great, I wasn't pulling up trees, but I had a boxing background. Enzo had no boxing background whatsoever, yet he managed to do what he did with Joe. That is amazing.

'It's funny. During the fight with Bernard Hopkins, I think Enzo was saying something to Joe, and Joe gave Enzo a look. I know that look. I give Viddal that same look.'

Viddal and his father have become a force to be reckoned with but they've faced criticism

Joe Calzaghe has described his own brief split from his father, and how he came back because he realised he wanted those highs to be shared with Enzo. Viddal sees the same story in his own.

'We relate to that story because we were severely doubted,' he says. 'It wasn't celebrated. The partnership is only now starting to get some recognition, with people acknowledging that it works. It wasn't like that at the beginning.

'It's been suggested to me that my dad shouldn't train me and that there are people better suited to the job. That's what we walked into. It wasn't accepted as, "Oh yeah, this is a nice family dynamic, let's get it going." It was challenged. The aim was to separate us.

'When we're up against it, we just keep proving ourselves, time and time again. That's what I take from Enzo and Joe. It wasn't celebrated either. They had to keep doing what they were doing, and he turned his son into a 46-0 fighter and one of the best to have ever done it.'

Fathers who train their sons are often accused of living through them. John Fury, so often more visible than Tyson, is the obvious example. Derrick, a former boxer himself, rejects the comparison.

'I don't live vicariously through Viddal. I don't want that,' he says. 'I'm not hogging the camera. It's not about me. It's about Viddal. He asked me to help him, and I'll help him.'

Viddal is just as clear about who he fights for. 'I do it primarily, first and foremost, for me,' he says. 'And very quickly after that, it's for everyone around me that's put work into me achieving it, because it couldn't be done by myself.

Derrick has said he resonates with Enzo (pictured right) and Joe Calzaghe (pictured left)

'When I became British champion, it made me give my dad the belt. We sat down at home for years watching people pick up the Lonsdale belt and hold the Lonsdale belt. So I heard the announcement, "British champion", and I'm like, "Dad, hold this." That's something he's always deserved.'

By rights, Viddal should already have fought for a world title. When Jai Opetaia was stripped of the IBF belt after signing with Zuffa Boxing, the Masternak win put Viddal in line for a shot at the vacant title against New Zealand's David Nyika. Then Opetaia sued the IBF, the governing body held off sanctioning the fight, and Viddal was left waiting.

At the same time, the division has been turned upside down. Opetaia is moving up to heavyweight to face Deontay Wilder on the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua card in Cardiff on December 11. David Benavidez holds the WBA and WBO belts and faces WBC champion Michal Cieslak next month. And now Oleksandr Usyk wants to come back down.

'As I have been saying, it's messy, but I'm trying to get in the mess,' Viddal says. 'I don't want to be on the outskirts of that mess. I'm trying to be in it.

'Right now, I'm just on the outside of the door. I can hear the music in the club, I can hear the bassline. I know there's a vibe in there. I've been seeing the people getting in the door, walking past me. I want to get in there. And Coupe this weekend is another step towards that.'

The most famous person trying to get through that door is Usyk. The Ukrainian became undisputed at cruiserweight, moved up to become undisputed twice at heavyweight, and his team says he now plans to return to 200lbs to chase Benavidez and become undisputed at cruiserweight again. He hasn't fought at the weight since knocking out Tony Bellew in November 2018, and he turns 40 in January.

Viddal admires him. But he isn't convinced.

'It's a bit greedy. It's a little bit greedy,' he says. 'He's completed the level here. He's gone up, he's completed it there, and I think he's just needing that challenge. He's a guy you can tell lives for challenge. All he does is take challenges. "If I'm fighting for a world title, I'm going to go to your country and I'll beat you there." He's that character. That's what makes him a GOAT. That's what makes him a legend.

Viddal has said Oleksandr Usyk is 'greedy' for returning to the cruiserweight division

'But it's dangerous too. Forty years old, dropping all that weight. He hasn't been a cruiserweight since 2018. If I'm in his circle, I'm saying, "Bro, you ain't got to do this. Why? There's no need to." It's not going to be financial. It's just that craving for a challenge.'

Regardless, Viddal is happy with where he is at.

'What I like is that if I'd done this interview four or five years ago, everyone would have asked me, "Do you want to fight Tommy Fury or Jake Paul?" he says. 'Now people ask me, "Would I fight Usyk?"

'Clearly, I'm doing something right.'

Sports.title: What REALLY triggered HSTikkyTokky's boxing night riot between Tommy Robinson and Mo Deen, as Muslim influencer breaks cover to claim 'set up'
Sports.content:
The Muslim influencer at the heart of HSTikkyTokky's shut-down influencer boxing night claims he was 'told to' attack Tommy Robinson in a 'scripted' moment that sparked a riot which saw a man stabbed and two arrests made.

The 'Unhinged' event, held in Kilkenny, Ireland, and streamed to millions online was held 'without any authorisation from anybody', sources say, and promised to be a 'proper scrap between the most chaotic names in the internet scene' – with Muslim influencer Mo Deen and a rival calling himself MrTikTokUK on the undercard.

But the night, with a capacity of up to 2,000 young fans, had to be cancelled three fights before its conclusion when venue owners refused to let it continue.

HSTikkyTokky, the controversial British 'manosphere' influencer whose real name is Harrison Sullivan, is behind the Unhinged event company. He now claims it has been banned 'worldwide' in the wake of the carnage, while simultaneously talking up a fight card for next month – with hopes that far-Right activist Robinson will fight on it.

At the point of cancellation, Mo Deen had jumped from the ring to attack Robinson, metal chairs were being hurled across the crowd by fighting fans, Sullivan had been hit in the head by a glass bottle and racist and sexist comments were being broadcast on commentary online. Later, one man was stabbed and two people were arrested. One teenager has been charged.

Sullivan suggested the event had run 'absolutely brilliantly' because it was trending online. His claims of his company being cancelled appear to have little substance, sources close to boxing authorities say.

Mo Deen now says he has received death threats from Robinson's supporters and, in one video, suggested he feared a 'hit' would be put out on him.

For all those people who claim Tommy Robinson was simply the victim in what became a mini-riot in Dublin, watch this video.



TR might have well been kicked by MoDeen earlier )or attempted flying kick but debatable if there was actual contact), but it was after that incident had… — Nick Lowles (@lowles_nick) November 8, 2026

A mass brawl erupts at HSTikkyTokky's Unhinged 003 boxing event in Kilkenny on Saturday

Far-right activist Tommy Robinson sparked the violent riot with an altercation inside the ring

Muslim influencer Mo Deen has claimed he was 'told to' attack Robinson in a 'scripted' moment

At the Hub in Kilkenny, a 1,900-capacity community venue which hosted The Boomtown Rats at the start of the year and is welcoming Irish singer Gavin James next month, an already violent event broke out into a brawl after an altercation between Robinson and Deen – whose real name is Mohammad Kubba.

Robinson, currently on bail after being found guilty in October of harassing two Daily Mail journalists in a campaign that caused them to fear for their safety, arrived in Kilkenny as a ringside guest, accompanied by a large contingent of his supporters. He is due back in court on December 16 for sentencing, with the hearing potentially to result in a custodial sentence.

The chaotic scenes in Kilkenny were preceded by an equally unruly press conference on Friday evening, where multiple fighters launched themselves at one another in a series of violent clashes involving streamers, rappers, OnlyFans models and convicted sex offender-turned-YouTuber Paul Flaherty.

Flaherty, who was jailed for five years in 2018 after being convicted of sexually assaulting a woman he met on Tinder, had already been embroiled in a chaotic brawl at a Unhinged promotional event in September, with footage of the confrontation quickly going viral online.

Tensions rose on Saturday night when Sullivan and his influencer friend Ed Matthews, who starred alongside HSTikkyTokky in Louis Theroux's documentary Inside The Manosphere, invited Robinson to join them at the commentators' desk before Deen's fight.

Holding a copy of his book, The Grooming Gang Cover-Up, the 43-year-old activist made a series of inflammatory remarks about Islam, claiming that 'Muslims have been raping our country for 100 years' and citing false statistics about Muslim men and sexual offences.

After defeating MrTikTokUK, Deen – whose real name is Mohammad Kubba – climbed out of the ring and launched himself at Robinson with a flying kick, in a moment he has since claimed was staged and designed to raise tensions ahead of a potential future bout between the two.

Deen took to social media to claim his attack was staged as he sought refuge in a utility room

The initial brawl spilled into the crowd but was largely contained by security, who managed to defuse the situation. Deen, 41, subsequently left the venue as the remaining bouts got underway, only to be escorted back inside by event security after it was claimed Sullivan called for him to return and face Robinson in the ring.

Sullivan has denied the claim as well as the claim by Deen that he was following a script.

With tensions through the roof, and many racially diverse spectators left furious at Robinson's previous remarks, the far-Right activist launched his book towards Deen, sparking a physical brawl that violently went out of control.

Robinson was grabbed as punches were thrown, while people from both entourages were caught up in the melee.

Violence quickly spread through the crowd, with chairs and metal barriers hurled across the venue, spectators exchanging blows and others scrambling to escape the commotion as security desperately attempted to intervene.

A string of videos showing people screaming, pushing and throwing punches were published to social media in real time as the chaos continued for approximately 20 minutes. Shouts of 'Oh Tommy Robinson' bellowed out from the riot before the livestream, which was broadcast on platform Kick to approximately 1.8million viewers, eventually cut to black.

Police, who had been alerted to disturbances at the venue before the mass brawl broke out, arrested and detained a man in his 20s after another man was stabbed and rushed to hospital earlier in the evening.

A teenager was also arrested by the Gardai and charged with violent disorder.

‘Gardai attended the scene of a number of incidents on the night of Saturday 7th November, 2026 at approximately 9pm at a premises on the Dublin Road, Kilkenny,’ a police statement read.

’One male, aged in his 30s was assaulted and removed from the scene to St. Luke’s Hospital. A man, aged in his 20s was arrested and is currently detained under Section 4 at a Garda station in the South East.

‘A second male was arrested, an adult in his teens, for violent disorder and has since been charged. He is due to appear in court later today, no court sitting has been set at this time. Investigations ongoing.’

Despite the arrests and widespread violence, Sullivan attempted to restart the remaining bouts without spectators, solely for the event's livestream, before a visibly upset venue representative intervened to stop him.

Robinson brawled with Deen and his entourage after being invited into the ring by Sullivan

Robinson greets the event's organiser HSTikkyTokky, whose real name is Harrison Sullivan

HSTikkyTokky CRASHED OUT after someone in the crowd THREW a GLASS BOTTLE at him while he was interviewing a fighter 😳 pic.twitter.com/Uq8uSghkXC — clipmate (@clipmxte) November 7, 2026

A spokesman for the Hub has since said in a statement to Kilkenny Live: 'Following an incident the decision was made by the management of the venue to step in and stop the promotions company from continuing with their event.

'The Hub has a zero-tolerance policy towards violence, aggression or disorderly behaviour.'

As the violence unfolded, Deen took to social media claiming his initial confrontation with Robinson had been staged for entertainment but spiralled out of control.

As he and his entourage sought refuge in a small utility room, Deen urged that his post-fight fly kick was scripted as he hurriedly told his crew to 'lock the doors'.

'The whole place is surrounded,' a concerned Deen said as wild shouting could be heard in the background.

'There's fights everywhere, we're locked in a room right now. Listen I'll make this clear to every single person in the UK. I'm not trying to cause problems. This is like WWE, they said this is what the situation is. I followed the script.

'I'm getting death threats, people trying to kill me. I don't know about this, I just know this is what we had to do. Why is everyone trying to kill me right now?

'This is a message to all supporters of Tommy, supporters, gangs, whatever you are. I just followed the script they told me to agree with. Tommy's agreed to it, they've agreed to it, I followed it.'

'Look at my hands bro,' he added looking visibly shaken. 'My guys are getting rushed, look at my friend's face bro. This whole thing is crazy.'

Deen went on to plead with Elon Musk, whom he described as one of Robinson's 'friends', and the activist's wider network of supporters not to 'put a hit out' on him.

'A fight is a fight, hopefully anyone who is with Tommy and is friends and that, Elon Musk or whatever, don't put hits out on me,' he added, holding his hand to his heart.

Sullivan, who initially stated that the event went 'absolutely brilliantly' because it was trending globally, has refuted Deen's claims that the fight and aftermath was staged.

In a video on his YouTube channel, Sullivan said: 'I was sat next to Tommy. Do you think that I wanted to get f***ing fly-kicked and f***ing some fat belly over me? My watch nearly got popped off. Do you think that that was a plan? No. The plan was for them to face off in the ring.'

The 25-year-old manosphere influencer also dismissed claims that he intentionally attempted to stage an impromptu bare-knuckle fight between Robinson and Deen when the Muslim fighter was escorted back into the venue.

According to The Guardian, Sullivan repeatedly shouted 'let Tommy fight him' while Robinson's entourage – referred to by the YouTuber as 'Tommy's boys' – were permitted to enter the ring to face off with Deen and Co.

He added: 'What is that nonsense? You think I would want them to have a bare-knuckle fight for free, not to just face off and hype up the next event?'

🚨MUST SEE: Hstikkytokky has OFFICIALLY SOLD AWAY his UNHINGED PROMOTIONS COMPANY…



He goes on to apologise to all fans and every supporter 😳



HS: “I’ve had message from police and the boxing commission, I am no longer able to host @UnhingedEvents pic.twitter.com/6EopqIhyMr — KickClipz (@Kickclipzfeed) November 8, 2026

Chairs were hurled and punches were thrown as the event descended into absolute chaos

HSTikkyTokky appeared on Louis Theroux's Inside the Manosphere documentary this year

Sources have told Daily Mail Sport influencer events such as Saturday's Unhinged 003 tend to take place without authorisation from any official boxing body.

HSTikkyTokky had promoted the event as a 'proper scrap between two of the most chaotic names in the internet scene', with British rappers Russ Millions and Kirky set to headline a card that was ultimately abandoned before their bout could take place.

After initially hinting that a potential bout between Robinson and Deen had been in the works for next month, Sullivan appeared crestfallen on a later video as he called an end to Unhinged Promotions, claiming they had been shut down from operating 'worldwide'.

'I've had a lot of messages from police around the world, message from the boxing commission... I am not allowed to put an Unhinged event on anymore after Tommy Robinson riots at Kilkenny last night,' he said on his channel.

'Obviously it's massively disappointing, I wanted to grow the company Unhinged Promotions, I wanted to make it massive and huge and take over the world but the risks that have come in play from the decisions some of my staff have made has now led to us having to cancel any future event. We won't be back, but I will sure be supporting some of the other promotions around the world.

'I just want to apologise to the internet. I didn't want to ever have to put on events that risked the safety of people that came to support. I'm super sorry and I won't be doing an event again. I wish I could, but I'm not allowed to now.'

In case the message wasn't already clear, he stated again: 'There is no venue around the world that will take me, there is literally nothing I can do. I feel cornered, I feel lost, I feel gutted. I feel jobless, this was my passion, my desire, my life.

'Now it's been taken away from me over something that was meant to be a light-hearted promotion for the next event. I'm gutted and I want to say again, sorry to everyone.'

Sullivan's self-pitying demeanour offered a stark contrast to the buoyant figure he immediately cut after the chaotic event, which he claimed went 'absolutely brilliantly'. Footage from earlier in the night had shown him being hit by a glass bottle thrown from the crowd while he stood in the ring.

Thrilled that Unhinged's third event had trended globally on social media platforms as a result of the riots, he said: 'I think it went absolutely brilliantly. Listen it was controversial as f*** but please tell me other promotion on their third event is trending globally on Twitter like this, has generated over 200 million views across TikTok, Twitter and Instagram.

'So everyone who's hating, you're clearly still watching. The fights were absolutely brilliant up until the venue got closed down.

'I'm gutted that we didn't get to see the final three fights but s*** happens. I totally hold accountability for misjudging the amount of security that was needed and the types of people that were coming. I misjudged that.

'But what I won't listen to is that wasn't a f***ing great night of entertainment. It was huge. Every single person is watching what I do. Every single person likes to talk about what I do because I'm the number one at what I do.'

Robinson was holding a copy of his book, The Grooming Gang Cover-Up, as he entered the ring

Robinson, who is on bail before his sentencing in December, said 'Muslims have been raping our country for 100 years' as he riled up the crowd with inflammatory remarks about Islam

Irish mobster Paul Flaherty just KNOCKED OUT a boxer at HSTikkyTokky’s Unhinged boxing press conference 😳 pic.twitter.com/NHVJFG10Ij — vxdeo (@vxdeo) September 17, 2026

Sullivan has seen other boxing events shut down in the past. In January, he complained that 'hundreds' of complainants had called the local council and police to cancel a show in Basildon, saying that one of his fighters was a 'convicted child predator'.

The mayor of Kilkenny called the scenes this weekend 'absolutely disgraceful'. Andrew McGuinness said on local radio station KCLR: 'I am absolutely disgusted Kilkenny was used as a backdrop for such a horrendously managed event.

'They are grooming young people to behave in a way that's absolutely disgraceful. They have no respect for themselves, no respect for other people and particularly no respect for women.

'They groom thousands of people into going to these events. The fact there were minors and teenagers at the event is just absolutely appalling.'

Sports.title: F1 set for V8 return from 2030
Sports.content:
Formula 1 has moved closer to a return to V8 engines from the 2030 season as the FIA announced that a unanimous agreement has been reached between the governing body, F1 management and the power unit manufacturers.

F1 has long worked towards cheaper and simpler engines for the next regulation cycle, which starts in 2031, having recognised the current formula is too complex and physically heavy, and a relic of a different direction in the road car industry.

The FIA could have set the series’ future power-unit regulations for 2031, when the current cycle ends, but there has been broad alignment within the sport to bring that timeline forward by one year, driven by both president Mohammed Ben Sulayem and F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali.

So following recent gatherings by the F1 Commission and power unit advisory committee, where key aspects like the formula, timelines and costs were discussed, there had been broad support to bring forward the next generation of engine regulations by one year and curtail the current formula. The consensus is for F1 to move to a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 engine with a smaller electric component of 200kW, half of which will be ringfenced for overtake-mode use.

The 2.1-litre capacity is derived from the current 1.6-litre V6 formula as a starting point, with two additional cylinders intended to reduce development costs.

After an aborted announcement on Tuesday, the FIA has now officially confirmed there is unanimous support among its stakeholders about bringing that move forward to 2030.

"The FIA presented F1 Power Unit regulations for introduction from 2030 with a 2.1 litre turbocharged V8 as the power unit of choice carrying over some geometrical specifics," the governing body said on Friday.

"The overriding objective is to deliver a power unit which is a lot less complex, lighter and cheaper than the current power units. It will feature limited hybridisation, relevant and sustainable technology with the aim of enhancing attack-oriented racing and a sound which resonates with fans.

"Additionally, the plan is to marry the V8 power unit to a chassis which will also be lighter, more agile and placing greater emphasis on driver skill and close racing. "

F1 and FIA Photo by: Benjamin Vinel

Ben Sulayem added: "This agreement marks a significant milestone in shaping the future of Formula 1.

“From the outset I have been clear in my ambition to deliver a sport that is more competitive and more exciting for our fans, while remaining at the forefront of innovation and sustainability.

"The return of V8 engines represents an opportunity to reconnect with the DNA of this championship, bringing back the sound, emotion and pure racing that is loved worldwide.

“Our vision is clear, lighter, simpler and more affordable cars that put driver skill at the heart of the competition."

The 2030 power unit rules still need to be formally voted through by the World Motor Sport Council and by the power unit manufacturers, with a number of finer details, including the exact level of the power-unit cost cap, still to be agreed.

Sports.title: Pirelli reintroduces stint limit for F1 Qatar GP
Sports.content:
Formula 1 teams will again have to follow a prescribed stint limit for each car at the Qatar Grand Prix to protect the Pirelli tyres around the high-degradation track.

Drivers must complete no more than 27 laps per stint at Lusail International Circuit, meaning teams will likely opt for a two-stop strategy in the 57-lap race.

It is a similar situation to last year when stints were limited to 25 laps following analysis of the 2024 contest, where “several tyres, particularly the left front, had reached the maximum wear”. The 2023 event was also the subject of stint limits, though that year, the enforced limit was just 18 laps.

That came after teams attempted stints of over 30 laps, which is especially challenging at the 16-turn, 5.4km circuit that features various types of corners - particularly medium-to-high-speed.

Pirelli’s chief F1 engineer Simone Berra said at this weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix: “The same limitation in terms of rules, but the number of laps will be 27, not 25.

“We increased by two laps. We have seen from our indoor testing that this is, let's say, acceptable without any particular risk.

Pirelli tyres Photo by: Alessio Morgese

“But we know the issue in Qatar is that we have very high localised wear, especially on the front, with 100% wear easily reached after 25, 26 laps on average.

“This is generating higher stress on the tyre because you don't have the thread compound protecting the structure and then you have high loads, high lateral loads there, and high temperature, high carcass temperature.

“So, these are the factors that are influencing more the integrity resistance of the tyre.”

Every lap a driver completes during the race, including those behind a safety car, will count towards the total and a disqualification is the likely punishment for anybody who fails to oblige.

It doesn’t mean strategic options are limited though, as 2025 saw McLaren opt against pitting under a lap seven safety car to maintain flexibility and not have to stop again before lap 32.

Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris stayed out until the end of the stint limit, but this still backfired as it meant both drivers lost the victory to title rival Max Verstappen at Red Bull.

Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Steven Tee / LAT Images via Getty Images

The grand prix ended as a predominantly two-stop contest nevertheless and it followed the 19-lap sprint race on the Saturday, which will not feature in this year’s event.

Berra added: “We are going to keep the same laps limitation just to induce the two stops and avoid any risk of running on the under-thread for multiple laps and generating integrity issues.

“We know that if you reach 100% wear on the front, then you don't really induce a big degradation.

“The teams, they can easily manage the front axle in the long runs, they don't stop if they don't see quite a significant drop in performance.

“So, that's the situation, and we will count the number of laps for each session. It will be a little bit easier because it's no more a sprint event this year, while it was last year.

“So, even the lap count will be easier for us and we will review the lap count and release the remaining laps per set at the end of Saturday running.”

Qatar will serve as the penultimate grand prix of the 23-round 2026 campaign with Abu Dhabi hosting the finale on 4-6 December.

Sports.title: "Same as Brazil" – Red Bull "trying to understand" the root cause of Verstappen's complaints
Sports.content:
After Thursday's practice sessions in Las Vegas, Red Bull – like all Formula 1 teams – has been left with very few answers. Isack Hadjar eventually finished fourth on the timesheets, but that means very little given that no more rain is forecast for the remainder of the weekend.

The conditions were therefore not representative during the practice day, and that was precisely why Max Verstappen stayed in the garage for so long. It was only in the final five minutes, following the late red flag, that the Dutchman set his first timed lap. There was simply very little to learn.

Read Also: Formula 1 What we learned from Thursday practice at the 2026 Las Vegas GP

Nevertheless, Verstappen was not happy with the RB22 during his brief appearance on track.

It started with a suspected power unit issue, with Verstappen reporting a lack of power on his out-lap. Red Bull responded by explaining that it was mainly related to the low temperatures and would improve on its own, although Verstappen replied: "This is not normal!"

After the session, technical director Pierre Wache explained the background to these complaints, which were also heard from Verstappen's team-mate Hadjar.

"I think it's mainly energy management and the MGU-K deployment around the lap. There was a little bit of fine-tuning on that aspect to make sure that it's optimised for the lap," Wache said.

"When the grip is so low in these conditions, the adaptation of the energy management takes some time on our side."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

However, that was not Verstappen's only complaint. The four-time world champion also said over the team radio: "This car is not good guys, same problem as Brazil."

Wache stressed that this was not related to the DM01 power unit, nor to engine braking – another aspect that has frequently troubled Verstappen this year – but purely to the car's balance.

"No, that's not about the power unit. It’s about the car balance, he was not happy with how the car behaved. We are trying to understand where it's coming from."

In Sao Paulo, Verstappen said that the balance had changed completely after the first stint on intermediates. According to him, this could not be fully explained by the switch to slick tyres, as the car also felt very different during the final laps on inters compared to the opening phase.

During practice in Las Vegas, Verstappen experienced the same balance problems at the rear of the car, something Red Bull will look into ahead of qualifying.

Nevertheless, Hadjar said he has "a good feeling" about this street circuit, although Wache is not yet prepared to fully share that optimism.

"I'm never optimistic. We have a lot of work to do, but it's unknown where we are," he said. "I think everybody is bringing some kind of update. Some teams are even bringing some engine updates.

Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Manuel Eletto

"We will see where we are. It's difficult to say. At the moment, Max is not very happy with the car, and Isack is. We have to work on it and see how we can extrapolate it to tomorrow’s conditions."

While Wache mentioned upgrades, Red Bull has also brought a minor update to the Nevada desert. It involves a small modification to the front wing endplate, which Hadjar has said is worth "less than a tenth".

However, due to the tricky conditions, Red Bull has not yet been able to test the new part and will have to wait until the third practice session to do so.

Sports.title: F1 Las Vegas GP: Russell fastest in damp FP2 from Gasly
Sports.content:
George Russell pipped Pierre Gasly to go fastest in second practice for the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix thanks to a late time in slippery conditions.

The Mercedes driver set a 1m47.272s at the chequered flag which put him 0.071s ahead of Gasly, who benefitted from track evolution to take a shock second for Alpine.

This was the first relatively meaningful session of the weekend after a rain-disrupted FP1 caused zero lap times to be set in the cold conditions - as low as 11C in FP2.

So it still caused complications, especially with the damp track, as drivers went out early on wets but Oscar Piastri quickly called for intermediates - despite McLaren’s insistence for the blue-striped rubber, which was initially correct.

Piastri set a 2m02.786s with his first lap, 3.256s slower than team-mate Lando Norris (1m59.530s) who set the pace in the opening few minutes as Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc split the pair after a 2m02.482s.

But these lap times were only temporary with track evolution being significant in Vegas, as Leclerc and Piastri greeted the top in the following minutes while battling the slippery conditions.

Pierre Gasly, Alpine Photo by: Manuel Eletto

It saw Max Verstappen go deep at Turn 7, likewise for Nico Hulkenberg at Turn 12, nearly colliding with Leclerc at the corner exit, while Norris also ventured off at Turn 14 during the opening 20 minutes.

By the end of that Leclerc was top with a 1m54.895s, 0.538s quicker than team-mate Lewis Hamilton, while Piastri (+0.574s), Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar (+0.881s) and Norris (+0.947s) completed the top five.

Then came the time for intermediates, however, as Norris went fastest with a 1m54.615s on his first run using that rubber, going two seconds quicker on his next lap by setting a 1m52.432s.

The 2025 champion had lowered that to a 1m50.930s by the halfway point, soon beaten by Leclerc and Hamilton who respectively achieved a 1m49.166s and 1m49.262s.

Those were set while heading into the final 20 minutes, just as Leclerc pitched for slick rubber, though Ferrari shot this down with the second half of a lap still proving too damp and slippery.

Both Rafael Camara and Gabriel Bortoleto, for example, went off at Turn 12, but track evolution was still prevalent as Leclerc improved to a 1m47.605s, 0.802s quicker than second-placed Hadjar.

A brief red flag threatened to end proceedings with 10 minutes left, due to a piece of plastic on track which Lance Stroll ran over, before the pitlane reopened for the final five minutes.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team Photo by: Manuel Eletto

There was still debate over whether to stick to the inters, a question Mercedes indirectly posed to Russell who jokingly responded, “if you’re asking about slicks, no way Jose!”

So all drivers stuck to the intermediate tyres, while it was Red Bull’s misery initially dominated discussion, as Verstappen reported power problems to struggle to a 1m50.141s for his only lap time of FP2.

Hadjar, meanwhile, had gone purple in the first two sectors until frustratingly being held up by Oliver Bearman during the final four corners, complaining “what he just did is crazy”.

But some drivers still managed to improve as Russell darted to the top with his 1m47.272s, while Gasly rose to second by setting a 1m47.343s at the chequered flag.

It meant Leclerc dropped to third on his 1m47.605s, ahead of fourth-placed Hadjar, while Piastri completed the top five and was 1.181s off Russell whose ex-team-mate Hamilton took sixth.

Norris (+1.565s), 2026 champion Kimi Antonelli (+1.771s), Franco Colapinto (+1.957s) and Fernando Alonso (+1.959s) round out the top 10, with Verstappen down in 13th.

Sports.title: Cadillac ditches plan to produce own V6 hybrid engine ahead of F1’s V8 push
Sports.content:
Cadillac is set to delay the introduction of its in-house Formula 1 power unit by a year to 2030.

The American squad's initial plan was to compete in the championship with its own General Motors power unit for the first time in 2029. However, that was based on the idea that the current regulations cycle would run its full course and that the next generation of power units would not be introduced until 2031.

That situation has since changed. Ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, the teams and manufacturers reached an agreement in principle on bringing forward the return of V8 engines, as the McLaren CEO Zak Brown also publicly confirmed during the team principals' press conference on Thursday.

The signatures have not yet been put on paper, as Alpine team principal Flavio Briatore added, but an agreement has been reached on a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 with a reduced proportion of electrical power from 2030.

This development has implications for General Motors' plans. If the American manufacturer were to press ahead with its intention to turn Cadillac into a works team as early as 2029, GM would have to develop a power unit to the current specifications for just a single season. That would be a costly undertaking.

Asked by Autosport whether it would therefore make more sense to continue as a customer team for an extra season, CEO Dan Towriss confirmed in Las Vegas: "Yes, we would remain a customer of Ferrari through 2029 and bring the Cadillac power unit online in 2030 with the V8."

Dan Towriss, Cadillac Racing Photo by: James Sutton / LAT Images via Getty Images

Towriss sees the arrival of the V8 as a positive development for F1, and one that Cadillac supports.

"Yeah, I mean, I think we're glad to see the series coming together under the leadership of the FIA to set that direction for a V8 in 2030. We're super happy with that," Towriss said.

He added that Cadillac and General Motors are approaching another milestone. In less than a month's time, their dedicated power unit facility in Charlotte, North Carolina, will open.

"Yes, our new power unit facility opens up on December 18," he said. "So as a new manufacturer coming into the sport, having this direction is obviously very helpful. We're excited about the direction and the crew's hard at work getting ready."

Besides being expected to appeal more to fans, the V8 is also intended to be simpler and cheaper, which is likewise good news for a newcomer.

When the facility begins operations, Cadillac will initially still be working on both V6 and V8 designs, although the current generation of power units will no longer need to be fully developed for 2029.

"Well, for a period of time, we're working on both. So they've already got a V6 base to build off of and then we’re working towards the V8," Towriss explained.

Sergio Perez, Cadillac Racing Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

"There are a number of designs that are in motion now, so there's a lot of good foundation for what we're trying to build and the direction we're headed in."

This should lead to the introduction of Cadillac's first in-house power unit in 2030, officially making the American newcomer a works team. That long-term ambition was also important in securing approval for its F1 entry, as the other teams saw it as the main source of added value for F1 as a whole.

Sports.title: F1 Las Vegas GP: Rain drowns out FP1
Sports.content:
"If we're on a track like Vegas and it rains, honestly, I think we're in trouble," Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson predicted after sampling this year's rain tyres in Brazil.

His comments reflected the general mood in the paddock as the Pirelli tyres are difficult to bring up to temperature, especially at a circuit with low corner speeds and glacial temperatures like the 6km street circuit in the gambling haven.

Lawson's comments proved relevant as the heavens opened up intermittently in Nevada on Thursday morning, and more rain arrived right before the start of FP1 at 4:30 pm local time.

With little rain expected for the remainder of the weekend, it naturally led to an action-starved session, leaving fans forking out the event's eye-watering ticket prices to look for action at the blackjack tables instead.

Venturing out on the low-grip surface, with the walls looming large, felt like a gamble, too. But as if intent to at least offer the home fans something, Sergio Perez of US-owned team Cadillac was first to brave the conditions on full wet tyres for an exploratory lap. He was later joined by Haas duo Rafael Camara and Ryo Hirakawa, the latter completing a rookie FP1 session instead of Oliver Bearman.

The second Cadillac of Valtteri Bottas also explored the inclement conditions, celebrating his 2027 confirmation with a huge tank slapper on his one lap, showing the two US-owned teams certainly couldn't be accused of not chipping in.

Sergio Perez, Cadillac Racing Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

While TV audiences and punters intent on analysing lap times and long runs were also left wanting, FP1 actually became one of the most picturesque sessions of the year. The Las Vegas Boulevard is photogenic at the best of times, but the rain further drowned the Strip in neon-tinted reflections, hues Hunter S. Thompson would have approved of.

"Amazing, it's a lovely Strip," gawked Ferrari reserve driver Dino Beganovic as he replaced Lewis Hamilton for the session.

"Enjoy the sightseeing... but we'll box this lap, please," came the perfunctory reply from Ferrari.

Beganovic may as well have enjoyed it, as staying tucking inside the garage was not an option to begin with for the Swedish-Bosnian driver. For any of the teams' four mandatory rookie FP1 sessions to count, drivers must at least leave the garage once.

It explains why all three rookie runners went out, including Jak Crawford who deputised for Fernando Alonso at Aston Martin, though they will be ruing the lack of actual mileage the rare opportunity was able to provide.

As world champion Kimi Antonelli reported aquaplaning, several more tenured drivers had close shaves with the walls. Alex Albon went straight at Turn 11 at the end of the Strip , while Audi's Nico Hulkenberg also locked up at the drenched left-hander.

"It's almost like an ice rink," reported Red Bull's Max Verstappen, The Dutchman a rather cool admirer of street circuits at the best of times.

Eventually, all but five drivers sampled the conditions, with the four cars from McLaren and Racing Bulls thinking better of it, and Aston's Lance Stroll also not feeling particularly motivated.

Camara and Alpine duo Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto were the only three drivers to venture out twice, with the Argentine nearly reliving the scenes of his high-speed qualifying shunt in 2024 for Williams as he momentarily lost control over his car on the straight.

For the avoidance of doubt, no laptimes were recorded.

Sports.title: Nike joins F1 as apparel partner
Sports.content:
Athletic apparel giant Nike has joined F1 as its official partner and uniform supplier, taking over from Puma at the start of 2027.

As was long rumoured, Nike will start supplying F1 personnel with apparel and footwear from the start of next season, a partnership that also extends to F1 Academy, which had both been using Puma kit until this year.

The athletic company will also come up with F1-inspired retail collections, the first of which will go on sale on Friday and be centred around the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

"Nike will bring new energy to the pinnacle of motorsport through capsule collections with a focus on style, performance, and lifestyle including footwear, apparel, and accessories, as well as performance innovations, and race-weekend experiences for the next generation of athletes and fans," the announcement promised.

"Fans will get a first look on 20 November, when the limited Las Vegas Grand Prix x Nike capsule collection drops at the F1 Hub and Nike Las Vegas stores.

Nike CEO Elliott Hill said: "Formula 1 is driven by competition, speed and a constant push to innovate. That’s an athlete mindset, and it’s one we share at Nike. Together, we have an incredible opportunity to bring new energy to the sport, serve its athletes and inspire fans around the world.”

Sports.title: FIA to phase in full-time F1 stewards from 2027
Sports.content:
The consistency of stewards’ decisions has been a topic of discussion in the Formula 1 paddock for years. While the complexity of the sporting regulations and racing guidelines is one factor, another question keeps coming up: would a permanent panel of stewards improve consistency?

From 2027, the FIA will take a step in that direction. The governing body announced on Thursday that it will gradually move towards full-time stewards, with the first phase beginning in 2027.

The intention is to recruit a panel of 12 to 15 full-time stewards, although that number will only be reached over time. The first full-time stewards will be recruited during the 2027 season, who will be joined at each race by the usual part-time stewards and a driver’s steward, whose specialist knowledge and perspective as a former racing driver will remain part of the process.

The main objective is to improve the consistency of decisions, although according to the FIA, the initiative goes beyond that. By making the role full-time, these stewards can also be deployed outside race weekends, for example “to identify emerging trends and areas requiring regulatory clarification” and to train FIA officials.

That would allow for shortcomings in the sporting regulations and racing guidelines used by stewards to be addressed more effectively. The aim is therefore not only to improve consistency during races, but also to make the rules and guidelines themselves more robust in the first place.

Start action Photo by: Clive Rose / Getty Images

This move is in line with what FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has been advocating for some time: further professionalisation of the stewarding panel. The FIA believes moving beyond the current voluntary, rotating system will help improve continuity and consistency.

And that is precisely one of the key areas the FIA wants to improve, while emphasising that the move also complements the FIA Remote Operations Centre, which recently opened at Biggin Hill.

“This latest major investment in FIA officiating reflects our dedication to delivering the highest standards of decision-making, fairness and integrity in motorsport. The recruitment of full-time stewards is a significant step in our longstanding mission of building a dedicated officiating ecosystem in the FIA Formula One World Championship, it is also an investment in the future of our sport,” Ben Sulayem said.

“This development will help to build greater expertise and continuity within our stewarding structure, strengthening our ability to review and improve regulations, support the development of future officials and ensure the highest standards of consistent officiating across all our championships.”

The FIA is now setting up the recruitment process for the phased introduction in 2027, with plans to expand the group in 2028 and subsequent years until it reaches the target of 12 to 15 full-time stewards.

Sports.title: FIA, F1 and teams unanimously agree to drop current power units after 2029 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
As the 2026 Formula 1 season draws to a close, the FIA has confirmed the new power units introduced this season will be dropped in just three years’ time.

Deep dissatisfaction with the V6 hybrid turbo regulations, which have already been modified for coming seasons, has led to a unanimous agreement they should be replaced. The FIA confirmed it, Formula One Management and the teams all back the introduction of a revised V8 hybrid turbo engine formula in 2030.

The FIA says the new power units will be less complex, lighter and cheaper than current designs.

FIA statement on new power unit rules for 2030

The Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), the global governing body for motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations worldwide, has today announced the 2030 Formula 1 Power Unit technical framework has been unanimously agreed between the FIA, Formula One Management (FOM), the teams and Formula 1 Power Unit manufacturers. The FIA presented F1 Power Unit regulations for introduction from 2030 with a 2.1 litre turbocharged V8 as the power unit of choice carrying over some geometrical specifics. The overriding objective is to deliver a power unit which is a lot less complex, lighter and cheaper than the current power units. It will feature limited hybridisation, relevant and sustainable technology with the aim of enhancing attack-oriented racing and a sound which resonates with fans. Additionally, the plan is to marry the V8 power unit to a chassis which will also be lighter, more agile and placing greater emphasis on driver skill and close racing. The next step is to present a definitive 2030 Regulatory Framework to the FIA World Motor Sport Council meeting in Shanghai next month.

This article will be updated.

Sports.title: Piastri needed to reduce his speed through F1’s quickest corners – Brown | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Oscar Piastri’s struggles in 2026 stemmed from him taking too much speed through high-speed corners, according to McLaren CEO Zak Brown.

In order to maximise the energy delivered by Formula 1’s 2026 power units, drivers are often instructed to reduce their speed through the quickest corners. In qualifying, drivers have found that if they increase their speed through a corner the power unit may deliver less energy on the following straight.

Brown says grappling with this unusual feature of F1’s rules has proved a challenge for Piastri as well as other drivers this year.

“I think we’ve seen the driver rosters get mixed up a bit this year,” he said. “Some have adapted quicker than others. These cars definitely take a different technique to drive.

“I remember in the first race in Australia talking about [drivers needing to] slow down to speed up. Historically it’s always been about putting your foot down as quickly as possible, keeping it down as long as possible, braking as late as possible. These cars require a different driving technique.”

Piastri has always been strong in very quick corners, said Brown, and McLaren had to tell him to slow down in them this year.

“When you look at Oscar, he’s quite brave through the high-speed corners, which is a real strength of his,” said Brown. “Now you’ll hear us on the radio sometimes compromising some of those corners.”

Piastri led the championship for the majority of last season and was still in contention to win the world championship at the final round. This year he has scored 152 points to his team mate Lando Norris’s 246.

“He’s been very, very close to Lando when you look at the lap times themselves,” said Brown. “I think he’s gotten on top of it.

“We got a lot of support for Oscar. He was one podium away from being a world champion last year. In all these sports, you get into momentum. He’s in a good place, we’re excited and want to finish the season strong and get ready for ’27.”

Sports.title: Spotlight: Donnelly to publish autobiography with contributions from Hamilton and Pitt | Brief
Sports.content:
Martin Donnelly, whose near-fatal crash inspired the plot of “F1: The Movie”, will publish his autobiography next year.

Seven-times Formula 1 world champion Lewis Hamilton is providing the book’s introduction. Brad Pitt, who played the Sonny Hayes character Donnelly inspired, will write a foreword.

Transworld will publish “Unbroken: A Memoir of Speed and Survival” in July.

“I am genuinely excited and looking forward to seeing my autobiography published in 2027,” said Donnelly. “I was fortunate enough to reach the pinnacle of motorsport and race in Formula 1 alongside giants of the sport including Alain Prost, Nigel Mansell and Ayrton Senna.

“However, following the catastrophic accident which ended my Formula 1 career in Spain in 1990, I spent 35 years believing my story to have been consigned to history.

“All that changed due to the inclusion of my accident as part of the back-story to the Sonny Hayes character in last year’s F1 Movie, thanks in no small part to the incredible work of Lewis Hamilton and Brad Pitt.

“In reliving those times, I realised there was great interest in what had happened, and in how I not only survived the crash but went on to lead a full life including driving Formula 1 cars again.”

Sports.title: “He’s decided on a direction”: Cadillac offered reserve role to “disappointed” Herta | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Cadillac has offered Colton Herta a reserve driver role for next season after choosing not to promote him to a race seat for 2027.

The IndyCar race-winner competed in Formula 2 this year to prepare himself for a potential Formula 1 debut in 2027. He has endured a tough campaign and lies 19th in the standings after 25 out of 29 races.

Herta secured enough FIA superlicence points to race in F1 through his appearances for Cadillac in practice sessions. Despite this, Cadillac CEO Dan Towriss said the team felt it would be best to retain its current line-up.

“We were working hard to get Colton Herta ready as well,” he said. “It’s important to have an American driver with our team racing.

“But ultimately, when we took a look at it, Valtteri is the right guy. We want to keep Checo and Valtteri together. Their experience, the continuity, what they bring to the team, ultimately it was the right decision for the team and we were happy to extend Valtteri. He’s been absolutely fantastic for us.”

Herta has “a number of options on the table” for 2027. “We’ve offered him a reserve position. The seat’s open for ’28, so there are options on the table for Colton.

“There are options in other sports as well. I think he’s decided on a direction, but we’re still in conversations on that and look forward to seeing what Colton wants to do.”

Towriss said it had been “a tough decision [and] tough discussion with Colton” about his future. “I think he was disappointed.

“There was a lot of work, a lot of build-up going to this. I think Colton was very brave in even taking on this risk, going into F2 and trying to cram all this learning in.

“I think it was obvious it was a very tough season for Colton in F2 this year, but I think the work that he did in FP1s and the testing [of previous cars] were quite strong and showed that he really is capable of driving this car.

“But when we look at where the team is right now and what’s needed for the team, Valtteri was the best decision going forward. But again, we’re going to continue to talk to Colton about the options that are on the table and give it a little bit of time, because I think he is disappointed to not have that opportunity.
