Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Sets Monday for Opponent Reveal
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia says he’ll reveal his next opponent on Monday, and Teofimo Lopez is the name fans are waiting to hear. Oscar De La Hoya has floated February 6 for a welterweight unification, but the WBA still expects Lopez to defend against Jack Catterall. Garcia’s post gave fans a day to circle and left the biggest question open.

“Whoever we announce on Monday, I’m knocking him out by the fourth round. At max 8 rounds. “BET THAT,” Garcia wrote on X.

De La Hoya said the WBA had already granted Lopez an exemption to face Garcia. WBA president Gilberto Mendoza said Friday that no special permit had been granted. Lopez’s manager, Keith Connolly, took Mendoza’s statement as a response to De La Hoya’s claim and said it didn’t settle whether the WBA might still grant permission. De La Hoya has mentioned Las Vegas and New York as possible locations for the February fight.

Lopez could still fight Garcia if he gives up the WBA belt. The two names would sell the fight either way, but Lopez won that title from Rolando Romero in August. Giving it up before making a defense would take some of the shine off his move to welterweight and cost both fighters the chance to leave with two belts.

Garcia has reason to bring up an early knockout after stopping Conor Benn in two rounds in September. Lopez has never been stopped as a professional, though. Shakur Stevenson outboxed him over 12 rounds at 140, and Lopez came back to beat Romero on points at 147. Garcia’s left hook would give Teofimo a different problem, but getting him out in four rounds is a big promise.

If Garcia names Lopez on Monday, fans will want to know whether they’re getting a unification or a defense of Garcia’s WBC title. If he names somebody else, the next question is whether Teofimo finally fights Catterall.

You don’t throw out a hard day like Monday unless the fight deal itself is basically done, and both Oscar De La Hoya and Mike Coppinger have been signaling that Garcia and Lopez are closing in on February 6 in either Las Vegas or New York. Plus, Ryan only has one fight left on his Golden Boy contract, while Dana White is circling to sign him to Zuffa Boxing, so everybody in his camp is motivated to get this announced and locked in.

So Monday probably brings a real opponent reveal, almost certainly Teofimo, even if they have to announce it without knowing whether the WBA strap will actually be on the line. Unless, of course, Ryan pulls one of his classic social media swerves and names a completely different tune-up while Lopez gets stuck dealing with Catterall.

Sports.title: Willy Hutchinson Fails Both of Canelo’s Tests
Sports.content:
Willy Hutchinson may be too tough a fight for Canelo Álvarez and too small a pay-per-view draw to justify taking it. If Canelo wants an opponent who sells and a win he can bank on, the WBC light heavyweight champion gives him no certainty on either count.

The WBC is willing to approve the fight if Canelo moves up from 168 pounds, where he took the belt from Christian Mbilli. “If he decides to challenge at light heavyweight, it would certainly be approved, champion against champion,” said WBC president Mauricio Sulaiman to Sky Sports. That gives Canelo a chance to win another belt at 175 after beating Sergey Kovalev there in 2019. It also puts him back at the weight where Dmitry Bivol beat him.

There’s a real chance Hutchinson beats Canelo more clearly than Bivol or Terence Crawford did. In the fourth round of his rematch with Joshua Buatsi, Hutchinson jabbed to the body and head from his orthodox stance, switched southpaw and knocked Buatsi off balance with a right hook. In the sixth, he made Buatsi miss by moving at angles. He was changing both the punches Buatsi had to watch for and where Buatsi needed to put his feet to answer.

That’s a problem for Canelo, who can spend large parts of a round waiting to get his feet set for a hard counter. A fighter who scores with a jab and moves before Canelo answers can win a quiet round with very little clean work. Repeat that for six or seven rounds, and Canelo could find himself needing to chase the fight against a natural light heavyweight.

Buatsi did have success when he put punches together. He scored to the body in the fifth and came on late as Hutchinson slowed. Two judges had it 115–113, and the third scored it 117–112, all for Hutchinson. Canelo has the body punching to take advantage of those openings. The question is whether he can throw often enough to make Hutchinson slow down before he’s already behind on the cards.

The sales case is just as uncertain. Hamzah Sheeraz could sell more pay-per-views even with fans who think he’s been overhyped. Some of those fans would tune in to see whether Canelo exposes him. Sheeraz also gives the promotion a 168-pound opponent Canelo can face without changing divisions. Hutchinson’s win over Buatsi made him a world champion, but it’s hard to see how that result alone makes him a bigger draw.

Canelo has already won a belt at 175. Going back up to beat a younger champion would be an achievement, especially after the Bivol loss. His team would still have to decide whether that’s worth a fight that could sell less than Sheeraz and leave Canelo chasing rounds harder than he did against Crawford or Bivol.

Sports.title: Keith Thurman Belongs in Boxing’s Untouchable Class for Top Card Slots
Sports.content:
Keith Thurman now sits in an untouchable class for any promoter putting together a main event or a pay-per-view co-feature. Nobody in the business can schedule him for a major card and feel confident the fight will ever reach the opening bell.

With roughly two weeks remaining before the December 5 DAZN pay-per-view event in Glendale, Arizona, Golden Boy Promotions is scrambling to find a replacement opponent for Vergil Ortiz Jr. because Thurman pulled out with another training camp injury. A promotional company cannot risk millions in marketing and broadcast commitments on a 38-year-old fighter whose body routinely breaks down before fight week.

Look at his recent history. Thurman tore his biceps in March 2024 right before he was supposed to fight Tim Tszyu, so Sebastian Fundora took the late replacement call instead and walked out with the WBC junior middleweight title. Two years later, Fundora stopped Thurman in six rounds in March 2026. Only three fights in seven years. Now two separate pay-per-view bookings have fallen apart because his body cannot hold together through camp.

“Thurman should keep fighting as long as he wants to fight,” said Mike Coppinger on Instant Inside the Ring. “He clearly still has the hunger.”

Rick Reeno countered by asking what Thurman had left to accomplish beyond another payday. Reeno nailed it. Hunger means nothing when a fighter cannot survive eight weeks of sparring without ending up on the shelf for up to two months. After getting stopped by Fundora, Thurman has no realistic route back to a world title, especially up at 160 pounds where unbeaten champions like Janibek Alimkhanuly, Carlos Adames, and Erislandy Lara hold the belts and Ortiz was supposed to serve as his first real test.

Golden Boy can still rescue the December 5 co-feature behind cruiserweight unification headliners David Benavidez and Michal Cieslak if Oscar De La Hoya opens the checkbook. Every available opponent knows Golden Boy is desperate on two weeks’ notice and will demand inflated money to take the call.

Meanwhile, Ortiz has to discard months of specialized camp preparation for Thurman’s lateral movement and adjust immediately to a completely different style. That is the real cost of trusting an unreliable co-feature.

Thurman ought to retire. Put him on the early prelims before the main broadcast starts if he refuses to hang up the gloves. Nobody watches the swing bouts anyway, and a sudden injury withdrawal down there costs the promoter nothing.

Sports.title: Keith Thurman Injury Leaves Golden Boy Two Weeks to Find a Real Opponent for Vergil Ortiz Jr.
Sports.content:
Golden Boy took a foolish gamble booking Keith Thurman for Vergil Ortiz Jr.’s comeback. The 37-year-old had fought only three times since 2019 and was coming off a sixth-round stoppage loss to Sebastian Fundora. Now Thurman is injured, and Golden Boy and Premier Boxing Champions have just over two weeks to find an opponent worthy of a pay-per-view co-main event.

Fans had already suspected that Thurman wouldn’t make it through camp without pulling up lame for some ache or pain. With his injury history and years of inactivity, it seemed obvious that he would fall apart during camp. Despite all that, Golden Boy still picked him to fight Vergil, and this is what they get. Promoters wanted an old welterweight name whose faded television reputation might trick casual buyers into paying for a PPV chief support slot that his recent ring record could never justify.

I’d offer Yoenli Hernández a stack of money. The WBC ranks him one spot below Ortiz at middleweight, and he has the power to make Vergil think twice about walking him down. Hernández would have every reason to demand a bigger purse for taking the fight on two weeks’ notice. If I were Golden Boy, I would hate that idea. Why pay Yoenli good clean cash just to watch him annihilate Vergil Jr.?

Mike Coppinger first reported Thurman’s withdrawal for The Ring. BoxingScene reported that the injury happened in training camp and cited a source close to Thurman’s camp who said it could take up to two months to heal. The 12-round fight was supposed to be Ortiz’s middleweight debut on the Dec. 5 David Benavidez vs. Michal Cieslak card in Glendale, Arizona.

“I’m active, and I’m gonna do my best to keep staying active,” said Thurman at the Los Angeles press conference, as quoted by BoxingScene. Two of those three fights since 2019, against Brock Jarvis and Fundora, came in the space of about a year. That counted as activity by Thurman’s standards. It was still a lot to ask of a fighter who’d spent most of the previous seven years out of the ring and had taken a beating in his last fight.

BoxingScene says Arizona’s Jesús Ramos Jr., the WBC interim middleweight titleholder, has expressed interest in fighting Ortiz. Ramos would give the Glendale crowd a local fighter with something at stake at 160. Jermell Charlo’s name has come up, too, but he already has a fight booked against Brock Jarvis in Australia.

Sports.title: Gerald McClellan Needed 171 Seconds to Crush John Mugabi and Win First World Title
Sports.content:
It took Gerald McClellan 171 seconds to capture his first world championship. On November 20, 1991, inside London’s Royal Albert Hall, the 24-year-old Kronk product dropped John “The Beast” Mugabi three times in the opening stanza. Referee Roberto Ramirez Sr. stepped in at 2:51 of round one to award McClellan the vacant WBO middleweight title.

Thirty-five years later, the striking detail is how fast McClellan shut the door on a fellow knockout artist. Both fighters weighed 157 pounds at the scale. Either man possessed the kind of heavy hands that could end a night early, yet Mugabi barely threw anything of consequence before getting hurt. McClellan simply beat him to the punch with a crisp right hand that landed cleanly while the former junior middleweight champion was still trying to find his range.

Mugabi never got a second to breathe. At 31, he was five years removed from dragging Marvin Hagler into an eleven-round war for the undisputed middleweight crown in Las Vegas. He had captured Olympic silver for Uganda in 1980 and later claimed the WBC 154-pound belt when Rene Jacquot tore his ankle in the first round. Terry Norris then obliterated Mugabi in one round in March 1990 to strip that title away. Two tune-up wins brought Mugabi into London at 38 and 3, with every single victory coming by knockout.

None of his 41 professional bouts had ever reached the judges’ scorecards. On paper, that meant trouble for any young contender willing to trade in close quarters. In reality, Mugabi was worn down from years of brutal wars and could no longer absorb a clean shot from a fresh puncher. Once the first knockdown landed, Mugabi had to recover on unsteady legs against a sharper, faster fighter who reloaded his right hand immediately.

McClellan entered the ring at 22 and 2 with 20 knockouts. Prior decision losses to Dennis Milton and Ralph Ward left genuine questions about how the Detroit fighter would handle an experienced veteran if the bout dragged into the middle rounds. Mugabi lacked the durability to test that theory. Three trips to the canvas in under three minutes forced Ramirez to wave the contest off with nine seconds left on the clock.

The Royal Albert Hall promotion was built around Frank Bruno’s comeback against John Emmen. McClellan was competing for a WBO strap that Chris Eubank had recently vacated, back when the organization was still fighting for recognition alongside the established WBC, WBA, and IBF belts. Still, destroying a recognizable name on British soil gave Emanuel Steward’s prized pupil instant credibility across the Atlantic.

McClellan vacated the WBO belt without making a single defense to chase bigger money in the established sanctioning bodies. In May 1993, he survived massive punches from Julian Jackson to score a fifth-round stoppage for the WBC middleweight championship, then wiped out three consecutive challengers inside the opening round. The Jackson fight proved McClellan possessed a chin to match his firepower. The Mugabi demolition proved he rarely needed to use it.

Sports.title: WBA Says Teofimo Has No Permit for Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Teofimo Lopez still needs WBA approval to fight Ryan Garcia in a welterweight unification before facing Jack Catterall. WBA president Gilberto Mendoza said no special permit had been granted after Oscar De La Hoya said the WBA had already ruled in Lopez’s favor. Lopez co-manager Keith Connolly said the process was still ongoing.

“No special permit has been granted to Teófimo Lopez,” Mendoza wrote on X. In a reply to the post, Connolly wrote, “He was just correcting Oscar the process is still ongoing.”

“It has already been worked out. The WBA has already ruled on it,” said De La Hoya, Garcia’s promoter, to Fight Hub TV. He said the WBA was giving Lopez an exemption because the fight would be a unification.

De La Hoya rated the chances of the fight happening as “great” and said February 6 was the target, with Las Vegas and New York in the running to host it.

Lopez holds the WBA Super title at 147 pounds. Garcia holds the WBC belt. A special permit would give Lopez a way to put his belt up against Garcia before satisfying his mandatory obligation to Catterall. Mendoza’s statement addresses whether a permit has been granted, and Connolly’s reply leaves open the possibility that the WBA could grant permission later. The exchange leaves the formal filing status unclear.

The WBA reaffirmed its order for Lopez to face Catterall on November 11 after considering a request from Lopez’s team. In that ruling, the organization said Lopez’s team had yet to submit a formal special-permit request for a unification. It also asked the Lopez and Catterall camps to resume talks and gave them ten days from the ruling to submit an agreement on a date for the mandatory fight.

Catterall earned his place by beating Shakhram Giyasov for the WBA’s other welterweight title. The WBA had already allowed Rolando Romero to make an optional defense before facing the winner of Catterall and Giyasov. Lopez beat Romero by majority decision in August and took on that obligation when he won the Super title. A permit for Garcia would mean Catterall has to wait through another fight for his shot at the Super belt.

There’s an obvious reason for Lopez and Garcia to pursue the unification. They can sell the fight on their names alone, and putting both belts up gives the winner a unified title at 147 pounds. Catterall has a simple argument of his own. He won the fight the WBA told him would put him next in line, and the WBA has already reaffirmed his position once.

That leaves De La Hoya talking up a fight the WBA has yet to clear. If the permit comes through, the next question is what timetable the WBA gives Catterall. In the meantime, the mandatory order remains in place, and Lopez’s camp is still pursuing a route to Garcia with the WBA belt on the line.

Sports.title: Deontay Wilder Looks Relieved After Jai Opetaia Pulls Out of Cardiff Fight
Sports.content:
Deontay Wilder called Jai Opetaia’s withdrawal a “blessing” and wished him well in his bid to become undisputed cruiserweight champion.

The former WBC heavyweight champion (45-4-1, 43 KOs) still has no announced replacement for the December 11 Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua undercard in Cardiff, though his sudden cheerfulness looks a whole lot like relief after dodging a dangerous southpaw who was supposed to test his legs in front of a massive Netflix audience.

“I’m not mad at Jai at all. Actually, it was a blessing for what’s to come after this,” said Wilder on the Heavyweight Truth channel. He was smiling and seeming way too happy for what should have been bad news. Wilder didn’t say what he had in mind or name anyone he expects to fight at Principality Stadium.

A normal fighter would be angry about their well-known opponent pulling out, but not Wilder. His behavior betrays his inner workings. He didn’t want to hit that hill, going up against a fighter who could wreck what’s left of his sagging career. Getting stopped by a cruiserweight would have been it for Wilder. Coming back from that loss, especially if it were a knockout, would be next to impossible at his age.

Derek Chisora has confirmed he was contacted about taking the fight, and he’s also stirring the pot over why Opetaia really pulled out. Chisora told talkSPORT he would accept a rematch if the money was right and said the offer had yet to meet his asking price, while also claiming Opetaia wasn’t actually hurt and simply walked out of the gym after getting worked over by a heavyweight sparring partner.

Wilder beat Chisora by split decision in London in April, dropping him twice in a fight that still went all 12 rounds and showed how hard it is for the 41-year-old Alabama puncher to finish durable heavyweights who keep walking forward.

Richard Riakporhe has also put his name forward. Like Opetaia, he made his name at cruiserweight, though he has already fought at heavyweight and doesn’t carry the same undefeated aura as the 31-0 Australian. Jarrell Miller (28-1-2, 22 KOs) said he received a call about facing Wilder, although he’s already scheduled to fight 2016 Olympic gold medalist Tony Yoka on December 20 in Accra, Ghana, on a Matchroom DAZN show where Miller enters as the WBA’s top-ranked contender.

Opetaia was due to make his heavyweight debut in Cardiff. His co-promoter, Mick Francis, said he injured his hand against Noel Mikaelian in September and aggravated it in training, though plenty of observers suspect Opetaia also realized he had everything to lose before his planned Cinco de Mayo 2027 unification clash with David Benavidez, who first has to get past Michal Cieslak on December 5.

Getting clipped by one Wilder right hand at heavyweight would kill that Benavidez payday on the spot and send Benavidez straight toward Oleksandr Usyk instead. Opetaia apologized to Wilder and his team after withdrawing and reaffirmed his goal of becoming undisputed at cruiserweight.

“We understand, Jai. We understand, bro. That’s all I got to say,” said Wilder. “I wish you nothing but the best moving forward with your career. Undisputed, baby. I’m rooting for you. Let’s go.”

The appeal of Wilder vs. Opetaia was seeing how an unbeaten cruiserweight would handle Wilder’s right hand in his first fight at heavyweight, especially with gym rumors already questioning how he handled heavyweight size in sparring.

A Chisora rematch would offer a different question, especially since fans already paid to watch that exact fight eight months ago without seeing a knockout. Wilder put him down twice in April and still had to settle for a split decision. Chisora has already shown he can get back up and make Wilder work the full distance, which is the last thing Wilder wants if he’s trying to look explosive on the Fury vs. Joshua broadcast.

The organizers have three weeks to fill the chief support slot. Chisora has made his price a condition of taking the fight, Riakporhe has volunteered, and Miller says he has been approached with another bout already on his calendar. Wilder’s response settled how he feels about Opetaia pulling out. Who he’ll fight in Cardiff is still open, and right now every available replacement brings either a recycled April rematch or a short-notice fill-in that won’t replace the buzz Opetaia brought to the card.

Sports.title: David Morrell Takes a Huge Step Backward Against Rodriguez
Sports.content:
David Morrell should beat Julio de Jesus Rodriguez on Saturday in Santo Domingo. The trouble is that even a quick knockout of the 44-year-old veteran will do little to repair the damage from Zak Chelli stopping him in the tenth round in May. For a fighter who was facing David Benavidez less than two years ago, this is a long way back.

Morrell (12-2, 9 KOs) is scheduled for ten rounds at light heavyweight against Rodriguez (27-10, 24 KOs) on Shuan Boxing’s card at the Coliseo Carlos “Teo” Cruz. Rodriguez has knocked out 24 men, but he’s on a long losing streak and has been stopped by James Metcalf and Ismael Villarreal. At 28, Morrell should have the speed to get his punches off first and the power to end it early.

The Benavidez defeat was easier to take. Morrell went the distance in a competitive fight against one of the best men in the division. His split decision over Imam Khataev five months later was a harder result to read. He got the win, but it was close enough that he still had something to prove when he went to Manchester to fight Chelli. Getting stopped there took away the argument that he was only a step behind the very best.

Morrell has been out since May, and there’s value in getting him back in the ring. He can get his timing back, put combinations together, and see how comfortable he feels throwing the left hand. Rodriguez’s recent form makes an early finish the expectation. If Morrell struggles to put him away or has trouble keeping control of the fight, those questions about his form will follow him out of Santo Domingo.

The next opponent will tell us more. Morrell needs someone who can make him work into the later rounds and still bring something back at him. That’s where the Chelli loss leaves the biggest question, and Saturday’s opponent is unlikely to make Morrell answer it.

Ghana News.title: Trump threatens ban on US firms building AI data centres overseas
Ghana News.content:
Donald Trump has said he will ban US companies from building AI data centres overseas, threatening a "tremendous tax" for tech firms who do so.

"We're going to keep it all in this country," the US president said, while providing little detail on the potential policy he said others in his cabinet were hearing about for the first time.

Data centres were a central issue in the midterm elections earlier in November, with many Democratic candidates promising tougher regulation on their construction.

Tech giants including Meta and Google have entered agreements to build data centres overseas. It remains unclear how such a policy would be enforced if it was brought in.

"We're not going to allow our companies to build data centres outside of our country," Trump told reporters in a press briefing following his return from his trip to Asia.

"Because China will take all of them, and we're not allowing that to happen."

But whether that idea will become policy remains unclear.

"I don't know if that's a breaking story, but I haven't even said that to my people. But I'm telling them now, they're here," he said.

Trump floated the policy after saying the US was leading on data centre construction, and he would not allow China to beat the US when it came to AI - which he calls super intelligence, or SI.

It also follows an announcement earlier this week that would restrict the export of advanced computer chips and who can access the computing power provided by them.

Washington on Monday announced firms would require a licence to buy advanced chips, so US officials can monitor whether they are being used to serve Chinese companies or they are being smuggled into China.

The move will impact South East Asian countries that have invested heavily in data centres, as Chinese companies seek to rent computing power from overseas.

Data centres are crucial to the AI boom. The vast warehouse-style buildings house the advanced computer chips and servers that are needed to run AI programmes such as Claude and ChatGPT.

As of April there were about 3,000 data centres across the US, with another 1,500 in various stages of approval and construction, according to the Pew Research Centre.

Many of them are built in rural areas, and concerns about issues including noise pollution and energy consumption helped drive Democratic candidates promising tougher rules on data centre construction to wins on 3 November.

"You ought to take advantage of the data centres. Make them pay you, make them pay your community, but take advantage don't shut them off," Trump said.

"We have a lot of places that want them badly, and they're great places. They have energy and they have everything. They're tremendous assets."

Large tech firms - often called AI hyperscalers due to the size of their investments in AI - have also been branching out, and Canada has made moves to step in to offer itself as an alternative location for these sites, with less local pushback against projects so far.

Meta has already broken ground on a data centre in the province of Alberta, and Anthropic has signed a long-term agreement to lease a proposed data centre in Nova Scotia.

The BBC has reached out to Meta for comment on Trump's remarks.

In September Google announced a €13bn ($15bn: £11bn) investment in AI infrastructure in Finland, which included funding for three data centres.

Last month, building work for two of those centres was halted due to concerns over the clearance of more than 300 hectares of forest.

Trump called out the build in Finland specifically, saying his administration was "not allowing that to happen".

Google has been contacted for comment.

Ghana News.title: White House removes cyber-security chief after series of tech outages
Ghana News.content:
The top cyber-security official in the US government is leaving his post after a little over a year in the job.

White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired after losing the confidence of the White House chief of staff, Stephen Miller, according CBS, the BBC's US news partner. Asked about his removal on Friday, President Donald Trump said it was because he was not "good enough".

His firing comes after a string of tech outages which hit banking, air traffic control and other sectors.

US officials said the outages were not caused by cyberattacks but the blackouts had sparked scrutiny from members of Congress who demanded a clearer explanation of what went wrong.

There has been no official confirmation of the removal of Cairncross but Secretary of State Marco Rubio posted on X to say Department of Defense chief information officer Kirsten Davies was the new national cyber director.

The news, first reported by Axios, follows security concerns, including the ability of advanced AI models - mostly from US companies - to discover vulnerabilities which humans would not be able to find on their own.

Earlier this week, Rubio said there was "zero evidence" the outages were connected, adding "we are not under systemic attack".

But the fact that so many have happened in quick succession has left some people worried about the safety of the tech which is heavily relied on in all aspects of daily life.

Cairncross was previously a lawyer in the Republican Party, before becoming the chief operating officer of the Republican National Committee.

In the first Trump administration, he was part of the team of the White House chief of staff.

He later worked in the private sector, before returning to government in August 2025.

Ghana News.title: Anthropic shares fall after blockbuster opening as wider tech sell-off continues
Ghana News.content:
Anthropic's shares have dropped back towards their initial price after a soaring first day on the stock market, as a wider tech sell-off deepens.

The fall in tech stocks continued to weigh on markets through Friday, with the S&P 500 down about 2.8% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average down more than 1% by mid-afternoon.

Both US indexes touched correction territory, a point where they are trading at 10% or more down from a recent high.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index also fell more than 4% by afternoon trading as shares in major tech companies continued to fall.

The speed at which AI investment has been growing - with more than $1 trillion spent in the last year alone by a small handful of major tech companies - has led to ongoing concerns of a financial bubble. Questions are being raised over whether those investments will pay off, and when.

Despite a positive first day of trading, Anthropic's shares fell on Friday, dropping at one point by more than 12% to about $85, close to its initial public offering (IPO) price of $83.

The artificial intelligence (AI) company's introduction to the Nasdaq stock exchange on Thursday was a crucial test for the industry and was largely seen as a success, with trading starting at $111.50.

The maker of the Claude chatbot raised a record $81bn in its initial public offering (IPO), but its share price moved significantly in the first day of trading.

The shares peaked at $115 on Thursday, before easing to end the day up 17% at $97.17.

Analysts said volatility was to be expected in the first days or even weeks of Anthropic's trading, as the company was the first frontier AI firm to go public so had no direct peers.

Some have also noted the similarities with Elon Musk's SpaceX, which at the time of its debut in June was the largest IPO on record. Shares in the rocket and AI company experienced large swings in its first few weeks of trading.

Most tech companies see their shares fall after hitting the stock market, often after reporting quarterly results for the first time.

But many, including Meta, Amazon and Google, have gone on to become the largest and most profitable corporations in the world.

Ed Moya, a strategist at market intelligence firm AlphaSense, said Anthropic's blockbuster IPO did not appear to have restored confidence in the broader AI market.

While AI demand was still very strong, Moya told the BBC that investors were trying to answer the question of how much were they willing to pay for that growth.

"As we've gone through the past past few weeks, it seems that there's been more risks that have surfaced," he said.

"Right now you're starting to see Wall Street is trying to shift from rewarding growth at any price, to demanding stronger cash flow and a clearer path to profitability."

Shares in some of the largest US tech companies also fell on Friday as the market sell off continued.

Nvidia shares had plunged by more than 11% by the afternoon, while Musk's firms SpaceX and Tesla had both fallen by more than 6%.

Meta was down more than 5% and Amazon was down more than 3.5%, while Apple and Alphabet experienced smaller falls.

Europe's main stock markets - which contain fewer tech stocks -also took a hit.

Germany's Dax index closed down 2.6%, France's CAC 40 was down 1.9% and the UK's FTSE 100 ended trading 1% lower.

Earlier on Friday, tech-heavy Asian markets saw steep falls.

South Korea's Kospi and Japan's Nikkei 225 indexes closed down about 5%, with shares in memory chip makers Sk Hynix, Kioxia and Tokyo Electron, and other tech firms such as Samsung Electronics, seeing losses.

Taiwan's stock market dropped about 6% on Friday, taking the weekly fall to more than 17% and what was reported to be its biggest weekly fall since 1990.

Ghana News.title: Ghanaian boy killed in US ‘deserved so much better’, says New York Mayor Mamdani
Ghana News.content:
A 15-year-old Ghanaian boy who was killed in the US last month was remembered as a hard-working student with dreams of becoming a doctor, as his father, New York City's mayor and civil rights leaders gave eulogies during his funeral on Friday.

Javits Frimpong was shot and killed while walking to school in the Bronx. His death has sparked outrage in both Ghana and the US, and reignited debates about gun violence in America.

"Javits deserved so much better and so do every single one of you," Mayor Zohran Mamdani said. "Though he was only a New Yorker for a short time, New York City will forever be proud to call Javits one of our own."

Frimpong moved to the US about a year before the shooting.

"I worked hard to bring you from Ghana to America because I wanted you to have opportunities, a better future, and a chance to achieve everything that you dreamed of," his father, Thomas Frimpong, said.

His mother was granted an emergency visa from Ghana to mourn her son at Friday's funeral service, following Mamdani's lobbying of President Donald Trump earlier this month.

Frimpong was chased down and shot on 29 October. He was taken to a local hospital, where he was pronounced dead.

Police have said three teenage boys were involved in the shooting. A 17-year-old has been arrested and charged with murder, and will be tried as an adult. Police are still searching for the other two.

"Gun violence is never the answer," Ben Crump, an attorney representing the family, said at the funeral as he vowed to seek justice for Frimpong.

Ghana's government has condemned the killing and said it would follow the case closely to ensure justice was achieved.

It has urged US authorities to conduct a thorough investigation and said it was ready to provide legal and consular support to ensure the perpetrators were brought to justice.

Ghana News.title: Sulemana Baba re-elected as NALAG Ahafo Regional representative
Ghana News.content:
The incumbent Ahafo Regional Representative to the National Executive Council (NEC) of the National Association of Local Authorities of Ghana (NALAG), Sulemana Baba Amadu, has been retained unopposed following a widely commended account of his stewardship during his one-year tenure.

At the close of the 2026 Ahafo Regional Delegates’ Conference, held in Goaso on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, officials from the Ahafo Regional Office of the Electoral Commission (EC) officially declared Mr Amadu duly elected after he emerged as the sole candidate to file nominations for the position.

The unopposed endorsement followed his presentation of a comprehensive 2025–2026 stewardship report under the conference theme, “Local Actions for National Impact”.

The report highlighted strides in grassroots representation, institutional welfare and community development across the region.

Addressing a gathering of Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs), Presiding Members, Assembly Members and government appointees, Mr Amadu detailed how his tenure had helped bridge the communication gap between Ahafo’s local government structures and NALAG’s national leadership.

A major highlight of his tenure was the successful collective advocacy by NALAG, in collaboration with the Minister for Local Government, the Chief of Staff and the Presidency, which resulted in MMDCEs across the region receiving brand-new official vehicles to enhance administrative mobility and service delivery.

Beyond executive logistics, his sustained engagement with MMDCEs ensured that the majority of Municipal and District Assemblies (MDAs) fulfilled their mandatory NALAG dues obligations, thereby strengthening the association’s financial footing and institutional commitment.

At the grassroots level, Mr Amadu championed the welfare and institutional identity of Assembly Members by facilitating the provision of customised identification cards for official recognition, while supporting orientation and training programmes aimed at improving accountability and local governance administration.

Between the fourth quarter of 2025 and the third quarter of 2026, he consistently raised the welfare, allowance and logistical concerns of Ahafo’s Presiding Members and Assembly Members at national NEC meetings, ensuring that regional voices shaped national deliberations.

Demonstrating NALAG’s commitment to social intervention and community development, he also facilitated the distribution of 6,900 customised NALAG exercise books to Municipal and District Assemblies across the region for onward distribution to beneficiary students.

While highlighting these achievements, the Ahafo representative used the platform to rally national leadership and regional stakeholders around critical challenges affecting grassroots governance.

He called for the establishment of a dedicated NALAG regional office in Ahafo to streamline coordination, the expedited procurement and distribution of motorbikes for Assembly Members, and the institutionalisation of capacity-building workshops.

Mr Amadu also underscored the urgent need for deliberate mentorship and public education initiatives to address the low representation of women in local government decision-making.

The Ahafo representative attributed the successes of the past year to the collective efforts of MMDCEs, Presiding Members, Assembly Members and the NALAG National Secretariat.

With a renewed mandate secured unopposed, he pledged to build on this momentum to strengthen institutional frameworks and make local governance more responsive to the needs of the people of the Ahafo Region.

Ghana News.title: Amputee World Cup: Black Challenge players, officials to receive US$8,000 each from Gold Fields
Ghana News.content:
Gold Fields Ghana Limited, the Ghana Football Association (GFA) and the National Paralympic Committee of Ghana (NPC Ghana) have agreed on a funding package that will see each Black Challenge player and delegation member receive US$8,000.

The agreement follows appeals from the players over outstanding per diems and bonuses during their campaign at the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico.

Under the revised arrangement, Gold Fields Ghana Limited will bring forward part of its 2027 sponsorship allocation to cover approved per diems and match bonuses from the group stage through to the final.

NPC Ghana President Samson Deen confirmed the agreement following discussions involving GFA President Kurt Edwin Simeon-Okraku, General Secretary Prosper Harrison Addo and Deputy General Secretary Alex Asante.

The development comes after Ghana’s historic 2-0 victory over Egypt in the quarter-finals, which secured the Black Challenge a place in the semi-finals for the first time in the competition’s history.

Ghana will face Turkey in the semi-finals as they seek to book a place in the final and continue their impressive run at the tournament.

The funding agreement is expected to address concerns over the team’s financial entitlements and allow the players to focus on their remaining matches.

Gold Fields Ghana Limited is providing the financial backing, while the GFA and NPC Ghana have worked together to facilitate the arrangement and address the welfare concerns of the delegation.

Ghana News.title: WWC 2027Q: Black Queens name squad for first phase of playoff tournament
Ghana News.content:
Black Queens head coach Kim Lars Bjorkegren has named his squad for the playoffs phase of the 2027 Women’s World Cup qualifiers.

Bjorkegren has named a 23-woman squad for the first phase of the tournament which is scheduled to be played in Rabat, Morocco.

The Swede has entrusted most of the players from the last international break with the only newbies being Beline Nyarkoh, Mavis Owusu and Nancy Amoh.

Owusu and Amoh make a return to the national team having been absent from the last two camps after training with the team before the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON).

Nyarkoh gets a first taste of senior football following her performances for Ampem Darkoa Ladies in the CAF Women’s Champions League in Egypt.

Captain Portia Boakye headlines the squad, alongside the likes of Grace Asantewaa, goalkeeper Cynthia Findiib Konlan, Jennifer Cudjoe and Chantelle Boye-Hlorkah, and a host of other players.

Ghana will open their campaign against Ecuador on November 28, before playing Uzbekistan on December 1, and then playing their final match against Papua New Guinea on December 5, 2026.

Ghana News.title: Ghana must protect inland fisheries to secure future fish supply – Fisheries Minister
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Fisheries and Aquaculture, Emelia Arthur, says that Ghana must intensify efforts to protect its inland fisheries resources through sustainable management, increased investment, and stronger collaboration with fishing communities to safeguard future fish supplies and secure livelihoods,

She said the country's fisheries future could not be secured by focusing exclusively on marine resources, stressing the importance of protecting lakes, rivers and reservoirs that support food security, employment and economic development.

“Ghana’s fisheries future cannot be secured by looking only to the sea. We must also look to our lakes, rivers and reservoirs and, more importantly, to the thousands of families whose livelihoods depend on them,” she stated.

The Minister was speaking at the maiden National Inland Fisheries Conference and World Fisheries Day Exhibition at the University of Energy and Natural Resources (UENR) in Sunyani on November 19, 2026.

The three-day event, which runs from November 19 to 21, is being held under the theme, “Sustaining Inland Fisheries for Food Security, Decent Jobs and a Resilient Blue Economy.”

According to Mrs Arthur, fisheries play a critical role in Ghana’s economy, public health and food security, providing approximately 60 per cent of the country's animal protein consumption.

She added that about three million people depend on the fisheries value chain for their livelihoods.

Highlighting the contribution of inland fisheries, the Minister disclosed that Ghana produced approximately 723,000 metric tonnes of fish in 2025, with inland capture fisheries and aquaculture accounting for nearly 39 per cent of total production.

“These are not marginal activities. They are central to our food security, rural economies, employment and national development,” she emphasised.

She identified the Volta Lake as a critical resource that sustains communities and economic activities but warned that increasing fishing pressure, pollution, destructive fishing practices and inadequate infrastructure were threatening its sustainability.

“We cannot continue to harvest today's fish at the expense of tomorrow's survival,” she cautioned.

Mrs Arthur said her recent tour of inland fishing communities across six of Ghana's 16 regions had exposed significant infrastructure and operational challenges confronting fishers.

These included deteriorating landing facilities, poor road networks, inadequate markets and safety concerns, among other challenges affecting their livelihoods.

She said the concerns raised during the engagements must translate into practical interventions and improved institutional support.

To address these challenges, the Ministry is pursuing three major priorities: sustainable fisheries management, productive investment, and the creation of jobs and economic opportunities.

On sustainable management, she announced that Ghana had developed its first-ever Inland Fisheries Management Plan, supported by the Fisheries and Aquaculture Act, 2025 (Act 1146).

She also highlighted a recently completed nationwide inland fisheries frame survey, which she said would provide an important evidence base for planning, policy formulation and investment.

However, she stressed that legislation and management plans alone would not guarantee the protection of inland fisheries resources.

“Traditional authorities, fishers and fishing communities must be partners in managing the resources on which they depend,” she said.

She added that the government's aquaculture programme would create opportunities for women, young people and vulnerable communities to establish viable businesses across the aquaculture value chain.

The Bono Regional Minister, Joseph Addae Akwaboa, also called for stronger efforts to protect inland water bodies, particularly against pollution from illegal mining.

He warned that pollution of rivers and other freshwater resources posed serious threats to fish production, the health of fishing communities and the availability of safe and nutritious food.

Mr Akwaboa further encouraged private sector investors, financial institutions and technical partners to explore opportunities in fish farming, processing, storage, transportation and marketing in the Bono Region.

The conference is expected to bring together government officials, traditional authorities, researchers, fishers, fish farmers, processors, investors and other industry players to deliberate on strategies for strengthening Ghana's inland fisheries sector.

Vice President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang is expected to join participants on Saturday, November 21, for the closing activities.

The exhibition also features local fish products, a cooking competition and an awards presentation recognising outstanding contributions to the fisheries industry.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Overturned boat carrying mourners to funeral kills at least four in Nigeria
World.content:
Police say two children among dead as search continues for more victims.

Share Overturned boat carrying mourners to funeral kills at least four in Nigeria on social media

A boat believed to be carrying hundreds of people to a funeral has overturned in southern Nigeria, killing at least four people, according to police.

The overcrowded vessel capsized on Friday in Bayelsa State after a mechanical failure while travelling from the communities of Ayama to Ukubie, police spokesperson Musa Mohammed told the Reuters news agency.

He said the dead were two adults and two children.

Police said 24 people were rescued, with 19 treated at a local clinic, and five taken to a hospital in the state capital.

Search teams were still looking for more victims, police said. Police did not say how many people were on board, but some residents told Reuters there were at least 300.

Police said the driver fled and the vessel’s manager was taken into custody.

According to a statement from the Bayelsa State Police Command, the accident occurred at the river junction between the Oweikorogha and Otuan communities, in the state’s Southern Ijaw district.

The boat that capsized was travelling “for a burial ceremony”, the statement also said, adding that police are “coordinating efforts with local divers and other responders”.

Such boat accidents are common on Nigeria’s busy rivers and waterways, often caused by overloaded vessels, poor maintenance or failure to comply with safety regulations.

A similar incident occurred in August, when at least 51 died after a boat sank in northwest Nigeria’s Sokoto State, and another in January, when at least 26 people drowned after a boat ferrying people from Jigawa to Yobe State capsized.

World.title: Fossil fuel talks deadlock pushes COP31 climate summit into overtime
World.content:
EU warns COP31 risks turning into a ‘fossil summit’ as critical climate commitments are omitted from the draft deal.

The COP31 climate summit has gone into overtime as nearly 200 countries remain deadlocked over a draft deal that no longer mentions fossil fuels.

The two-week talks in Antalya, Turkiye, were due to end on Friday, when a late closing session approved some technical matters, but not the wider political deal.

“We are close to the finish line, but we are not there yet,” COP31 President and Turkiye’s Environment Minister Murat Kurum told delegates.

Environmental groups tracking the two-week conference said the meeting lacked ambition to address the ‌worsening climate crisis and was on track to be the “worst COP ever”.

A third draft is expected on Saturday, the AFP news agency reported.

The fossil fuel fight

An opening draft from cohost and lead negotiator Australia on Monday called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels. A slimmer version on Thursday removed every mention of them after Saudi Arabia and other major oil and gas producers objected.

Oil producers have also resisted similar language at past talks, including at COP28 in 2023. The revised text also dropped a $120bn target for money to help poorer countries adapt to climate change.

The European Union said the draft “risks turning this climate COP into a fossil summit”. Panama, which signed a letter with a dozen other countries demanding “a clear transition away from fossil fuels”, threatened to walk away from the talks.

“It is not acceptable to have a COP or a cover document that does not even mention fossil fuels, and we simply will not put up with it,” Panama’s environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, told a news conference.



Other contested points

The draft proposes raising the share of the world’s final energy consumption that comes from electricity to 35 percent by 2035. It does not say the power must come from renewables, and some countries want the target to say “clean”.

Some countries also reject a push to expand carbon capture, a technology that traps emissions from power plants and factories. They say it is costly and unproven, and could let polluters keep burning oil and gas.

“We want to see the references to false solutions removed,” said Vanuatu’s climate minister, Ralph Regenvanu.

Developing countries are angry that rich nations are falling short on climate finance. “We didn’t come here to beg,” said Ghana’s environment minister, Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings.

Tough backdrop

A UN report last month found the world is set to pass the 1.5-degree-Celsius (2.7F) warming limit set under the 2015 Paris Agreement.

The United States, the largest historical emitter, is absent for a second year after President Donald Trump ended climate cooperation.

The US-Israel war on Iran and higher living costs have also drawn attention away from the talks.

Environmental groups say the summit lacks ambition.

“This has been the worst COP ever,” said Mohamed Adow, director of the think tank Power Shift Africa.

World.title: US lawmakers push for tougher AI chip rules amid China export crackdown
World.content:
Washington has new rules restricting remote access to advanced US AI chips, but lawmakers want more.

United States lawmakers say more regulations are needed to protect advanced AI chips once they leave the country, even as they support the recently imposed chip export controls.

This week, the US Department of Commerce announced a new rule to restrict how advanced US AI chips can be accessed remotely in the wake of the previous Nvidia CEO’s affair with a suspected spy for Beijing. The move would close what officials described as a loophole that allows Chinese companies to tap into computing power through data centres in third countries, bypassing US restrictions.

The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), which sits under the Commerce Department, said the rule would require data centre customers in Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Brazil to apply for a special licence to buy advanced chips from US companies, including Nvidia, because they “present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion”.

“The export controls should have been in place, certainly,” Democratic Representative Pramila Jayapal told Al Jazeera. “I also think it’s a bigger conversation about who dominates the AI market. We should not have this consolidation of all the AI knowledge in a couple of companies because that poses an enormous threat on multiple levels, including national security.”

In October, Jayapal introduced a policy framework that would require every AI company operating in the US to obtain a federal charter in an effort to protect the public interest.

The AI charter, the framework says, is modelled after existing regulatory frameworks, combining the round-the-clock federal oversight, strict safety mandates, and structural separation built into national bank charters with the rigorous pre-release federal testing required for nuclear materials and dangerous weapons.



The framework also bans AI companies from building empires, releasing risky models, stealing through surveillance, exploiting workers, or causing harm.

Lutnick probe

Jayapal is a member of the House of Representatives Judiciary Committee, whose ranking members announced a probe to determine whether Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had blocked efforts to stop the suspected smuggling of advanced Nvidia chips to China.

Lutnick is facing criticism, including from members of US President Donald Trump’s cabinet, for allegedly refusing to impose restrictions on companies accused of diverting advanced chips to China, including Megaspeed, which is at the centre of the Nvidia probe.

The House Foreign Affairs Committee also announced that the Trump administration had approved exports of 879,000 chips manufactured by Nvidia and AMD to Chinese companies between December 2025 and May 2026.

Democrats, who will control both chambers of Congress in January, expressed a desire to better limit chip exports amid growing scrutiny over the extent to which US computing power may have reached China.

“I’m excited to get these gavels and go through the investigatory work that’s necessary, but also to rein in and regulate artificial intelligence. The very industry is asking to be regulated by Congress,” Democratic Representative Everton Blair told Al Jazeera.

‘Tremendous penalties’

The US accounts for nearly 75 percent of the world’s AI spending and computing power, followed by China.

US tech giants, including Amazon, Microsoft and Google, operate nearly 90 major AI computing hubs globally, according to an Oxford University study. The same research found that US companies were building 63 AI computing hubs outside the country as of 2025.

Stephen Ezell, vice president for global innovation policy at the Information Technology and Innovation Foundation (ITIF), said Washington would find it difficult to enforce the BIS rule.

China has rejected the restriction, calling it “economic coercion” by the US.

On Friday, after his return to the White House from his historic trilateral meeting with the Chinese and Russian presidents in Shenzhen, China, Trump promised to prohibit US companies from developing data centres in other countries.

“We’re going to put tremendous penalties on companies that try and do it,” Trump said.

It was unclear what Trump had envisioned, or how he would enforce it.

At the same time, he urged Americans to embrace data centres in their neighbourhoods, despite communities’ increasing concern about the centres’ impact on quality of life, environment and energy demands.



Analysts say the recent export regulation has likely not had much effect on China’s efforts to become the global leader in AI semiconductor chips.

“China does not want to depend upon American or other foreign semiconductors. They want to develop them themselves, and one can argue that we’ve slowed them down a little bit with our export controls, but in no way has it changed China’s aspirations to become the global AI semiconductor chip leader,” Ezell said on Al Jazeera’s This Is America.
