World.title: Trump defends Putin relationship, warns AI data centres must stay in US
World.content:
The US president also spoke about the war in Iran and praised trip to China during a wide-ranging news conference.

United States President Donald Trump has praised his recent trip to China and defended the relationship with his “friend” Vladimir Putin, but questioned whether the Russian president was a friend to the US.

On Friday, during a White House news briefing, Trump was asked about the “friend” remark — made during his historic summit with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping earlier this week — and whether the Russian leader was a friend to the US.

“I can’t speak to America,” Trump told reporters before saying Putin had been “very nice” during what he described as the “Russia hoax” investigation after his 2016 presidential campaign.

“I consider him to be somebody that I have a very good relationship. And it’s actually very good,” Trump added as he talked about Russia’s nuclear weapons capabilities.

“I think it gives us a lot of additional strength,” he said.

Trump also spoke about the historic nature of his meeting with Xi and Putin, praising the “first of its kind trilateral peace agreement”. He said there was “great electricity” between the leaders of the world’s main nuclear powers.

“We had one of the most momentous international summits in many years. That was the first ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China,” Trump said.

“I have fantastic relationships with Putin. That’s a very good thing. I have fantastic relationships with President Xi. That’s a good thing, and our country is safe because of that,” he also said.

No major deals were announced from the summit. But Trump, on Friday, played up his agreement with the two leaders to hold future discussions on nuclear proliferation.



The US president’s remarks came during a wide-ranging news conference, where topics from Iran to artificial intelligence were also discussed.

Trump accused Iran of negotiating in bad faith to end the war, which is about to mark its 10-month anniversary.

“They want to make a deal, but they don’t want to make a deal that’s acceptable to me,” he said. “We wanna make a real deal, not a fake deal.”

Trump added: “They’ve been b*********** people for 51 years.”

During the news conference, US Vice President JD Vance and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, both possible 2028 presidential contenders, flanked Trump in the White House press briefing room.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and US Defence Secretary Hegseth, as well as newly minted White House chief of staff Stephen Miller, were also present.

Trump denied he was upset at Vance for blaming US Republicans’ historic midterm losses on the Iran war, saying, “People that work for me, they have a right to their opinion.”

“I thought his statement was fine, except I would have had one other thing that, if we were asked, I would have said that, would you do it again, and absolutely the answer is yes,” Trump said. “I saw that, but no problem there at all.”

No data centres abroad

Vance was asked by reporters about his thoughts on his party’s midterm drubbing.

“I think the president is the one who makes the decision. And the president has said he would do it again,” Vance said. “My goal, in my job, is to support the President of the United States.”

Trump also warned US tech companies against building new artificial intelligence data centres overseas. Otherwise, he said, they will face a “tremendous tax”.

“We’re not allowing data centres to go into other countries because China will take all of them”, Trump said. “And we’re going to put tremendous penalties on companies that try and do it.”

Trump did not provide details on how he would enforce such a policy and said he had not yet told his own officials about his plan.

Al Jazeera has reached out to the White House for comment but has not yet heard back.

World.title: Tech stock sell-off drags markets down as Anthropic shares slide
World.content:
Anthropic's shares have dropped back towards their initial price after a soaring first day on the stock market, as a wider tech sell-off dragged markets down.

The sell-off comes as concerns remain over the speed and size of artificial intelligence investment, but also as some large companies including Nvidia and SpaceX faced specific issues that worried investors.

Those pressures combined to weigh on US markets through Friday, with all key US indexes closing sharply down on the day, furthering earlier falls over the week.

The S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average were pushed into correction territory, a point where they are trading at 10% or more down from a recent high.

The S&P 500 closed down 3.7%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 1.9% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index plunged 5.3%. However, all three indexes were up on where they were a year ago.

The speed at which AI investment has been growing - with more than $1 trillion spent in the last year alone by a small handful of major tech companies - has led to ongoing concerns of a financial bubble. Questions are being raised over whether those investments will pay off, and when.

Investors were also spooked after the Democrats' resounding win in the US midterms in early November, which sparked fears of a reduction in AI development.

Despite a positive first day of trading, Anthropic's shares fell on Friday, dropping at one point by more than 12% to about $85, close to its initial public offering (IPO) price of $83. It closed down 8.5%, reversing half of the gains made on Thursday.

The artificial intelligence (AI) company's introduction to the Nasdaq stock exchange on Thursday was a crucial test for the industry and was largely seen as a success, with trading starting at $111.50 before easing to end the day up 17% at $97.17.

Analysts said volatility was to be expected in the first days or even weeks of Anthropic's trading, as the company was the first frontier AI firm to go public so had no direct peers.

World.title: UK to explore even closer ties with EU after agreeing deal, says Burnham
World.content:
Andy Burnham said the UK will discuss possible options for even closer ties with the EU, after agreeing a deal covering British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme.

The prime minister said it was a "good day" for Britain and Europe, adding the Treasury believes the deal could boost the UK economy by up to Â£17bn a year.

European Council President AntÃ³nio Costa said the EU remains "open to have the closest possible relationship" with the UK.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the deal "isn't fair" - and Reform's Nigel Farage called it a "betrayal of the British people".

Legislation to implement the deal is expected to be introduced in the UK Parliament next week.

Burnham arrived in Brussels to finalise the latest stage of the government's post-Brexit "reset" of relations with the EU, which originally began under former prime minister Sir Keir Starmer.

The agreements announced on Friday included scrapping most of the checks on British food exports, in return for the UK following some EU regulations, from 2028.

The UK government believes the changes will cut costs for businesses and could bring prices down for shoppers, while critics argue the change will make the UK a "rule taker" from Brussels rather than a rule maker.

World.title: Russian missile hits Poland as Ukraine's allies hold military exercise, says Tusk
World.content:
Poland says a Russian cruise missile was among three objects that violated its airspace early on Friday, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk saying it did not appear to be an accident when Western military exercises were taking place in the region.

Nobody was hurt and no damage has been reported, but Warsaw described the incident as a "provocation" from Moscow.

Russia has made no comment about the violations, which took place during one of its biggest aerial attacks on Ukraine since the start of the full-scale invasion in 2022.

Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said the Kh-101 missile hit a rural area at Nowy Lipowiec in southeastern Poland about 50km (31 miles) from the Ukrainian border.

The cruise missile, designed for precision targets, crashed at about 06:30 (5:30GMT) and Natalie Szponar, a local resident, said she was getting her children ready for school when she heard a "whistle and a dull impact".

The moment of impact was caught by a camera on a farm, and officials later made clear there was no risk to residents.

Another suspected missile went down near Rudnik nad Sanem to the west of Nowy Lipowiec, and a jet-powered drone crashed to the south near MoÅodycz, said Kosiniak-Kamysz.

World.title: French police officers sentenced for beating of music producer Michel Zecler
World.content:
Three French police officers have been convicted of beating up a black music producer six years ago in Paris in what the court upheld as an aggravated circumstance of racism.

The three were also found guilty of signing a falsified police report stating that the producer - Michel Zecler, 47 - had violently resisted their attempt to arrest him.

Their lies were exposed because the whole scene at Zecler's recording studio was caught on CCTV, revealing the producer had suffered some 30 punches, kicks and baton strikes while offering little resistance at all.

Aurelien Lapersonne, 29, Philippe Tondeux, 50, and Pierre Plantier, 37, all received five year sentences, with different amounts suspended.

Lapersonne had three years of his sentence suspended and Tondeux three and a half years suspended. Plantier had four years suspended, and will serve his one year with an ankle monitor.

All were told they could never serve in the police again.

The case became a cause cÃ©lÃ¨bre for critics of the police, who say it exposed systematic racism among officers. With police again facing criticism for alleged use of excessive force in stopping recent protests, the verdict was hotly awaited by Zecler's supporters.

Much depended in the two-week trial on Zecler's own testimony that the officers called him a racial slur during the beating.

This was denied by the three policemen, who in court admitted the beating and the faked report but denied there was a racial motivation. But the court preferred the evidence of the producer, because - unlike the police - everything else he said was verifiably true.

Because the racist element was accepted by the court, the sentences were toughened.

The case was heard by a panel of five judges.

The incident took place during the Covid lockdown in 2020. Zecler was accused by the officers for not wearing a mask when doing so was obligatory as he approached his studio on foot.

They later claimed his behaviour aroused their suspicions, and they thought he might be carrying drugs. No evidence of this emerged.

After Zecler entered the lobby, the police followed - without a warrant - and tried to bring him outside. Zecler refused to go out, and the beating ensued. Zecler cried for help and some people appeared from the basement and pushed the police outside.

The officers then smashed a glass pane and sent a tear-gas grenade into the building, forcing those inside to come out - after which Zecler was again hit. He was then arrested.

During the trial Zecler said had it not been for the CCTV video, he would have been in court not as a victim but as a potential criminal.

In their last words before the court, all three police officers apologised for what they had done. Tondeux said he was sorry "for the image of the police that I have given".

World.title: In a year of AI solving maths problems, Anthropic may have just solved the biggest
World.content:
An Anthropic employee and mathematician claims to have used the company's artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot to prove the famed Riemann hypothesis.

Levent AlpÃ¶ge said, external on Friday, a day after Anthropic made its US stock market debut, that over the course of about six weeks, he used the Claude chatbot to create a detailed proof of the maths problem.

If found to be correct, the proof would be among the most significant in history. AlpÃ¶ge described it as "one dawn across science of something far greater".

The claim comes as AI firms like OpenAI have in recent months announced scores of solutions to major higher maths problems that have eluded scholars for decades.

As for the Riemann hypothesis proof put forward on Friday, it was found using a non-public version of Anthropic's Claude.

It is a nearly 170-year-old maths problem that deals with prime numbers and is widely considered to be the single most famous problem in maths, in large part due to how complex it is.

Named for the mathematician Bernhard Riemann, the hypothesis puts forward that prime numbers have a determined order along the number line.

Prime numbers are the bedrock of higher maths, leaving breakthroughs related to them to have broad impact.

AlpÃ¶ge said that he messaged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Sunday, asking him directly about how he could announce the discovery.

"The precise timing is horrible," AlpÃ¶ge said, referring to Anthropic's public stock listing. "If I could have, I'd have finished this all much earlier."

"I am clearly unilaterally responsible for feeling I just could not live if I waited even longer. There is an obvious cynical view, to do with the timing, but it is false," he added.

The complete proof that AlpÃ¶ge put forward in Lean, a computer language used for confirming maths proofs, is over 250,000 lines long.

Terrance Tao, a prominent mathematician, said on Friday, external that verification of the proof is still some way off.

"I imagine the digestion process will take some time, though in this case at least we have a human author to communicate with to assist with this task," Tao said.

No such human was obviously a part of major maths proofs made earlier this year using AI.

OpenAI in September claimed that employees using a non-public version of its AI tools were able to solve part of a notoriously difficult problem in just 88 hours. The problem was part of the Navier-Stokes equations, which concern how fluids move.

More than 10,000 AI agents, or computer programmed bots that operate somewhat autonomously, were put to the task as an AI training exercise.

The proof that OpenAI released on Navier-Stokes has yet to be confirmed as accurate, and it set off criticism within academic and higher maths communities and organisations about the use of AI to solve maths problems.

Anthropic has also claimed to have made other progress and solutions in maths, external and physics, external.

A group of maths scholars said, external AI companies boasting of major solutions to show how sophisticated their commercial products had become was "detrimental to the science of mathematics".

"We are witnessing a general threat to intellectual work, with misalignment between the outcome of the use of AI and its initial purpose," the scholars said in a group letter.

A month later, OpenAI released, external what it claimed were solutions, proofs, or major progress on 372 more outstanding higher maths problems.

It will take months, if not longer, for those claims to be reviewed by experts to prove their validity.

World.title: Gérard Depardieu and French author investigated over sexual allegations
World.content:
Warning: this story contains graphic content

French authorities are investigating disgraced actor GÃ©rard Depardieu and the author Michel Houellebecq over "allegations of a sexual nature", a source with knowledge of the investigation says.

The confirmation comes after reports in French media that the two were accused of being involved in a "gang rape" on the set of the film Thalasso in 2018 by an actress.

The source told the BBC that a judicial investigation was launched after a complaint was filed in May 2025.

Depardieu has already separately been convicted of unrelated sexual assaults. The BBC has contacted Depardieu's lawyers and Houellebecq, an acclaimed French author and occasional actor, for comment.

The actress, who has not been named publicly, accused Depardieu of penetration without consent and Houellebecq of forcing her to perform oral sex, in an interview with Mediapart, a French investigative site which first reported the allegations.

She told the outlet that none of this had been written into the script, and that she experienced "profound humiliation" and "unspeakable shame".

French law stipulates as of 2025 that all sexual acts performed without consent constitute rape.

The film's director, Guillaume Nicloux, has been accused of being complicit because he was said to have filmed the incident, Mediapart and AFP report. The BBC has contacted his agent and the Paris prosecutor's office for comment.

Nicloux told Mediapart that the scene had been improvised and he had not intervened as he had not observed "any constraints, verbal or physical opposition, or even discomfort".

The site published production documents showing footage of the scene had been destroyed.

The actress told the outlet that she had told friends, her agent and others involved in the film's production in Normandy about the incident at the time, but only filed the complaint after other women accused Depardieu of sexual misconduct.

The Asterix and Obelix star will next week find out whether he will stand trial for allegedly raping another actress, Charlotte Arnould.

On Monday, Depardieu dropped his appeal against a separate conviction for two counts of sexual assault during another film shoot, for which he was handed an 18-month suspended sentence.

Several other women have made allegations against the 77-year-old in the media.

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, details of help and support in the UK are available at BBC Action Line

World.title: Russia targets Kyiv crossings days after Ukraine hits Crimean Bridge
World.content:
Russia targeted bridges in Kyiv and railway stations overnight in a major attack launched days after Ukraine badly damaged the strategically important Crimean Bridge.

Ballistic missiles hit key crossings in the capital during a nationwide assault which Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said was "one of the most massive strikes" of the war so far and left at least nine dead.

Russian President Vladimir Putin had threatened to retaliate for the attack on the Crimean Bridge, which the Kremlin built to link Russia and the occupied Crimean peninsula.

The latest Russian strikes coincided with talks around the war, and came as the Kremlin pushed back against a US claim that Russia could be open to Western-backed security guarantees for Ukraine.

The overnight attack against Ukraine was spread across several cities and regions, Zelensky said, with residential buildings and energy facilities also hit.

Air raid sirens lasted non-stop throughout the night and were ongoing into the morning.

Zelensky said over 110 missiles and more than 400 attack drones were launched by Russia, adding that "particularly insidious" tactics to launch the waves in 20 to 30-minute internals made it "more difficult to extinguish fires, clear debris, and restore services".

The three bridges targeted in Kyiv - the Podilsko-Voskresensky Bridge, the Darnytskyi Bridge and the Southern Bridge - were closed to traffic.

Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko urged people to "avoid travelling into the city by private car unless absolutely necessary", adding to the disruption around the capital following a first round of strikes against vital crossings earlier this week.

World.title: Mamdani announces plan to close New York's Rikers Island jail by 2032
World.content:
New York City's official overseeing the closure of the city's most notorious jail hopes a new plan from Mayor Zohran Mamdani will lead to "a moment of transformation" for how people are detained in the largest US city.

Mamdani on Friday unveiled a plan to close the Rikers Island complex by 2032, to build four new jails and drastically reduce the city's detainee population.

Plans to shutter the troubled facility date back to 2019, when the city council first voted to close it by this year. But plans have been delayed over the years in part due to the logistical difficulties over where to place inmates.

Dana Kaplan - who Mamdani appointed as the city's "Close Rikers Czar" told the BBC News channel on Friday that his latest proposal is not just about getting rid of a decrepit facility.

It is also a "generational opportunity" to "build a different type of detention system" and figure out how to detain people more appropriately, she said.

The Rikers Island jail complex is perched on a 413 acre (167 hectare) island between Queens and the Bronx, and has earned a variety of nicknames over the years because of its dilapidated conditions, including Gladiator School and Torture Island. The jail has housed a number of high-profile inmates awaiting trial, including Tupac Shakur, DMX and Harvey Weinstein.

It houses more than 6,500 inmates at a given time. Mamdani hopes to reduce that number to 4,100 - a goal that has been met with skepticism by the New York City correction officers' union.

"[B]uilding a new system that puts an arbitrary cap on the City's available jail beds is ill-conceived, irresponsible and jeopardizes the safety of all New Yorkers, including our Officers," NYC Correction Officers' Benevolent Association said in a statement. "The City cannot keep the jail population at around 4,100 without irresponsibly releasing individuals who committed violent felony charges."

Kaplan disagreed.

"It's actually possible to have fewer people in jail in New York City - and that is what we should be planning for," she said.

The jail complex has long faced backlash over staffing shortages, crumbling conditions and inmate deaths in the facility, including nine this year. Legislation required the jail to be shuttered by 2027, but Mamdani blamed lags under former Mayor Eric Adams' administration as well as the Covid pandemic for the delays.

Last year, under Adams, a federal judge removed Rikers from the city's control, appointing an independent outside official to make decisions concerning the facility.

In an 88-page report released on Friday, Mamdani said Rikers was a product of "deteriorating infrastructure" and that officials had a "moral imperative" to close it.

New York City Council must approve the updated timeline, with members, including the city's speaker, indicating they support the plan.

Mamdani's office said the city would open up four new jails - one in Brooklyn by 2029, two in the Bronx and Queens by 2031 and one in Manhattan by 2032.

The mayor's office argues the new, smaller facilities will provide inmates "access to daylight, fresh air and clean space" leading to better outcomes for detainees. The facilities will be easier for families to access as well, as travel to the remote Rikers can take hours.

Mamdani said his administration would work to reduce the number of people being held in jail across New York City, including by offering alternative programmes to detention for some awaiting trial, by making it easier for families to post bail online and by trying to speed up the pretrial legal process.

He also wants to open up hundreds of beds in therapeutic housing units for prisoners with serious mental health issues.

Kaplan said Mamdani's administration had already opened 100 therapeutic beds at Bellevue Hospital in Manhattan, moving 100 people off of Rikers Island.

The proposal involves a large investments: $146m (Â£111m) for mental health and substance use treatment and vocational and education programming inside and outside the jails.

World.title: 2027: Abiodun says investors bet on Ogun’s political stability, governance continuity
World.content:
Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, has attributed the sustained influx of investors into the state, even as his administration approaches the end of its tenure, to growing confidence in his government’s policies, the peaceful political atmosphere and the prospect of continuity under the All Progressives Congress (APC).

Abiodun said the orderly political transition within the ruling party had further strengthened investors’ confidence that the stability, economic reforms and development trajectory established by his administration would be sustained beyond 2027.

The governor spoke on Friday when he led the APC governorship candidate, Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, to a meeting with members of the Egba Traditional Council at Ake, Abeokuta.

He noted that Ogun State had continued to attract fresh investments because of its peaceful environment, improved infrastructure and deliberate policies aimed at creating an enabling environment for businesses to thrive.

According to him, his administration has attracted more than 6,000 companies to the state in the last seven years, constructed over 1,700 kilometres of roads, built about 8,000 houses and recruited more than 8,000 teachers into public primary and secondary schools.

Abiodun maintained that the absence of political violence, thuggery and wanton destruction of lives and property had become a major selling point for Ogun State, assuring investors that their investments were safe and their businesses could operate without unnecessary disruptions.

“Investors can now come here, bring their dollars, change them into naira and know that their profits can also be repatriated at an exchange rate that is meaningful to them. There is confidence in the economy of Nigeria,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The governor particularly observed that the continued interest of investors, despite the approaching end of his administration, demonstrated their confidence in the political and economic direction of the state.

He cited the recent groundbreaking of the $1.8 billion industrial park project by the LEE Group as evidence that investors remained confident in Ogun’s economic prospects.

He also acknowledged the economic reforms introduced by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, particularly the removal of fuel subsidy and the unification of foreign exchange rates, saying they had created opportunities for governments to redirect resources towards critical infrastructure and economic development.

According to him, the reforms had helped create a more predictable economic environment, encouraged investment and strengthened the capacity of governments to provide infrastructure that supports industrial growth.

“By removing subsidy and achieving convergence of the naira, the economy has since stabilised. Our foreign reserves have gone from a mere three billion dollars to 60 billion dollars today.

“Tax revenue generation has gone from N19 trillion to N28 trillion, a record in the last 19 years. When I hear someone saying he would return subsidy, I wonder if they understand what they are talking about. The same subsidy was taking 20 per cent of our budget, and none of us could feel its impact,” he said.

Abiodun urged traditional rulers and residents of Ogun Central Senatorial District to support the APC candidates in the forthcoming elections, warning against entrusting leadership positions to individuals without clearly articulated development plans.

He said political ambition alone was not sufficient qualification for leadership, stressing the need for candidates to demonstrate a clear understanding of governance and the practical steps required to move the state forward.

The governor described the relationship between his administration and the APC governorship candidate as unprecedented in the political history of Ogun State, noting that the peaceful process of identifying a successor had reinforced confidence in the state’s political future.

“Where a sitting governor is unveiling his successor in the same party in a manner where there was no rancour, bitterness or violence, it has instilled confidence in investors. Everybody continues to avail us the same confidence that they have had since 2019.

“What does that mean? It means one thing: continuity is extremely important to socioeconomic development. We cannot allow just anyone to come and reverse the fortunes we have achieved, particularly in the last seven years,” he said.

Abiodun expressed confidence in Senator Adeola’s capacity to build on the achievements of his administration, saying the APC candidate understood the development agenda and would sustain ongoing projects and programmes.

In his remarks, Adeola commended the cordial relationship between the governor and the party’s leadership, describing continuity as essential to sustaining development.

He pledged to consolidate on the achievements of the Abiodun administration, promising to continue from where the incumbent governor would stop.

“I will be seated as your governor to ensure that where Governor Dapo Abiodun stops, I will continue from there, and that is why we are preaching continuity,” he said.

Adeola cited Lagos State as an example of how successive administrations within the same political structure could sustain development policies and build on the achievements of their predecessors.

He expressed optimism that Ogun’s economic prospects would expand further with the development of the Gateway Deep Sea Port and commercial oil exploration activities around Eba and Tongeji Island.

According to him, these projects, alongside other ongoing investments, would significantly expand the state’s revenue base, with the potential to increase its internally generated revenue from the current N250 billion to N1 trillion.

He also attributed the state’s development prospects to the working relationship between Abiodun and President Tinubu, saying the cooperation had helped attract strategic investments and infrastructure projects.

Former Ogun State Governor, Chief Olusegun Osoba, in his remarks, commended the Abiodun administration for promoting industrial development in Ogun Central and expanding educational opportunities across the state.

Osoba urged sons and daughters of the senatorial district to participate actively in the forthcoming elections.

The meeting also featured the conferment of traditional chieftaincy titles on some political leaders. Senator Adeola was conferred with the title of Araba Egba, while his wife, Temitope Adeola, received the title of Asiwaju Iya Ewe. The APC deputy governorship candidate, Mrs Kudirat Balogun, was conferred with the title of Asiwaju Iya Ibiye.

World.title: Nigeria begins construction of passport factory, targets six million booklets yearly
World.content:
The Federal Government has begun construction of a passport manufacturing plant expected to produce six million Nigerian passport booklets annually by May 2027, as part of efforts to end reliance on foreign manufacturers.

The Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, disclosed this on Friday during the groundbreaking ceremony for the National Passport Manufacturing Centre at the Nigeria Immigration Service headquarters in Abuja.

Mr Tunji-Ojo explained that the facility, which occupies 1.1 hectares of land, would be artificial intelligence-driven and operate off-grid, with capacity to increase production to 10 million booklets annually.

He said the project would complete the localisation of Nigeria’s passport production value chain, allowing the country to manufacture the travel document locally rather than import it.

According to the minister, Nigeria currently requires approximately two million passport booklets annually, meaning the proposed facility would have capacity to produce significantly more than domestic demand.

He said the additional capacity could allow Nigeria to supply neighbouring countries that currently obtain their passports from Europe and the Americas.

Mr Tunji-Ojo described the project as a major step in Nigeria’s efforts to strengthen its control over the production of a document that represents the country’s identity and sovereignty.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said Nigeria would become the first country in West Africa to have an e-passport manufacturing plant and the second on the African continent with full e-passport production capacity.

“This facility will complete the full localisation of the Nigerian passport value chain,” he said, explaining that the project followed reforms introduced since 2023 to automate passport application and approval processes.

He added that the reforms continued in 2024 with the introduction of contactless biometric passport applications, followed by the establishment of a passport personalisation centre in 2025.

The manufacturing plant, he said, would complete the process by bringing the production of passport booklets fully within Nigeria.

Mr Tunji-Ojo said the development would also reduce the influence of foreign exchange fluctuations on passport production costs, although he did not provide details of how the new facility would affect passport fees.

Previous reforms in passport production

PREMIUM TIMES had earlier reported that the Interior Minister said the Nigeria Immigration Service had undergone significant technological and infrastructure reforms under the Tinubu administration, including the establishment of an 8.3-petabyte data centre and the introduction of systems for passenger profiling.

The minister also explained that the government had cleared a backlog of 204,332 passports, introduced contactless passport renewals for Nigerians in the diaspora and deployed e-gates at major airports.

The passport manufacturing project builds on these reforms, with the government seeking to bring application processing, personalisation and booklet production under a locally managed system.

He highlighted that the new facility would enable Nigeria to produce the sovereign travel document domestically and potentially supply other countries.

He also said the project was part of the government’s broader efforts to modernise the Immigration Service.

“Under this administration, Nigeria will no longer import the sovereign document that carries our identity,” he said.

World.title: PCN seals 261 illegal, non-compliant medicine outlets in FCT
World.content:
The Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) says it has sealed 261 medicine outlets in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) for operating illegally or violating pharmaceutical regulations.

The Head of Enforcement at the PCN, Suleiman Chiroma, disclosed this at a press briefing in Abuja on Friday while presenting the outcome of a four-day enforcement exercise in the FCT.

Mr Chiroma said the council inspected 455 premises in Bwari Area Council and parts of Lugbe in the Abuja Municipal Area Council (AMAC).

He said the sealed premises comprised 100 pharmacies, 115 patent medicine shops and 46 illegal outlets, while six compliance directives were issued to operators found violating regulatory requirements.

According to him, the inspection covered 246 pharmacies, 163 Patent and Proprietary Medicine Vendor (PPMV) shops and 46 illegal outlets.

Mr Chiroma said the exercise was part of the council’s efforts to sanitise Nigeria’s drug distribution system and enforce compliance with the National Drug Distribution Guidelines (NDDG).

He said the exercise aimed to curb the unauthorised sale and distribution of ethical and controlled medicines while ensuring that pharmaceutical premises were managed by qualified and licensed personnel.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He added that the council was working to ensure that PPMVs operated strictly within their approved scope of practice and to eliminate illegal medicine outlets.

The enforcement team observed that some pharmaceutical premises operated without registration, while several PPMV shops stocked ethical medicines, injectables and intravenous infusions contrary to the Approved Patent Medicine List.

Other violations included poor record-keeping, improper signage, unhygienic premises, unrestricted access to poisons by unauthorised persons and the training of apprentices.

Mr Chiroma also identified unethical conduct among some pharmacists as one of the regulatory breaches observed during the exercise.

He said 59 per cent of the pharmacies inspected complied fully with regulatory standards, while only 29 per cent of PPMV outlets met the required standards.

He said all 46 illegal premises identified during the exercise were sealed in accordance with the law.

The enforcement officer expressed concern over an incident in which a registered pharmacist allegedly broke the seal placed on his premises by the council.

He said the pharmacist would face the full disciplinary process and appropriate sanctions to deter other operators from similar violations.

Mr Chiroma warned that the council would not tolerate breaches of pharmaceutical laws and regulations, adding that offenders would face prompt and appropriate sanctions.

He urged members of the public to purchase medicines only from PCN-licensed premises, advising operators to display valid and current licences as proof of authorisation.

He said the enforcement exercise formed part of the council’s sustained efforts to eliminate unlicensed and non-compliant operators from the medicine distribution chain.

According to him, the initiative will help curb the circulation of substandard and falsified medicines and ensure that medicines are handled, stored and dispensed by qualified personnel in approved premises.

Mr Chiroma said the Registrar of the council, Ibrahim Ahmed, had directed sustained enforcement of pharmaceutical regulations in the FCT.

He appreciated residents of Bwari and Lugbe for their cooperation and support during the exercise, emphasising the importance of stakeholder collaboration in ensuring access to safe and quality medicines.

The PCN is the federal agency responsible for regulating pharmacy education, training and practice, including the activities of pharmacy technicians and patent and proprietary medicine vendors. (NAN)

World.title: Court remands 11 Malians over alleged kidnapping, human trafficking
World.content:
The Federal High Court in Abuja on Friday remanded 11 Malian nationals at the Suleja Correctional Centre over allegations of kidnapping victims for ransom and human trafficking.

Justice Obiora Egwuatu ordered their remand after they pleaded not guilty to an amended four-count charge.

The defendants are Abdul Ngeki, Ahmed Kasango, Hassan Dauda, Saidu Traore, Ahmed Sirama, Mohammed Dembele, Musa Sidibe, Fatima Coulibaly, Aisha Dembele, Habi Tohgo and Lah Ahmed.

The Nigerian government accused the defendants, including four women, of committing the offences in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) between March and April 2026.

Rotimi Oyedepo, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) and Director of Public Prosecutions of the Federation, filed the amended charge on behalf of the federal government on 26 October.

In the first count, the prosecution accused the defendants of conspiring to detain Alfonseni Diakite and other victims against their will to demand ransom from their families.

The second count accused them of detaining Mr Diakite and other victims for the same purpose.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The prosecution said the alleged offences contravened Sections 26(1) and 24(1)(a) of the Terrorism (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022.

In the third count, the defendants were accused of conspiring to receive Mr Diakite and other victims through deception for exploitation in exchange for money and other property.

The fourth count accused them of receiving the victims through deception for the same purpose.

The prosecution said the two trafficking-related counts violated Sections 27 and 13 of the Trafficking in Persons (Prohibition) Enforcement and Administration Act, 2015.

Arraignment

Before the arraignment on Friday, M.A. Oladunjoye, an Assistant Chief State Counsel, asked the judge to direct that the charges be read to the defendants so they could enter their pleas.

The defence lawyer, Steven Ogbadu, did not oppose the application. The charges were subsequently read and interpreted to the defendants in French through an interpreter. All 11 pleaded not guilty.

Ms Oladunjoye then asked the court to fix a trial date and remand the defendants to the Suleja Correctional Centre pending the proceedings.

ALSO READ: Police arrest seven over alleged kidnapping plot in Kwara

When Justice Egwuatu asked why the prosecution preferred the Suleja facility, she explained that the Kuje Correctional Centre did not accommodate female inmates.

Mr Ogbadu did not oppose the remand application. He, however, told the court that the defence was already “engaging with the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF), Lateef Fagbemi, to resolve the matter through a ‘plea bargain’ rather than proceed to trial.

Justice Egwuatu subsequently ordered that the defendants be remanded at the Suleja Correctional Centre pending trial.

He adjourned the case until 26 January for the trial to commence.

World.title: ‘Akwa Ibom State’s finest gift to Nigeria’: Ex-Gov Emmanuel celebrates Attah at 88
World.content:
Former Governor Udom Emmanuel of Akwa Ibom State described Victor Attah, the state’s second elected governor, as a towering figure in Nigeria’s history.

Mr Emmanuel stated this in a tribute celebrating Mr Attah’s 88th birthday on Friday, 20 November.

“As one of Akwa Ibom State’s finest gifts to Nigeria and the world, you remain a towering figure in our national story, a statesman whose name evokes visionary leadership, the dignity of public service and an abiding faith in the possibilities of his people,” Mr Emmanuel said of Mr Attah in a message posted on Facebook.

Mr Emmanuel said Mr Attah’s stewardship in Akwa Ibom remained historic, distinguished by a vision that looked beyond the limitations of its circumstances and dared to imagine what a determined people could become.

Mr Attah served as governor of the oil-rich Akwa Ibom State from 1999 to 2007.

Often referred to as the father of modern Akwa Ibom, Mr Attah conceived the Akwa Ibom airport project and commenced its construction before leaving office in 2007. The airport is named after him.

Apart from the Victor Attah International Airport in Uyo, the home base of the Akwa Ibom-owned Ibom Air, Mr Attah also built the multi-million-dollar Ibom Independent Power Plant at Ikot Abasi and the Akwa Ibom State University at Ikot Akpaden, Mkpat Enin Local Government Area.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

But Mr Attah’s most profound impact, perhaps, was his fierce fight for resource control during President Olusegun Obasanjo’s administration, which led the Federal Government to pay the 13 per cent oil-derivation fund to the states in Nigeria’s Niger Delta region.

The recent PREMIUM TIMES report that Governor Umo Eno’s administration in Akwa Ibom received ₦2.934 trillion in public revenue in 38 months aptly reflects the impact of Mr Attah’s fight. Other states in the Niger Delta are also reporting huge revenues.

Attah has ‘attained immortality’

Pat Utomi, a politician and political economist, visited Akwa Ibom last month, was astonished by the enduring influence of Mr Attah’s development vision, and afterwards wrote that the former governor had “attained immortality, like Chief Obafemi Awolowo, Dr Michael Okpara and Sir Ahmadu Bello.”

Former Governor Emmanuel, in his birthday message to Mr Attah, said his (Attah’s) years of service remind us that the measure of leadership lies not merely in the offices occupied, but in the possibilities opened for others.

“You understood that leadership must be more than the administration of the present; it must be the courage to imagine a future generations yet unborn can inherit with pride. Your advocacy for resource ownership, fiscal justice and the equitable place of the Niger Delta in Nigeria’s federation further testified to a statesmanship unconfined by the boundaries of political office.

“The truth permanently etched on the minds of millions of Akwa Ibom people and Nigerians is that your legacies and imprints of patriotic stewardship continue to remain an abiding source of inspiration to Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria and generations yet unborn.

“On this auspicious event of your birthday, we celebrate the elder statesman, patriot and visionary whose contributions remain woven into the political and developmental history of our state.

“May the years ahead bring you abundant grace, the warmth of family, enduring good health and the profound satisfaction of seeing your dreams continue to find expression in the lives of your people.

“Happy Birthday, our patriot and statesman!” Mr Emmanuel wrote.

Mr Emmanuel was the fourth elected governor of Akwa Ibom. His administration conceived and set up Ibom Air, the first commercial airline established by a state government in Nigeria. The administration also built the new international terminal at the Victor Attah International Airport.

World.title: Tompolo, Okpebholo target 2.5m votes for Tinubu in Edo; group donates 25 vehicles for campaign
World.content:
The Grand Patron of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, and Edo State Governor Senator Monday Okpebholo have set a target of 2.5 million votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 16 January 2027 presidential election.

The duo made the declaration in Benin City, Edo State, during the inauguration of the state chapter of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, established to mobilise grassroots support for Tinubu’s re-election.

President Tinubu is the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate in the election.

Tompolo, represented by the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited, Kestin Pondi, also donated 25 campaign vehicles equipped with loudspeakers, generators and amplifiers to facilitate the mobilisation campaign across the state.

He said the vehicles would be deployed to take the message of Tinubu’s administration to households, markets, churches and communities, urging residents to support the president for another four years.

He said although Nigerians were experiencing economic difficulties, the reforms introduced by Mr Tinubu were beginning to yield results, adding that the benefits would gradually extend to small businesses and ordinary citizens.

According to him, the president needs another four years to consolidate the foundation his administration has already laid.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Big businesses are already benefiting from the reforms. In no distant time, the benefits will get to small businesses,” he said.

Tompolo urged members of the movement to engage their neighbours, relatives and community members, explaining the administration’s policies and persuading them to vote for Mr Tinubu.

Also speaking, Mr Okpebholo said the 2.5 million-vote target was a commitment to Mr Tinubu, stressing that the state would work to deliver promised votes.

He described Tompolo as a great leader for establishing a grassroots political mobilisation platform, adding that the initiative would strengthen support for Tinubu’s continuity in office.

The governor called on party members and supporters to take the campaign to individual homes and communities to ensure that the target was achieved.

Earlier, the National Coordinator of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Sunday Asuku, said the initiative was established to mobilise Nigerians for Mr Tinubu’s re-election, insisting that the president deserved another four years to consolidate his reforms.

Mr Asuku argued that the administration had improved allocations to states and local governments, strengthened their financial capacity and enabled state governments to meet salary and pension obligations while executing development projects.

Also speaking, the Edo State APC Chairman, Jarrett Tenebe, said the state party leadership was committed to delivering the votes the President promised.

Mr Tenebe cited Mr Tinubu’s support for the emergence of a South-south son as senate president and other appointments given to people from the region as reasons for the zone to reciprocate through massive electoral support.

He expressed confidence that the inauguration of the movement would strengthen the party’s grassroots mobilisation and help Edo State achieve the 2.5 million votes target.
