World.title: Police arrest nine over alleged N8.6 million robbery in Ibadan
World.content:
The Oyo State Police Command has arrested nine suspects over an alleged robbery in Ibadan, during which valuables worth N8.62 million were reportedly stolen from a motorist and his friends.

The suspects were arrested following an attack on a Toyota Camry occupied by Oyewole Wisdom and his friends in the Agugu area of Ibadan on 18 November.

The Police Public Relations Officer, Ayanlade Olayinka, disclosed this in a statement on Friday.

According to the police, the incident occurred around 4 p.m. as Mr Wisdom drove his newly acquired, unregistered Toyota Camry around the Bus-Stop Gate area. A group of hoodlums reportedly chased the vehicle to the Adekile area, where they attacked its occupants and dispossessed them of their valuables.

“The stolen items include an iPhone 17 Pro Max, an iPhone Air, an iPhone 16 Plus, an 11-gram gold necklace, a 2.5-gram gold ring, two power banks and a Dell laptop, with a combined estimated value of N8,620,000. In addition to the robbery, the assailants inflicted extensive damage on the victim’s vehicle, valued at N10,000,000,” the statement said.

After receiving a report of the incident, operatives of the Agugu Police Division visited the scene and launched an investigation that led to the arrest of nine suspects.

They were identified as Olaitan Adegbite, Oladayo Mohammed, Moruf Mufutau, Toheeb Taofeek, Segun Olalere, Animashun Ibrahim, Gbolarinwa Tajudeen, Ridwan Omotosho and Ajala Opeyemi.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The police said preliminary investigations indicated that the suspects had confessed to their alleged involvement in the robbery and were providing useful information to investigators.

Items recovered from the suspects included an iPhone 16 Plus, two power banks, a vehicle bumper, a car charger and the vehicle key.

The command said the suspects and recovered exhibits would be transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Iyaganku, Ibadan, for further investigation.

The Commissioner of Police, Abimbola Ayodeji Olugbenga, urged residents to remain vigilant, provide credible information to security agencies and report suspicious activities.

He said the suspects would be charged in court after the investigation concluded.

World.title: Tinubu’s reforms make Nigerian passport processing easier – Oshiomhole
World.content:
Edo North Senator Adams Oshiomhole says Nigerians living in the country and abroad can now apply for, renew, and obtain international passports more easily because of reforms introduced by the Bola Tinubu administration.

Mr Oshiomhole, chairman of the Senate Committee on Interior, said there had been significant improvements in the passport application and collection processes, unlike in the past when citizens struggled to obtain the travel document.

He spoke on Friday at the groundbreaking ceremony for the National Passport Booklet Production Centre at the headquarters of the Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) in Abuja. The facility will be Nigeria’s first domestic passport booklet production centre.

Mr Oshiomhole, a former governor of Edo State, referenced the experience of his grandchildren, who, he said, had been unable to obtain Nigerian passports despite several attempts in previous years.

He said the reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration have made it possible for them to obtain the passports.

“They (grandchildren) tell me, ‘Grandpa, now I have a Nigerian passport.’ So these are not in the advert; they are real stories that speak to what is changing, the real meaning of Renewed Hope,” he said.

The senator also recalled how Nigerians in the diaspora had been stranded and unable to visit their families in the country because their passports had expired and they could not renew them.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He commended the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, for his foresight in making passport applications and renewals easier for Nigerians living abroad.

“Within months of the honourable minister’s assumption of office, these issues were dealt with satisfactorily.

“If a man couldn’t get a passport, even as a Nigerian who wants to come home as a patriot, he couldn’t. He was being frustrated by the incompetence of the Nigerian state. And now that Nigeria is celebrating, has renewed his hope in our country, the Renewed Hope Agenda, I believe, is what is being translated here and now,” he added.

Mr Oshiomhole said the new facility would make passport production easier, more affordable and more efficient for Nigerians.

For years, obtaining or renewing a Nigerian international passport has been a frustrating experience for many citizens, with applicants frequently complaining about processing delays, difficulty securing appointments, shortages of passport booklets, and alleged demands for unofficial payments by some immigration officials.

The challenges have also affected Nigerians living abroad, some of whom have complained about difficulties renewing expired passports or obtaining new ones at Nigerian diplomatic missions. For some, the delays have disrupted travel plans, prevented them from visiting family members in Nigeria and created difficulties with immigration and residency requirements in their countries of residence.

These challenges have repeatedly raised questions about the efficiency of the Nigeria Immigration Service, which administers passports and other immigration-related services.

In recent years, the federal government has announced reforms aimed at improving passport application, processing and collection. These include efforts to simplify application procedures, reduce processing delays, improve access to passport services and expand the country’s passport production capacity.

Establishing a domestic passport booklet production centre is expected to further address challenges in the supply of passport booklets by reducing Nigeria’s dependence on foreign production and increasing the availability of the travel document.

However, the effectiveness of these interventions will ultimately depend on whether applicants can obtain their passports promptly and without unnecessary bureaucratic hurdles, both in Nigeria and at diplomatic missions abroad.

READ ALSO: How Tinubu transformed NIS in three years Interior Minister

Nigeria targets six million passports annually

In his remarks, Mr Tunji-Ojo said the passport booklet production centre would enable Nigeria to increase its production capacity to six million booklets annually.

He added that the government planned to expand capacity further to 10 million booklets annually.

“The requirement of Nigeria is roughly between 1.8 million and two million passports a year, but by May we will have the capacity for six million passports a year, which we are going to scale to 10 million passports a year,” he said.

World.title: Lagos renews campaign against open defecation
World.content:
*Once upon a time: Open defecation in Bauchi

…Calls for improved sanitation, gender-sensitive toilet facilities

By Olasunkanmi Akoni

The Lagos State Government has renewed its campaign for improved sanitation, proper hygiene practices and access to safe toilet facilities as part of efforts to eliminate open defecation and promote public health.

The Special Adviser to the Governor on Environment, Olakunle Akodu, and the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources, Tajudeen Gaji, made the call on Friday as the state joined the rest of the world to commemorate World Toilet Day at Alausa, Ikeja.

The 2026 celebration was held under the theme, “Sanitation and Gender Equality.”

Akodu said women and girls required toilet facilities that guaranteed adequate privacy, reliable water supply, handwashing stations and hygienic conditions.

He noted that Lagos’ growing population, rapid urbanisation and expanding commercial activities had placed enormous pressure on existing sanitation infrastructure.

According to him, addressing the challenges requires deliberate public policies, sustained capital investment, institutional discipline and collective civic responsibility.

He said the state government recognised that a clean, resilient and sustainable environment must guarantee every resident access to safe, dignified and functional sanitation facilities.

Earlier, Gaji, who was represented by the Director of Sanitation Services, Hassan Sanuth, said the commemoration underscored the importance of proper sanitation in preventing diseases, protecting public health and promoting a cleaner environment.

He described access to safe toilets as more than a basic necessity, saying it was fundamental to human dignity and public health.

Gaji said sanitation was closely linked to personal security, social equality and the fundamental right of every citizen to live in a healthy environment.

He warned that inadequate access to safe and private toilet facilities could undermine people’s health, security, dignity, education and participation in economic and social activities.

The permanent secretary therefore called for inclusive policies and investments that would address the sanitation needs of women, girls, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups.

World.title: NUC approves medical university in Anambra, opens December 1
World.content:
…Tuition starts at N3m, says VC

By Vincent Ujumadu

The National Universities Commission (NUC) has approved the Transatlantic University of Medicine and Health Sciences, Umuchukwu, in Orumba South Local Government Area of Anambra State, with academic activities scheduled to commence on December 1, 2026.

The Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Charles Esimone, disclosed this while briefing journalists at the university, saying admissions began on October 1, while lectures were expected to commence on December 3.

Esimone said the NUC had formally communicated the university’s approval to the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB), which had subsequently issued the institution an identification code to enable prospective students to apply for admission.

He explained that candidates seeking to transfer to the university would be required to change their first-choice institution to Transatlantic University before accessing the platform for the post-UTME screening exercise.

“The students who transferred to our university will have to change their first choice to our university before they can access the platform for post-UTME. That process started in October.

“So we have started the admission process and verifying the students’ credentials before approving their admission letters. They will then get their admission numbers and pay the necessary fees before the commencement of lectures when we are sure the numbers are there. Orientation will then follow,” he said.

On tuition fees, the vice-chancellor described the university’s charges as affordable, despite the high cost of providing quality education.

He said students in programmes other than Medicine and Surgery would pay about N3 million annually, while those studying Medicine and Surgery would pay approximately N5.5 million.

Esimone explained that the university could not have commenced operations without securing the necessary NUC approval, adding that the commission had conducted physical inspections of its facilities, infrastructure, academic manpower and curriculum before granting the approval.

According to him, the NUC subsequently presented its findings to its board, which reviewed and approved the institution before recommending it to the Federal Executive Council for a provisional licence.

He said the provisional licence required the university to deposit N500 million as a financial guarantee to protect students and staff in the event of the institution’s failure to meet its obligations.

“If at any time the university fails to meet its obligations to them, they can petition the NUC and that money will be used to offset what they are owed,” he explained.

The vice-chancellor said the provisional licence was valid for three years, after which the institution’s operations would be reviewed.

He added that the university had successfully undergone resource verification and would invite the NUC for full accreditation after its first year of operation.

On the institution’s medical training facilities, Esimone said the founder planned to establish a teaching hospital to support clinical training and other medical programmes.

He disclosed that the teaching hospital was expected to take between two and three years to complete, while arrangements were already underway for the importation of medical equipment.

In the interim, he said the university had signed memoranda of understanding with some teaching hospitals to provide clinical training for its medical students.

Esimone also disclosed that some expatriate academics working with the university’s proprietor in the United States would periodically come to Nigeria to teach students.

He said the university would occupy the first to 11th floors of the building, while the proposed teaching hospital would occupy the 12th to 17th floors.

World.title: Waste crisis: LAWMA acting MD unveils 60-day action plan
World.content:
LAWMA

…Warns staff against laxity, promises operational overhaul

By Olasunkanmi Akoni

The newly appointed Acting Managing Director of the Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA), Olajuwon Akinyemi, has unveiled a 60-day emergency action plan to tackle waste management challenges across Lagos State, warning staff against indiscipline and poor performance.

Akinyemi, who has assumed office amid growing concerns over waste accumulation across the metropolis, said the plan was aimed at clearing waste backlogs, strengthening regulatory enforcement and restoring the agency’s operational efficiency.

He disclosed this on Friday while addressing management and staff at a workers’ forum held at LAWMA’s headquarters in Ijora-Olopa, Lagos.

Accompanied by the Acting Executive Director, Operations, Dr. Olorunwa Tijani, and the Executive Director, Finance, Kunle Adebiyi, the acting managing director called for renewed commitment, discipline and professionalism among workers.

He said repositioning the agency would require active participation and dedication from personnel at all levels.

“We are bringing in resilience and a new paradigm shift. It is a new wave in handling waste in Lagos.

“We already have the template to transform LAWMA positively. All we need to do is recreate, modernise and do better than in the past,” Akinyemi said.

Outlining the 60-day action plan, he said personnel would be redeployed across the state’s three operational districts based on their familiarity with the respective areas to strengthen field monitoring and improve response times.

He also announced plans to establish decentralised operational hubs to improve supervision, facilitate faster interventions and address waste disposal blackspots across the state.

On indiscriminate waste disposal, Akinyemi said the agency would intensify public enlightenment on waste sorting at source and responsible disposal practices.

He said traditional rulers, Community Development Association (CDA) leaders, market associations and artisans would be mobilised to promote compliance with proper waste management practices.

The acting managing director also called for stronger collaboration with Private Sector Participation (PSP) operators and urged residents to comply with approved waste collection tariffs to sustain service delivery.

On staff welfare, Akinyemi assured workers that their well-being remained a priority, disclosing that efforts were underway to procure Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)-powered buses to address transportation challenges.

Earlier, Tijani called for urgent action to revitalise LAWMA’s operational framework, saying the agency needed an immediate overhaul to improve field performance.

Similarly, Adebiyi said the success of the 60-day plan would depend on prudent financial management, accountability and effective collaboration across the agency’s directorates.

He urged workers to embrace professionalism and shared responsibility in implementing the proposed reforms.

Following the meeting, Akinyemi led members of the management team on an inspection tour of various departments at the headquarters to assess operations and identify immediate challenges requiring attention.

World.title: Anthropic sets IPO price at $83 per share, targets $1.5trn valuation
World.content:
–Claude maker raises $81.3bn in world’s largest IPO, overtakes SpaceX as investors rush for AI, despite $104bn loss

By Vera Anyagafu, with agency report

The artificial intelligence race just produced the biggest stock market debut in history.

Anthropic, the United States artificial intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot, on Wednesday priced its initial public offering at $83 per share, above its expected range of $70 to $78, valuing the company at about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

The company sold 980 million shares, up from the 825 million originally planned, raising $81.34 billion and surpassing SpaceX’s $75 billion record to become the world’s largest IPO at initial pricing.

The offering is expected to close on Friday, November 20, subject to customary closing conditions, as demand became extraordinary.

One early investor said the original sale was oversubscribed by roughly ten times.

And reports put demand at close to $500 billion worth of shares, far above the offering size.

That demand brushed aside market jitters over AI stocks, the recent slide on Wall Street, and even the spy scandal that toppled Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang.

Anthropic is now the first major United States company specialising purely in AI development to go public.

It is also the only public US company focused entirely on AI, and it did it in just five years.

Founded in 2021 by seven former OpenAI employees, including siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, Anthropic did not exist until about five years ago.

In May, it raised $65 billion in its last private round, at a valuation of $965 billion. Six months later, it is worth $1.5 trillion.

That puts it roughly on par with Tesla, more valuable than Walmart and Samsung, and more than the combined market capitalisation of India’s top 10 companies, according to Indian banker Uday Kotak.

“Anthropic, an AI company known for Claude, listed at a valuation of $1.5 trillion. It did not exist till ∼5 years ago. This is more than the combined market cap of the top 10 Indian companies. Are we undervalued, or do we need to catch up in the new world? Or both?” Kotak wrote on X on Thursday.

But the total money raised is even bigger than the IPO alone.

Seven technology companies, AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron Technology, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC Partners, have separately agreed to invest a combined $26 billion in Anthropic through a private placement at the IPO price.

Together, the IPO and the private placement are set to raise a record $107 billion, above the $86 billion SpaceX raised in its listing.

The company is going public to finance its long-term commitments, estimated at around $900 billion, related to computing power and data centres. About $70 billion of computing bills are due in the next year alone.

Anthropic reported revenue of $33.2 billion in the first nine months of 2026, about 13 times the same stretch a year earlier. In the third quarter alone, revenue was about $17 billion, more than 12 times the year-earlier level, it reveals.

But for the same nine months, it reported a net loss of $104 billion, according to its IPO document, underscoring the financial demands of AI development.

Anthropic has already reported its first quarterly operating profit, but its prospectus warns that its computing commitments could strain its finances if growth slows.

At $83, Anthropic is valued at about 43 times trailing sales on a fully diluted basis, less than half SpaceX’s multiple at its June debut, but still leaving little room for error.

Earlier estimates had put Anthropic’s valuation as high as $2 trillion, but they fell as AI stocks slid on Wall Street in recent weeks. The tech-heavy Nasdaq has lost 12 per cent since its peak in October.

Its biggest rival, OpenAI, maker of ChatGPT, is expected to go public next year.

For now, though, the message from Wall Street is clear, investors still believe the AI boom is real, and they are willing to pay a record price to be part of it.

Korea presents roadmap for Nigeria’s Unified, citizen-centred digital government

By Vera Anyagafu

South Korea, through the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA), has handed over the final report of Nigeria’s e-Government Master Plan 2.0 (e-GMP 2.0) to the Federal Government for formal adoption.

The handover took place on Thursday in Abuja at the closing ceremony of KOICA’s project, ‘Building Foundations Towards Digital Governance in Nigeria (2022–2026)’, where KOICA Country Director, Mr Kim Eunsub, , presented the report to the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy.

The e-GMP 2.0 provides the strategic and implementation framework for Nigeria’s digital government transformation from 2026 to 2030. It was developed from May 2022 through consultations with relevant Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs), with technical expertise from South Korea. The plan consolidates the 25 initiatives under the first e-Government Master Plan into 10 strategic initiatives organised under five pillars: Integrated Digital Infrastructure, Sustainable Digital Government, Citizen-Centric Digital Service Transformation, Digital Governance and Institutional Reform, and Innovation, Partnerships and Digital Capacity. Presenting the document, Prof. Hung Kook Park, Project Manager from Sangmyung University in South Korea, outlined its development process, key achievements, critical success factors and roadmap for implementation.

The government says the plan is meant to move Nigeria from disconnected digital platforms towards an integrated, citizen-centred system. It is expected to provide common direction and standards for digital transformation across government, and to transform how institutions operate, exchange information and deliver services. A key outcome of the partnership is the soft launch of Nigeria’s first single-window Government Service Portal (GSP) in July 2026. KOICA’s 2022 to 2026 project also delivered 572 NIN registration devices and trained 2,276 Nigerian officials, according to reports on the handover. The Federal Government acknowledged at the ceremony that Nigeria is yet to fully realise its digital governance ambition, making formal adoption and implementation of the 2.0 plan the next critical step.

World.title: Nwobodo urges ESUT to prioritise innovation, research, good governance
World.content:
By Alumona Ukwueze

ENUGU—-Former Governor of old Anambra State and former Minister of Sports, Chief (Dr.) Jim Ifeanyichukwu Nwobodo, has urged the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) to prioritise research, technological innovation, entrepreneurship and good governance to enhance its contribution to national development.

Nwobodo made the call while delivering the 3rd Distinguished Personality Lecture of ESUT during the university’s Special Convocation Ceremony at its permanent site at Ebe-ano City, Enugu State.

The lecture was titled, “From Vision to Legacy: Technology, Education, Leadership, Good Governance and the Responsibility of a New Generation.”

Nwobodo, who founded the Anambra State University of Science and Technology (ASUTECH) in 1980, said the establishment of the institution was a deliberate investment in the future, driven by the conviction that education, scientific knowledge, technological competence and visionary leadership were essential to societal progress.

He expressed satisfaction with the growth of the university, noting that the institution’s continued development more than four decades after its establishment demonstrated the enduring value of its founding vision.

According to him, the true measure of leadership goes beyond achievements recorded while in office to include the institutions established and the opportunities created for future generations.

Reflecting on his experience in public service, Nwobodo said governments and political office holders might come and go, but institutions founded on sound principles and sustained through responsible governance could endure for generations.

He stressed that visionary leadership required the courage to make difficult decisions and undertake initiatives whose benefits might extend beyond one’s tenure in public office.

On the future of ESUT, the former governor called for its transformation into a leading centre for research, innovation, entrepreneurship, technological development and practical solutions to societal challenges.

He said the university’s success should not be measured solely by student enrolment and graduation figures but also by the quality of its research, technological discoveries, entrepreneurial achievements and contributions to national development.

Nwobodo advocated increased investment in applied research, urging engineering students to develop solutions to energy and infrastructure challenges, agricultural scientists to improve food production, medical researchers to advance healthcare, and computer scientists to develop applications in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and digital technology.

He also called for stronger collaboration among students of management, law, economics and social sciences and their counterparts in science and engineering to translate research findings into commercially viable enterprises.

The former minister further urged the university to strengthen its partnerships with government, industries, investors, research institutions and alumni.

He specifically encouraged ESUT to establish or strengthen a dedicated centre for innovation and entrepreneurship where students, researchers and industry partners could transform promising ideas into products, businesses and practical solutions.

Nwobodo also underscored the importance of alumni participation in the university’s development, calling for stronger partnerships between the institution and its graduates through scholarships, research endowments, mentorship, industry partnerships, internships and support for entrepreneurship.

He said alumni who had distinguished themselves in business, industry, technology, academia and public service possessed valuable knowledge, professional networks and resources that could strengthen the university.

On technology and leadership, Nwobodo cautioned that technological competence must be accompanied by critical thinking, ethical judgment, responsible leadership and an understanding of society.

He noted that although artificial intelligence could process information at extraordinary speed, human beings must remain accountable for decisions made with its assistance.

“Technology determines what society is capable of doing. Leadership, values and governance determine how that capability is used,” he said.

He therefore urged universities to produce not only technologically competent graduates but also knowledgeable, innovative and ethical citizens capable of applying technology in the service of humanity.

Addressing the issue of good governance, Nwobodo said effective leadership required transparency, accountability, competence, fairness, respect for the rule of law and responsible management of public resources.

He maintained that public office was a position of trust that must be exercised in the public interest.

The former governor further stressed the need for continuity in institutional development, warning that when successive administrations abandoned the worthwhile initiatives of their predecessors, development became discontinuous and difficult to sustain.

He said institutions must be stronger than individuals and establish systems that preserve continuity, merit and accountability beyond changes in leadership.

Nwobodo noted that ASUTECH was established under an administration that eventually ended, but its educational vision endured because successive generations contributed to its development.

He urged the university community, particularly graduating students, to embrace leadership founded on integrity, responsibility, sound judgment and service to society.

The Governor of Enugu State, His Excellency, Dr. Peter Mbah praised Nwobodo’s vision and courage in leadership, especially for investing heavily in human capital development, taking the bold step to establish ESUT a few years after the civil war, not minding the enormity of the challenges involved.

“I have often wondered what it must have felt like to be governor in 1979. Nigeria had just returned to civilian government after thirteen years of military rule.

“The Civil War had ended less than a decade earlier, and the country was still dealing with its consequences. There was much to rebuild, and enormous pressure on the resources available to government.

“For many families, university education remained beyond their reach. And here was a young governor, who decided that his state should establish a university of science and technology.

“People questioned whether it could be done. Was there enough money? Could a state government sustain such an institution? Shouldn’t this be left to the federal government?,” the Governor said.

Earlier in his welcome address, the Vice Chancellor of ESUT, Professor Aloysius-Michaels Okolie, lauded the contribution of Senator Nwobodo, to the education sector, stating that “he dared to establish the first University of Technology in Nigeria.”

“Today, 46 years after, that seed had grown into a giant, producing thousands of scientists, engineers, doctors, managers and leaders serving Nigeria and humanity in various capacities. We are forever grateful, Sir.

“As the first civilian Executive Governor of old Anambra State (1979-1983), Senator Nwobodo broke all records of achievements and laid foundation of modern Anambra and Enugu States respectively. Your incredible footprints are still visible,” he said.

Equally, the Chairman of the Local Organizing Committee for the Lecture, Professor Okechukwu Oji, while welcoming guests at the event, stated that the Distinguished Personality Lecture Series was conceived by the University to bridge the gap between the town and gown and to address burning issues of public interest for the benefit of society.

He further stated that the Lecturer, Senator Nwobodo, given his wealth of knowledge and experience in leadership, politics and governance, as well as his God-given wisdom would do justice to the topic.

Honorary Doctorate Award for Leadership, Governance and Human Capital Development – Honoris Causa was conferred on Senator Nwobodo by ESUT during the lecture.

The lecture drew dignitaries including the Visitor to the University and Governor of Enugu State, Dr. Peter Mbah, ministers, commissioners and other critical stakeholders to ESUT.

World.title: 2027: Sowore faults NELFUND, promises non-repayable grants
World.content:
Omoyele Sowore

By Dickson Omobola

African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore, Friday, faulted the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), saying he will abolish the scheme if elected.

Sowore promised to introduce N100,000 grants per semester for students, saying the scheme would provide financial support without requiring repayment.

He made the promise during a live session on his Facebook page, adding that students should not be burdened with debt while pursuing their education.

He said, “The NELFUND that this government has put in place. First, our party is going to abolish NELFUND. We will turn it into grants.”

He added that the policy would replace the existing student loan arrangement.

He said, “We are going to give N100,000 per semester, which is N20,000 more than what they are getting now. For two semesters, you get N200,000 so that you can focus on your studies.”

Sowore argued that Nigeria should avoid introducing a system that could leave graduates struggling with debt, particularly in a country where employment opportunities were limited.

Citing his experience in the United States, where he said he spent 20 years, the AAC candidate described student loans as a source of financial hardship for many graduates.

He said, “The biggest cause of depression in America is student loans. Where are you going to get the employment to pay back the loans? But the truth is that even the loans they are giving to them now, they are not paying back. So it just makes sense to turn it into grants.”

Sowore said a student completing a four-year program would receive a total of N400,000 under the proposed arrangement, assuming two semesters per year.

He described the amount as a reasonable investment in young Nigerians who would contribute decades of service to the country.

The former presidential candidate also proposed scholarships for students with outstanding academic abilities, saying beneficiaries could be sponsored to study abroad.

“Grants for anybody, whether… scholarships for people who show exemplary ability. We give you a scholarship; we send you abroad,” he said.

He advocated increased government investment in education, citing China’s support for students studying abroad as an example of how countries could develop their education systems.

Sowore blamed the decline in Nigeria’s education sector for several of the country’s challenges, arguing that investment in schools was essential to reducing poverty and developing human capital.

He recalled that during his childhood, free education and community efforts to ensure school attendance made education a priority.

The activist also cited the University College Hospital, Ibadan, as an example of Nigeria’s former standing in the health sector, saying members of foreign royal families previously travelled to the country for medical treatment.

He contrasted this with the present situation, where many Nigerians struggle to afford medical treatment abroad.

Sowore further recalled that Indian and Ghanaian teachers worked in Nigerian secondary schools in the 1980s, arguing that the country’s education system had since declined.

He maintained that increased public investment in education was necessary to reverse the trend and improve opportunities for future generations.

“We already have the template to transform LAWMA positively. All we need to do is recreate, modernise and do better than in the past,” Akinyemi declared, signaling zero tolerance for operational inefficiencies.

​To back up his charge, Akinyemi rolled out a 60-day blueprint aimed at rapid waste evacuation, stricter regulatory enforcement, and aggressive field monitoring across Lagos State.

While giving key highlights of the emergency plan, the MD boss said personnel will be redeployed across the state’s three operational districts based on their familiarity with local terrains to sharpen field monitoring and speed up response times.

Hinting on decentralised operational hubs, Akinyemi added that the hubs will be established to decentralise waste management, tighten supervision, and bring rapid intervention closer to blackspots requiring urgent attention.

On ​indiscriminate dumping, he avowed the agency’s determination to intensify community sensitization on waste sorting at source, mobilizing traditional rulers, Community Development Association (CDA) leaders, market associations, and artisans to enforce responsible disposal habits.

Akinyemi, therefore, called for closer synergy with Private Sector Participation (PSP) operators and demanded stricter public compliance with approved waste collection tariffs to sustain operations.

​While reading the riot act on performance, the Acting MD also moved to boost morale, assuring workers that their welfare remains a top priority.

He revealed ongoing efforts to procure Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)-powered staff buses to cushion transportation challenges.

​Earlier, Tijani, reiterated the call for urgency, promising an immediate overhaul and revitalisation of LAWMA’s operational framework to boost field performance.

​Similarly, Adebiyi, warned that the success of the 60-day plan hinges on prudent financial management, strict accountability, and synergy across all directorates, urging staff to embrace professionalism and shared responsibility.

​Following the address, Akinyemi led the management team on an on-the-spot inspection tour of various departments at the headquarters to assess workflow and identify immediate operational bottlenecks.

World.title: Transmission lines restored after grid disturbance – NISO
World.content:
The Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) says it has restored all transmission lines that tripped during a grid disturbance on Friday.

The management of NISO said this in a statement in Abuja on Friday.

The ​‌‍‌​⁠‍⁠⁠‍‍⁠​⁠​​‌‍‌​system operator also said that the incident was not a system collapse.

It said that the disturbance resulted from the tripping of some transmission line, which caused load losses in parts of the country.

”NISO wishes to clarify that the grid disturbance experienced earlier today was not a system collapse.

“It resulted from the tripping of some transmission lines, which caused load losses in parts of the country.

”At 12:34 p.m., the Omotosho–Ikeja West transmission line tripped, resulting in a significant load drop within the Lagos Complex.

”Subsequently, at 12:50 p.m, the Ihovbor–Oshogbo transmission line tripped alongside the Benin–Egbin and Ihovbor–Ajaokuta transmission lines, resulting in load losses in some parts of the country,” it said.

The system operator said that prompt emergency response measures were activated by the relevant operational teams in coordination with TCN to stabilize the grid and restore affected transmission lines.

It said that all the affected lines had since been successfully restored to normal operation as of 2:49 p.m. on Friday.

It reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining grid stability, coordinating system operations, and ensuring the reliable and secure operation of the Nigerian electricity grid.

”The public is advised to rely on official communications from NISO for accurate information on developments within the national electricity grid,” it said. (NAN)

World.title: Union Bank’s Next Chapter: Building for Future of Banking
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Oluchi Chibuzor

At 109, Union Bank of Nigeria remains focused on the changing needs of its customers and the opportunities emerging within Nigeria’s financial services industry

With three million active customers and a network of 256 branches, the bank provides financial services to individuals, small and medium-sized enterprises, and corporate organisations across the country.

As banking habits evolve, customers increasingly expect convenient digital access, secure transactions, responsive service and financial solutions suited to their circumstances. Meeting these expectations requires sustained investment in technology, people and the systems that support everyday banking.

To meet these expectations, Union Bank has continued to strengthen its service channels and develop solutions that respond to evolving customer and business needs. This includes supporting Nigerian entrepreneurs beyond traditional banking services, creating opportunities for them to reach new customers, build business relationships and expand their markets.

In September 2026, the bank hosted an SME Sales Fair at its Lagos headquarters, Stallion Plaza, bringing together entrepreneurs across fashion, beauty, footwear, accessories and other sectors. The event offered participating businesses a platform to showcase their products, reach new customers and develop business relationships.

The initiative reflects the growing importance of combining financial services with practical business support, particularly for smaller enterprises seeking opportunities to expand.

Union Bank has also continued to invest in its workforce. In July 2026, the bank received two honours at the Euromoney Awards for Excellence, emerging as Nigeria’s Best Bank for Diversity and Inclusion and Africa’s Best Bank for Diversity and Inclusion.

The recognition highlighted workplace policies and employee support initiatives, including six months of fully paid maternity leave and CareCube, a childcare facility at its Lagos head office provided at no cost to employees.

These initiatives form part of the bank’s efforts to attract, develop and retain talent in an increasingly competitive financial services industry.

Union Bank’s priorities also reflect the need to respond to changes in how individuals and businesses manage their finances. Digital banking, customer service, business financing and employee development remain important areas through which financial institutions can improve their relevance and effectiveness.

With 109 years of banking experience, the institution’s focus is on meeting today’s expectations while developing the capabilities required for the future.

Beyond these initiatives, Union Bank’s transformation is becoming increasingly evident in the expansion of its digital banking capabilities and efforts to make financial services more accessible. Among its recent developments are the launch of a new Union360 platform and, more recently, a new omnichannel solution, both reflecting the Bank’s investment in improving how customers access and manage their banking services across different channels.

The bank has also introduced SmartOpen, an account-opening platform designed to simplify the process of becoming a customer. Alongside these developments, Union Bank has reactivated more than 70,000 dormant and inactive accounts in 2026, reconnecting customers with banking services. It has also recorded a significant increase in the number of digital loans booked, reflecting the growing role of technology in expanding access to credit and responding to customers’ financing needs.

For businesses, the Bank is strengthening its relationships across Nigeria’s evolving financial ecosystem. This includes onboarding new fintech accounts and expanding partnerships with anchor businesses to deepen its value-chain banking activities.

By developing stronger connections with businesses and the networks of suppliers, distributors and other enterprises that support them, Union Bank is positioning its services to address a broader range of commercial needs, including collections, trade and business financing.

Technology however, is only one part of the transformation. Union Bank has continued to invest in developing the skills and capabilities of its employees through training and professional development initiatives. These efforts are aimed at equipping employees to work with evolving technologies, respond to changing customer expectations and support the Bank’s operational priorities.

All together, these developments point to a transformation agenda extending across digital banking, customer acquisition, value-chain collections, trade, operational integration and workforce development. The emphasis is on combining the Bank’s longstanding experience and expanded institutional capabilities with investments that can improve service delivery, strengthen operational resilience and create more relevant solutions for customers.

For Union Bank, the next chapter is therefore not simply about introducing new platforms or expanding its range of services. It is about how effectively these investments translate into a banking experience that is simpler, more responsive and better suited to the needs of individuals and businesses. As Nigeria’s financial services industry continues to evolve, the Bank’s ability to combine its heritage with innovation, operational discipline and customer-focused solutions will be central to its future.

World.title: Fela Kuti: Afrobeat Revolutionary Who Conquered World’s Musical Stage
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Ferdinand Ekechukwu

From challenging military rule in Nigeria to influencing generations of musicians across the world, the late Afrobeat legend, Fela Anikulapo-Kuti, has earned another historic place in global music history with his posthumous induction into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame.

The recognition, which followed two unsuccessful nominations, makes Fela the first major African music figure to be honoured by the institution. The Afrobeat pioneer was inducted in the Early Influence category at a ceremony held on Saturday, November 14, 2026, at Los Angeles’ Peacock Theater, decades after his death in 1997.

The honour adds to a remarkable year of international recognition for the musician fondly called ‘Abami Eda’. In February 2026, the Recording Academy presented him with a Lifetime Achievement Award, making him the first African to receive the honour.

Fela’s journey to the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame was not without setbacks. His name first appeared among the 16 nominees announced for the 2021 class in the performers’ category, attracting considerable support in Nigeria. However, the 1,200 members of the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame did not include him in the final selection.

A second nomination in 2022 also ended without success. His eventual induction was announced last April in the Early Influence category, following a review by a special committee. The Cleveland-based institution surveyed more than 1,000 musicians, historians and industry members in selecting its 2026 inductees.

The category celebrates performers whose music and artistic styles influenced the evolution of rock and roll and helped shape popular culture. The Rock Hall recognised Fela as a revolutionary voice who blended jazz, West African music and soul to create Afrobeat, using his music to confront injustice and inspire political change.

Nearly three decades after his death, the institution said, “Fela Kuti’s innovative music, revolutionary message, and generational impact continue to represent the indomitable and evolving spirit of rock & roll.” It also described him as “a revolutionary voice that denounced injustice, provoking political change while fusing jazz, West African music, and soul.”

The moment was also a family celebration. A trending post showed his children and grandchildren, including Femi, Seun, Yeni, Shalewa and Made Kuti, at the ceremony, receiving the honour on his behalf. Speaking on the red carpet, members of the family described the induction as one of the greatest recognitions of Fela’s career and expressed excitement over another historic achievement.

Fela shared the Early Influence Award with Queen Latifah, MC Lyte, Celia Cruz and Gram Parsons. Sade, the British band led by Nigerian-born singer Sade Adu, was inducted in the Performer category alongside Oasis, Phil Collins, Billy Idol, Iron Maiden, Joy Division/New Order, Luther Vandross and Wu-Tang Clan.

Born in 1938, Fela created Afrobeat by bringing together highlife, jazz, funk, traditional African rhythms and politically charged lyrics. His music confronted military rule, corruption, colonial influence and social inequality, earning him international acclaim as well as repeated confrontations with successive Nigerian governments.

His musical vision took shape during a 1967 stay in Ghana, where he studied with Hugh Masekela and developed a fusion of highlife and other West African styles, jazz, funk, soul and rock. During a 1969 tour of the United States, his exposure to the Black Power movement, particularly through Black Panther Party member Izsadore (née Sandra Smith), further influenced his artistic direction.

World.title: Davido, Wizkid, Asake, Others Earn 2027 Grammy Nominations
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Ferdinand Ekechukwu

African music will once again take the spotlight at the Grammyss as Nigerian superstars Asake, Burna Boy, Tems, Wizkid earned nominations for the 2027 edition. The Recording Academy unveiled the nominations, with Nigerian artistes securing multiple recognitions across the Best African Music Performance, Best Global Music and other categories.

Tems emerged as Nigeria’s leading nominee with four nominations, while Asake secured two nominations in the Best African Music Performance category. Other Nigerian artistes aiming for the gramophone include Davido, Ayra Starr, Burna Boy and Wizkid, who shares nomination with Asake.

Also in the Best African Music Performance category, Nigerian artistes account for four of the five nominated entries, underscoring the country’s growing influence on the international music scene. Asake earned nominations for his songs ‘Gratitude’ and ‘Jogodo’, his collaboration with Wizkid.

Tems received a nomination for ‘Big Daddy’, while Ayra Starr earned recognition alongside Beninese music legend Angélique Kidjo for their collaboration, ‘Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?)’. The fifth nominee is Ghanaian musician King Ayisoba, whose song ‘No Tradition, No Africa’ features Rocky Dawuni.

Beyond the African music category, Tems secured three additional nominations. She was recognised in the Best R&B Solo Performance and Best R&B Song categories for ‘What You Need’, as well as the Best Global Music Album category for her 2026 EP, Love Is a Kingdom.

This marks her second nomination in this category after her album ‘Born In The Wild’ was nominated in 2025. It also marks her 12th nomination, making her the second most nominated Nigerian artist in the award’s history, only behind Burna Boy, who has secured 14 nods.

Ayra Starr also earned another nomination in the Best Global Music Album category for Starrgirl, while Davido’s Oriadé 6th album, released July 2026, earned nomination in the same category. Davido earns his second nomination in the category and his his 6th nomination.

Burna Boy secured a nomination in the Best Global Music Performance category for ‘Dìá Dìá’, his collaboration with Colombian superstar Shakira. The song was released in May 2026 as the unofficial anthem for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, jointly hosted by the United States, Mexico, and Canada.

World.title: Medical Tourism Africa Enters New Era with Lifestyle Thryvv Wellness App
