World.title: Coalition air defenses intercept 3 Houthi ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh
World.content:
RIYADH: Saudi air defenses intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles launched by Yemen’s Houthi militia toward Riyadh early Saturday, the Saudi-led Coalition to Support Legitimacy in Yemen said, as the Kingdom faced a renewed wave of missile and drone attacks.

Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki announced the interceptions on X shortly after 2 a.m., following a Civil Defense alert issued at 1:53 a.m. warning Riyadh residents of an “aerial threat.”

Two explosions were heard in the capital, witnesses said, after which Civil Defense lifted the alert, saying the danger had passed.

The Houthis said on X they were striking targets across Saudi Arabia, including Riyadh.

Civil Defense also issued early-warning alerts in Al-Sulayyil governorate, south of Riyadh, and in Najran, near the Kingdom’s border with Yemen.

The latest attack followed two ballistic missiles launched toward the Jazan region on Friday evening that were intercepted and destroyed by Saudi air defenses, according to the coalition. Debris fell in the Al-Shuqaiq area, prompting authorities to head to the site.

Civil Defense warnings were also issued in Jazan region and Khamis Mushayt in the Asir region as attacks continued across the Kingdom.

Earlier Friday, Al-Maliki said the coalition had targeted one of the Houthi militia’s main supply depots in Sanaa.

Saudi air defenses had intercepted five drones and three ballistic missiles on Friday, including the two missiles aimed at Jazan, according to a previous coalition announcement. Four drones and another ballistic missile were intercepted over the Kingdom’s southern region, while a drone was shot down over the Riyadh region.

The attacks came a day after a Houthi strike damaged several floors of a tower in Riyadh’s King Abdullah Financial District and neighboring buildings. No injuries were reported, Saudi Civil Defense said.

The Kingdom condemned the targeting of civilian and economic facilities, with its Foreign Ministry warning that Houthi attacks threaten regional and international security and reaffirming Saudi Arabia’s right to take necessary measures to defend its sovereignty and protect its citizens, residents and national assets.

The Saudi-led coalition, which backs Yemen’s internationally recognized government against the Houthis, said it was conducting operations against Houthi targets and missile capabilities in Sanaa, Saada and Taiz, as well as facilities at the Red Sea port of Hodeidah.

The coalition said the operations aimed to neutralize threats to civilians in Yemen and Saudi Arabia.

The Houthis resumed attacks against government forces in Yemen and civilian targets in Saudi Arabia earlier this year, breaking a four-year truce in the conflict.

World.title: Federal jury convicts man of starting the deadly 2025 Palisades Fire in Los Angeles
World.content:
LOS ANGELES: The man accused of sparking last year’s deadly Palisades Fire was found guilty of arson charges Friday after his first federal case earlier this year ended in a mistrial.

Jurors convicted Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, of lighting a fire on Jan. 1, 2025, that burned undetected deep in root systems before flaring back up Jan. 7, becoming one of the most destructive wildfires in California history. The Palisades Fire killed 12 people as it incinerated entire neighborhoods in Los Angeles and Malibu.

Rinderknecht pleaded not guilty to federal charges of destruction of property by means of fire and arson. The scope of the first charge was narrowed to only include the Jan. 1 blaze, known as the Lachman Fire, and the second addresses the Palisades Fire. He was convicted on both charges.

With little apparent reaction, Rinderknecht gave his attorneys hugs before leaving the courtroom.

Rinderknecht’s attorney Steve Haney said in a statement they were disappointed in the verdict but respected the jury process.

“After a lengthy deliberation, they clearly gave this case a great deal of consideration,” Haney said. Regarding an appeal, he said they would review all the options at the right time.

Rinderknecht’s is set to be sentenced March 17, 2027. Each count carries a mandatory minimum of five years and a maximum of 20 years in federal prison.

Prosecutors continued to pursue the case after Rinderknecht’s first jury deadlocked 10 to 2 in favor of acquittal after a two-week trial in June. They dropped a third charge of timber set afire when they filed a new indictment for the retrial.

Juror says Rinderknecht’s own testimony pointed to a guilty verdict

Juror No. 3, who only wanted to be identified by his first name Cameron, said he was the only person who felt Rinderknecht was not guilty at the start of deliberations. Another person was undecided, and the rest of the 10 jurors believed Rinderknecht was guilty.

“It took a lot for me to be convinced otherwise,” he said. “After listening to every single point, I do now agree that he’s guilty.”

Cameron said he initially had concerns about a technical review conducted by a defense expert witness, who argued the government had gotten the origin area of the fire wrong. He said there was a “lack of information” presented to the jury about the technical review.

In the end, it was Rinderknecht’s own testimony that was the strongest piece of evidence pointing to a guilty verdict, he said.

“Stating that he was up on the hill, didn’t smell a fire, didn’t see fireworks … no one else was on the hill that night,” Cameron said.

Prosecutors say Rinderknecht had been ‘mad at everything’

During the second trial, prosecutors presented a more tightly organized case that presented digital forensic data, expert testimony and Rinderknecht’s state of mind in the hours leading up to the fire. They did not focus as much on his resentment toward the rich and powerful to present the crime as arson motivated by “societal revenge” like they previously did.

Prosecutors zeroed in on evidence placing him at the fire’s origin area, such as photographs that showed his car parked at the base of a trail leading up to where the fire started and cellphone tower data pointing to his movement on the hill. Fire detection camera images showed the time window the blaze ignited, and experts eliminated any other source of ignition that night, including fireworks.

They established that Rinderknecht was acting erratic and angry in the hours leading up to the fire through the testimony of Uber passengers and texts sent to his girlfriend at the time.

“He was mad at everything, and frustrated,” said Assistant US Attorney Mark Williams.

After the fire began, Rinderknecht called 911 more than a dozen times as he walked down the hill. Prosecutors presented the video he screen-recorded on his phone while calling. As he was calling, he asked ChatGPT: “Are you at fault if a fire is lit because of your cigarettes?”

These were part of an alibi Rinderknecht was trying to create for himself, prosecutors said.

They also presented extensive testimony on how fire investigators determined the Palisades Fire was a holdover fire from the initial blaze Rinderknecht sparked.

Defense argues fire’s origin is unproven

Haney cast doubt on the government’s case, saying the fire scene could have been compromised because the area was publicly accessible until the Palisades Fire started Jan. 7.

The defense called their own expert witnesses, including a retired fire investigator for the US Forest Service who argued the fire origin area was different from what the government concluded.

Haney argued the government could not conclusively say there was no one else by the fire ignition point that night because of missing cell data records, and pointed to a neighbor’s testimony that he saw a group of teenagers running away from the direction of the trailhead.

He told jurors to disregard any evidence related to Rinderknecht’s character, such as his angry text messages, because they were “evidence of the man, not evidence of the act.”

Finally, Haney presented an alternate explanation for what ignited the fire — fireworks. Multiple witnesses, including two neighbors and a local firefighter, all said they heard a loud bang or explosion from the direction of the hill the fire purportedly started on.

In the thousands of images of the evening collected from cameras in the area, none showed fireworks in the sky above the hill where the fire started, prosecutors said.

World.title: More than 23,000 Syrian children killed by Assad regime since 2011: Syrian rights group
World.content:
DAMASCUS: Grave violations committed against Syrian children during the years of the revolution by the ousted regime’s forces and security agencies, including extrajudicial killings, arbitrary detention, enforced disappearance, and attacks on schools and medical facilities, have left deep humanitarian and legal consequences that require truth, accountability, and comprehensive reparations, human rights and legal experts said.

Marking World Children’s Day on Nov. 20, experts stressed the importance of protecting children’s rights in conflict zones, addressing the legacy of systematic abuses suffered by Syrian children, and guaranteeing their rights to life, safety, education, healthcare, and legal identity in line with international conventions.

More than 23,000 children killed, 3,736 disappeared

Speaking to SANA, Syrian Network for Human Rights (SNHR) Executive Director Fadel Abdul Ghany said Syrian children were among the civilian groups most heavily affected by systematic violations committed by the ousted regime since March 2011. He stressed the need to move from documentation to independent criminal investigations and victim compensation.

Abdul Ghany said SNHR has documented the extrajudicial killing of 23,146 children by the ousted regime’s forces, in addition to 222 children who died under torture in detention centers, noting that these figures represent the minimum number of verified cases.

According to updated figures released by SNHR on Friday, the ousted regime’s security agencies arrested and forcibly disappeared 3,736 children who remain unaccounted for. Abdul Ghany noted that enforced disappearance remains an ongoing crime as long as the fate or whereabouts of the victims are unknown, prolonging the suffering of their families.

The network also documented about 1,287 attacks on schools and kindergartens and at least 566 attacks on medical facilities since March 2011.

“These attacks destroyed hundreds of educational and healthcare institutions and deprived an entire generation of safe education and medical care,” Abdul Ghany said.

Legal identity challenges

Abdul Ghany said SNHR documented cases in which children were transferred by regime institutions to state care facilities without proper legal procedures, underscoring the need for independent investigations to establish their identities and reconnect them with relatives.

He added that the disappearance of parents and loss of civil records have created significant challenges in proving lineage and registering births. While the loss of documents does not automatically result in statelessness, it creates serious obstacles to accessing basic rights.

Abdul Ghany stressed that human rights databases built on testimonies, documents, and visual evidence are vital not only for documenting violations but also for identifying perpetrators and reconstructing crimes. Their value has increased with access to seized security, military, judicial, and civil archives of the former regime, which may help uncover the fate of missing children and identify those responsible for their detention.

He said priority should be given to safeguarding these archives, facilitating access to detention records, and strengthening cooperation among Syrian judicial authorities, the International, Impartial and Independent Mechanism (IIIM), and human rights organizations. Such efforts, he added, should support comprehensive reparation programs that include physical and psychological rehabilitation, restoration of civil documents, educational reintegration, and financial compensation.

War crimes and accountability

For her part, Rihada Abdoush, a member of the Freedoms and Human Rights Committee at the Central Bar Association, said the systematic violations committed against Syrian children amount to serious breaches of international human rights and humanitarian law and may constitute war crimes and crimes against humanity.

She emphasized that such crimes are not subject to statutes of limitations under international law and require parallel accountability efforts through Syrian courts and international legal mechanisms.

“These practices violate the 1989 Convention on the Rights of the Child and its Optional Protocols, as well as the four Geneva Conventions of 1949, which provide special protection for children and prohibit attacks on civilian sites, particularly schools,” Abdoush said.

She added that enforced disappearance is legally considered a continuing crime whose limitation period does not begin until the victim’s fate is established.

Abdoush noted that Syrian legislation also criminalizes such offenses, including Child Rights Law No. 21 of 2021, which prohibits the recruitment of children in armed conflict and obliges authorities to protect children from trafficking and treat trafficked children as victims in need of rehabilitation.

She added that the Syrian Penal Code, Legislative Decree No. 3 of 2010 on Combating Human Trafficking, and Law No. 30 of 2003 on Organ Transplantation impose severe penalties on those involved in trafficking children or human organs.

According to Abdoush, legal responsibility extends beyond individuals to associations, organizations, orphanages, and care institutions that failed to meet their legal and ethical obligations. She said prosecutions before Syrian courts, complemented by cases pursued abroad under universal jurisdiction, can help establish both individual and command responsibility using official archives as key evidence.

Abdoush called for aligning national legislation with international standards and adopting urgent legal and administrative measures to cancel records that erased children’s identities or deprived them of lineage and official documentation, thereby safeguarding victims’ rights to truth, justice, and reparation.

Observed annually on Nov. 20 since its establishment in 1954 and supported by UNICEF, World Children’s Day promotes international solidarity, raises awareness of children’s rights, and advances child welfare worldwide.

World.title: UNIFIL records 2,840 Israeli artillery shells, 90 airstrikes in southern Lebanon in October alone
World.content:
BEIRUT: The United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) said Friday that Israeli violations continued across southern Lebanon in October, including airstrikes and artillery shelling targeting several towns and villages.

According to UN News, UNIFIL said in a statement that its peacekeepers recorded 2,840 Israeli artillery shells fired, 870 airspace violations and 90 airstrikes during October, in violation of UN Security Council Resolution 1701.

The mission also reported the continued presence of Israeli occupation forces in parts of southern Lebanon, noting that extensive damage to homes and civilian infrastructure was preventing displaced residents from returning to their communities.

Children and schools affected by continuing violence

UNIFIL highlighted the humanitarian and psychological impact of the ongoing tensions, particularly on children, saying schools within its area of operations continued to function under difficult security conditions.

UNIFIL spokesperson Candice Ardell said that during a visit to a public intermediate school in the town of Tibnin for an explosive ordnance risk-awareness session, she heard drones overhead and explosions in the distance.

Ardell quoted the school's principal as saying that children became frightened and trembled whenever they heard warplanes, prompting teachers to comfort them through clapping and singing to help ease their fear and anxiety.

UNIFIL to continue operations until mandate expires

UNIFIL reaffirmed that its peacekeepers would continue carrying out their duties despite challenges on the ground.

The mission said its priorities during the remaining weeks of its mandate include monitoring developments and reporting impartially, maintaining communication and coordination with relevant parties to help reduce tensions, and supporting the Lebanese Armed Forces in extending state authority across southern Lebanon.

"Our mandate remains in place, and our peacekeepers will continue fulfilling their duties to the fullest until the final day," Ardell said.

UNIFIL has been deployed in southern Lebanon since 1978 and currently comprises approximately 7,500 personnel from nearly 50 countries.

In August 2025, the UN Security Council adopted Resolution 2790, extending UNIFIL's mandate for the final time until the end of 2026.

Under the resolution, the mission is scheduled to begin withdrawing on Jan. 1, 2027, with the withdrawal process continuing throughout the year.

World.title: American woman freed after 10 years in Cuba
World.content:
WASHINGTON: The US State Department said Friday that Cuban authorities have released a US citizen who was held in Cuba for nearly 10 years.

CNN reported Friday that Alina Lopez was freed earlier this year, and that American officials chartered a plane to Havana to return her to the United States.

“We welcomed Alina Lopez’s return to the United States in September,” a State Department spokesperson told AFP, stressing there was “no exchange” for the release and declining to offer further details to respect her privacy.

The release came amid Washington’s increased pressure on the communist island, which has been under a US embargo since 1962, through sanctions and an oil blockade.

The James Foley Foundation, which works to secure the return of Americans “wrongfully detained” abroad, said Lopez is an educator who returned to Cuba at her ex-husband’s urging in 2017 and was sentenced to 13 years in prison on espionage charges.

“Alina has urgent medical needs that are worsening without the treatment she requires in the United States,” the foundation said on its website.

Under international pressure from the United Nations and protests, Cuba had released Lopez from prison in 2022 and barred her from leaving Cuba. But she was imprisoned again in 2023.

World.title: Gulf alternatives may save Excelerate Energy’s LNG project in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Iraq is witnessing rapid on-site progress amid efforts to overcome geopolitical challenges and navigation risks associated with the Strait of Hormuz.

According to project updates, the field team and the materials required for constructing the marine jetty and terminal infrastructure have arrived in Iraq, Attaqa News reported.

US-based Excelerate Energy, which is carrying out the project, expects the pace of work to accelerate over the coming weeks, with construction activities progressing at the marine terminal and the facility’s infrastructure.

The firm aims to complete and commission the project during the second quarter of 2027, following a delay in 2026 caused by the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

Once Iraq begins imports, it will become the sixth Arab nation in history to import LNG—joining Kuwait, Egypt, the UAE, Jordan, and Bahrain.

The consequences of the Iranian conflict have caused delays for Iraq’s LNG project, which had originally planned to open in the third quarter of 2026. As a result, Excelerate Energy has moved the Excelerate Acadia, its floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU), to Jordan for nine months.

To overcome disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the company plans to utilize an FSRU already stationed within the region, eliminating the need to traverse the strategic waterway.

The company is likely to utilize the FSRU currently stationed in the UAE, known as Express.

The US firm indicated that it is working to arrange the import of LNG from countries within the Gulf region, a statement that strongly suggests Qatar or the UAE.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate rises in Iraq’s parallel market
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar experienced a slight increase on Thursday in both Baghdad, the Iraqi capital, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,706.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,706 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,710 Iraqi dinars and 1,700 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also increased, fluctuating between 1,709.5 and 1,708.5 Iraqi dinars.

US dollar exchange rates rose noticeably in the Baghdad and Erbil markets on October 7, following the cabinet’s decision to revalue the official rate of the local currency, causing turbulence and instability in the parallel market.

Iraq officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

Following the announcement, parallel market rates in Baghdad and Erbil soared, with exchange shops reporting market gains of more than 1,700 Iraqi dinars per US dollar.

World.title: Iraqi PM orders reopening of closed roads in Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Ali al-Zaidi, ordered on Thursday to expedite the reopening of all closed roads in the Jurf al-Sakhar district in the central province of Babil.

During his meeting with security officials, al-Zaidi emphasized that the army and security forces would uphold the authority of the state across all Iraqi territory, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister emphasized that the enforcement of state authority would be carried out in accordance with the constitution and the law. He affirmed the government’s commitment to protecting the lives and interests of citizens across the country and to preventing any violations or assaults on public and private properties.

According to al-Zaidi, the security forces operate as a unified entity, with their numerous branches and units cooperating with one another.

These directives come ahead of the deadline set by the government for Kataib Hezbollah, an Iran-backed militant faction, to withdraw from Jurf al-Sakhar—a deadline expiring on Friday—paving the way for security forces to enter and redeploy in the area.

The deadline for the withdrawal from Jurf al-Sakhar, also known as Jurf al-Nasr, follows an investigation by a government committee, which Baghdad stated uncovered evidence of oil smuggling operations in the area.

The armed faction rejected the smuggling allegations, claiming the sites inspected by investigators were abandoned facilities or fuel tanks for military vehicles.

World.title: Iraq’s trade exchange with China drops to $19.8 billion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Chinese Ambassador to Iraq, Xiang Bo, said on Thursday that the decline in trade exchange with Iraq—which fell to $19.8 billion—is due to the escalating security tensions in the region.

During a press conference in Baghdad, Bo projected that trade between the two countries would recover, reaching $26 billion by the end of 2026 or early 2027.

According to Bo, China is a trusted partner to Iraq. He noted that the two countries share deep historical and cultural ties, dating back thousands of years.

Bo emphasized that bilateral relations have seen significant development, with Iraq serving as a key trade partner. Trade volume between the two countries reached $51 billion in 2025, reflecting the strength of their mutual commitments and relationship.

Bo mentioned earlier that major Chinese firms are involved in the construction and development of several industries in Iraq, such as oil, energy, and infrastructure.

The Chinese diplomat expressed his hope that this collaboration will continue and grow into other sectors, contributing to the development of a complete partnership between Iraq and China.

Chinese companies have been heavily involved in the oil industry and in significant infrastructure projects, such as the construction of major bridges and schools, with more than 600 schools completed in several Iraqi provinces.

World.title: Iraq studies issuing electronic dinar to expand financial inclusion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is investigating an electronic dinar as a digital extension of the current national currency to modernize payments, increase financial inclusion, and lessen reliance on physical cash.

Prime Minister’s financial adviser Mazhar Mohammed Saleh highlighted the initiative in remarks to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) on Wednesday, though no launch date, technical specifications, or formal issuance decision have been announced.

The electronic dinar will serve as a digital representation equal in value to the physical paper dinar rather than a new currency issue. It will not automatically generate new liquidity but will improve the management and circulation of existing funds.

According to the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI), approximately 102 trillion dinars ($67.38 billion)—nearly 92 percent of all currency issued—is held outside the formal banking system.

The purpose of a digital currency is to direct the financial reserves into formal savings, lending, and profitable ventures.

Moving transactions onto official digital channels will help curb unregulated financial dealings, reduce cash-printing costs, and align Iraq with the CBI’s financial inclusion strategy.

The digital dinar plan is different from suggestions to eliminate zeros from the physical currency.

Although the CBI has expanded bank cards, digital wallets, and points of sale, it has not yet declared a formal launch date or technical introduction timetable.

World.title: Egypt expresses interest in Iraq’s Development Road project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Egyptian officials have renewed their push for national firms to participate in Iraq’s Development Road project and broader infrastructure initiatives.

Egyptian Minister of Transport Kamel el-Wazir said that Egyptian companies are ready to join the Development Road and railway projects with competitive pricing, quality standards, and fast delivery.

El-Wazir’s remarks took place during his meeting with the Iraqi Ambassador to Egypt, Qahtan Taha Khalaf, in Cairo, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

Egypt’s Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs, Hussein Issa, also met with Khalaf to discuss expanding trade, investment, and Egyptian company involvement in Iraqi development and reconstruction projects.

During a regional transport summit held two weeks ago in Alexandria, Egypt, Iraqi Transport Minister Wahab al-Hassani said that Iraq is moving toward the early implementation of land transport agreements with Jordan and Egypt to boost regional trade and cross-border movement.

Al-Hassani confirmed that Baghdad has finalized several land transport agreements with Amman and Cairo that are expected to enter into force soon.

The deals build upon a previously signed memorandum of understanding between the Iraqi and Egyptian transport ministries covering the overland movement of both passengers and goods.

Alongside the deals with Jordan and Egypt, al-Hassani highlighted Iraq’s broader push to establish itself as a regional transit hub through the country’s strategic project of the Development Road.

The strategic corridor spans 1,200 kilometers from the al-Faw Grand Port in the southern province of Basra to the Turkish border, combining new highway and railway networks.

World.title: Baghdad replaces forces holding Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered on Wednesday the replacement of the forces holding Jurf Al-Sakher, following an investigation into alleged oil smuggling.

The move seeks to end the 12-year control of the strategic Babil province area by the Iran-backed armed faction Kataib Hezbollah.

Iraq’s Supreme Committee for Security Sector Reform, chaired by Al-Zaidi in his capacity as Commander-in-Chief, ordered the replacement of the current force stationed in Jurf al-Sakhar with joint units from the Iraqi army, federal police, and other Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) brigades.

The Energy Police, an Interior Ministry force, was officially assigned to secure the three branches of the strategic Basra-Haditha oil pipeline running through the area.

Findings from a government investigative committee alleging oil theft and pipeline tampering were referred to the judiciary for legal action.

Before Wednesday’s deployment order, al-Zaidi dismissed nine senior security, intelligence, and oil ministry officials—including the director of the Oil Pipelines Company—in connection with the smuggling investigation.

The orders follow escalating tensions between Baghdad and Kataib Hezbollah, which has controlled the area south of Baghdad since recapturing it from ISIS in 2014.

The armed faction rejected the smuggling allegations, claiming the sites inspected by investigators were abandoned facilities or fuel tanks for military vehicles.

World.title: Najaf refinery expansion to raise Iraq’s refining capacity by 70,000 bpd
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s oil refining capacity is set to increase further as the expansion project at the Najaf refinery progresses.

The project aims to add 70,000 barrels per day to the country’s refining output, aligning with Baghdad’s broader plans to boost the production of petroleum products and reduce reliance on imports.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi visited the refinery expansion site on Tuesday to evaluate the progress made and to assess the technical and logistical challenges encountered during the project’s implementation.

The project is being carried out amid Iraqi efforts to improve the efficiency of its refining sector and increase its capacity to meet the domestic market’s fuel needs.

The expansion of the Najaf refinery will increase fuel production to meet the requirements of surrounding industrial projects, create new job opportunities, and boost economic activity within the province.

The Najaf refinery expansion project includes the construction of a new refining unit with a capacity of 70,000 barrels per day. This development encompasses the completion of essential facilities and services needed to support its operation.

The project includes the development of energy infrastructure, an industrial water treatment unit, oil storage tanks, and other facilities associated with the refining unit.

The refinery’s current processing capacity stands at 30,000 barrels per day. With the addition of 70,000 barrels per day from the new unit, the expansion plans aim to increase the total capacity to 100,000 barrels per day.

World.title: PM Modi & Nepal's Balen to review full range of bilateral ties
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India officially announced Friday Nepal PM Balendra Shah's state visit to India on Nov 22-23, saying it reflected the importance India attached to its relations with Nepal under its Neighbourhood First policy.

Balen's first visit to India after assuming office in March 2026 will see him holding talks with PM Narendra Modi Monday and also calling on President Droupadi Murmu.

According to the ministry of external affairs, Modi and Balen will review the full range of India-Nepal relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest. The visit comes on the back of the goodwill created by India's relief and rescue assistance to Nepal after floods this year.



"India and Nepal share close and friendly relations, rooted in historical, cultural and civilisational links and strong people-to-people ties. Bilateral cooperation has witnessed progress across diverse sectors, including trade and commerce, development partnership, energy and water resources, and physical and digital connectivity, with growing engagement in newer areas such as start-ups, technology and innovation, and sports," said the MEA.





Many MoUs are expected to be signed during the visit, including in areas like health, sports, education and disaster management.

While India has not confirmed the likely takeaways, Nepal media has reported in the past few weeks, quoting local govt sources, that the two sides are finalising a 10-point joint visit statement to strengthen ties and that progress is expected on a $2 billion economic package that Kathmandu is seeking from India.

"The leadership of both countries will hold discussions on enhancing economic cooperation in areas such as trade, transit, investment, energy, connectivity and infrastructure development," said Nepal's foreign secretary, Amrit Bahadur Rai.

External affairs minister S Jaishankar will call on Balen Sunday, shortly after the latter's arrival. The Nepal PM is also expected to raise the boundary issue in his engagements, underlining the need to address the differences.

World.title: Jawan hit by own gun, friendly fire during op to get war pension: SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: It is not necessary for Army personnel to be hit by an enemy's bullet in order to be entitled to pension under War Injury Element,

ruled Friday, ordering that pension be granted even in a case where a soldier is injured in accidental firing from his own gun or his own troops during an operation.

A bench of Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N K Singh said that the order specifically mentioned that Army personnel would be classified as 'Wounded Battle Casualty' in such cases and the grievously injured soldier would be entitled to the pension.

The court said the Army order contemplated two situations: a gunshot or splinter injury suffered 'accidentally', or such an injury caused by firing by own troops. "In either situation, the injury must have been sustained while carrying out operations against the enemy or militants.



The present case rests on the first limb, 'sustained accidentally'," SC said.

"A service weapon may discharge without an intention to cause bodily injury to himself, for example, while holding a weapon, an impact or fall, snagging of the trigger, inadvertent pressure on the trigger, or a mechanical defect... These nature of incidents are clearly distinguishable from the idea of self-inflicted injury, which has a certain element of knowledge or intention so as to disqualify from getting enhanced pensionary benefit," the bench said.

SC allowed the plea of Subedar Major and Honorary Lieutenant Devi Singh who got injured in Aug 2002 during Operation Rakshak/Operation Parakram in J&K when his weapon accidentally discharged a bullet that passed through his thigh and damaged the femoral vein. It made him 40% disabled and he was granted an ordinary Disability Element of pension. He sought an enhanced pension under War Injury Element. SC quashed the order of Armed Forces Tribunal, which had rejected his claim.

World.title: Indian Team leaves for Bangladesh for talks on Ganga water
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A four-member team from India headed to Bangladesh Friday to attend a meeting of the joint committee constituted under Ganga Water Treaty between the two countries to monitor the sharing of the river's waters.

The meeting is scheduled for Nov 21-23.

The visit comes weeks before the 30-year-old treaty is due to lapse on Dec 12, even as the team, led by head of India's Joint Rivers Commission Sharad Chandra, visiting Dhaka doesn't have the mandate to discuss the agreement's extension beyond its existing term.

Sources hinted that it is for the political leadership of both nations to take a call on its renewal or interim extension and its terms, whatever the case may be. Bangladesh has said instead of renewing the existing one, it wants to negotiate a new treaty with India, including a clause guaranteeing that its required share of water during the dry season is protected.

World.title: US Navy vessel in Tamil Nadu shipyard for repairs
World.content:
NEW DELHI: US Navy's supply ship, USNS Wally Schirra, arrived at the Kattupalli shipyard near Chennai Friday for repairs under the India-US Master Ship Repair Agreement, said govt in a statement.

The vessel is part of the US Navy's Military Sealift Command, which provides ocean transportation, logistics and specialised maritime support to US military and govt agencies worldwide.

While this marks the fifth occasion on which a US naval vessel has undertaken repairs at Kattupalli, USNS Wally Schirra is the first US naval vessel to arrive for repairs following the coming into force of the revised SOP facilitating the entry and exit of ship crew.

"This underscores India's efforts to facilitate international ship-repair operations, strengthen maritime industrial cooperation and create an enabling environment for greater utilisation of Indian shipyards," MEA said in a statement.

World.title: NIA seeks UAE's cooperation in probe of attack on Indian flydubai pilot Machchhar
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

, as part of its ongoing probe into the mid-air attack on Indian co-pilot Smit Machchhar aboard a flydubai flight, has sent a legal assistance request to UAE seeking copies of "certain documents" as well as permission to examine some people in the Gulf nation, agency chief Rakesh Aggarwal said Friday.

Machchhar was stabbed multiple times with a cockpit crash axe by his Omani co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami during the Sept 30 flight, allegedly in an attempt to hijack or crash the Israel-bound aircraft. NIA registered an FIR in the wake of the incident with the intent of probing the "larger conspiracy" behind it.

Aggarwal, while addressing the media at the end of the two-day anti-terror conference here, said UAE's response to its mutual legal assistance request is awaited.

"We will go ahead as soon as we get the legal documents or permission from UAE to join investigation," he said.

World.title: SC allows lighting of lamp at Deepathoon as one-time measure
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

Friday allowed lighting of the traditional

on Nov 24 as a one-time measure at Deepathoon - the stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram hill in

's Madurai district.

A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said only authorised persons from the temple administration and govt officials would go for the lamp lighting and restrained the public from going to the place.

It said no procession, public congregation, slogan-raising or demonstration shall be allowed during the ceremony.

"The present arrangement does not proceed on any finding that the stone pillar is or has historically been a place of customary religious observance, nor does it determine whether lighting of the lamp at the said location constitutes an essential religious practice or whether any individual, institution or denomination possess any enforceable right in that regard," the bench said.



The court, however, stayed portions of the judgement that had upheld the direction to restore the practice of lighting the lamp at Deepathoon. It clarified that the permission granted by it could not be relied on by any party as "evidence of any established custom".

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The court also barred excavation, construction and structural alterations at the disputed site. "Neither the permission nor the ceremony can be relied on as proof of custom or a right of access, or as a basis for permission in future years," it said.





For decades, the lamp was lit at the Deepa Mandapam, near the Uchipillaiyar temple on the lower slopes. Hindu groups had sought permission to light the lamp at Deepathoon, the stone pillar located higher up the hill approximately 50m from a dargah.

The dargah side told SC Thursday it was the owner of the entire hilltop of Thiruparankundram and opposed the demand by Hindu worshippers for permission to light the Karthigai Deepam.

World.title: Fake university list grows from 20 to 32 in 3 years, 18 old names still on it
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

(UGC) has issued a fresh public advisory warning students and parents against enrolling in unrecognised institutions, even as its list of fake universities has grown from 20 to 32 in three years.

More strikingly, 18 of the 20 institutions flagged in March 2023 continue to figure on the latest list, despite warnings and letters seeking action from state govts.

The Nov 17 advisory, issued following Supreme Court directions, has renewed questions over the effectiveness of action against institutions accused of illegally awarding degrees. SC's intervention followed reports of an alleged fake medical college operating from a farmhouse in Etah, Uttar Pradesh.



In its Oct 9 order, SC directed UGC and other regulators to issue public advisories cautioning prospective students against unauthorised institutions.

A comparison of UGC's March 2023 list with its Feb 2026 list showed that 90% of the originally identified institutions remain flagged. Continued inclusion, however, does not necessarily mean an institution remains operational or that no enforcement action has been taken.





Delhi accounts for the largest concentration, with 12 fake universities, up from eight in 2023. All eight institutions identified in the capital three years ago remain on the list. UP has four, while six other states and UTs have two each. UGC records revealed that the commission wrote to state education authorities in April 2023 seeking action against institutions violating UGC Act, 1956. Follow-up letters were issued in July, while a Sept communication directed the institutions concerned to submit compliance reports within 15 days.

In an Aug 2026 parliamentary reply, the education ministry said states had been asked to register FIRs and initiate steps to close unauthorised institutions. The latest advisory asks students to verify institutional recognition, authority to award degrees, course approvals and permission to operate online, distance or off-campus programmes before paying fees.

It cautions against relying solely on s, websites, brochures or social media claims, urging independent verification through official regulatory websites.

World.title: Consider law to curb marriage between relatives: SC to government
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The ordeal of a 20-year-old Bengaluru-based woman who defied serious physical conditions to gain admission to an elite law school became the trigger for a fresh

push for a

(UCC).

Moved by her plight, the court said Friday the Union govt must explore the legislative route to prevent marriage between close relatives, prevalent among Muslims and some Hindu communities in the south, to protect their offspring against genetic disorders.

Born to parents who are first cousins, the LLB student at National Law School of India University who suffers from genetic disorders photophobia and cone dystrophy, pleaded in her PIL that exceptions carved out to allow marriage between close relatives must be ended to give offspring the right to a healthy life.



"Should the law continue to retain statutory and customary exceptions that permit marriages between close blood relatives, notwithstanding established medical evidence that such unions significantly increase risk of autosomal recessive disorders, congenital anomalies, disabilities, infant morbidity and other lifelong health issues in children?" she asked.

Photophobia is an abnormal intolerance of light, while cone dystrophy causes breakdown of cone photoreceptor cells in the retina.





Children in marriages between close relatives are at greater risk of inheriting two copies of the altered recessive gene from the parents, leading to genetic disorders.

The PIL challenged the custom-based exceptions preserved in Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, and Special Marriage Act, 1954.

A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was convinced the problem would be best addressed through the legislative route rather than a symptomatic judicial antidote.

Quoting National Family Health Survey data, the petitioner said consanguineous marriages (marriages between people related by blood) were deeply entrenched in cultural, religious and social practices. According to NFHS, "13% of ever-married women were related to their husband before their marriage, and 11% of marriages were consanguineous marriages. The most common type of consanguineous marriages were marriages to first cousins (8% of all marriages).

"

The survey said, "Women in urban areas are about equally as likely to be in consanguineous marriages as women in rural areas. Muslim and Buddhist/Neo-Buddhist women are the most likely to be in consanguineous marriages." It had put the rate of such marriages among Muslims at 15.8%, among Buddhists/Neo-Buddhists at 14.5%, among Christians at 11.9%, and among Hindus at 10.1%.

The survey further said, "Women in all southern states except Kerala are much more likely to be in consanguineous marriages than women in other states.

More than one-fourth of women in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka, and almost one-fifth of women in Telangana and Puducherry reported being in consanguineous marriages."

The bench sought Centre's response on two aspects - the desirability of legislation to prevent consanguineous marriages, and an awareness campaign on possible adverse genetic disorders afflicting children from marriage between blood relatives, including making it a part of school and college curricula.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The petitioner said, "Children should not be subjected to preventable and irreversible genetic risks, especially when the law continues to defer to custom where constitutional protection, public health and child welfare are at stake."

"Consanguineous marriages pose a... demonstrable threat to public health, particularly to the right to life and health of children born out of such unions, who are disproportionately susceptible to congenital and genetic disorders bey-ond their control," she said.

World.title: In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare
World.content:
Between the pages of a logbook recording Dakshina’s treatment are ₹100, ₹50, ₹20, and ₹10 notes. Dakshina’s mother, Minnal Rani, had filed them away for her daughter’s medical expenses. The child is gone, but the money remains untouched. “We will never spend it,” she says, fighting back tears.

Dakshina was five months old when doctors detected a hole in her heart. Born on June 13, 2025, she was taken to many hospitals, including one in Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam’s capital. With surgery ruled out, she was eventually referred to a cooperative hospital at Perinthalmanna, in Malappuram district, a two-and-a-half-hour drive away from home. She died here, on April 13, 2026.

Rani and her husband Chandra Sekhar say the hospital refused to release their daughter’s body until they paid a bill of ₹10,000. They managed to raise the money with the help of a ward councillor.

“We buried her under that tree,” says Rani, pointing to a coconut tree near their house at Vechapathi hamlet in Sholayur panchayat of Attappadi, Palakkad district.

Dakshina’s death is among a series of 10 infant deaths reported this year from Attappadi, a predominantly tribal settlement. There have been four back-to-back deaths in October. Of the 10 infant deaths, six involved congenital anomalies, with heart defects among the commonly reported conditions. An expert committee of doctors and researchers is examining the deaths.

World.title: U.S. court sentences Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 235 months in jail in Pannun murder plot
World.content:
Indian national Nikhil Gupta was sentenced to 235 months in jail by a U.S. court on Friday (November 20, 2026) for his involvement in a murder-for-hire plot against a Sikh extremist on American soil.

Gupta, 55, had pleaded guilty earlier this year to charges of murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, and conspiracy to commit money laundering, in connection with his efforts to murder Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York.

Judge Victor Marrero of the Southern District of New York announced 235 months prison term to Gupta after an almost 80-minute hearing.

The judge did not impose any sentence of supervised release on Gupta, saying he will be put in deportation and removal proceedings once he completes the prison term.

Also Read | Pannun’s civil lawsuit: U.S. court allows Pannun to serve NSA Doval and former intelligence chief Goyal

Gupta, wearing a tan prison suit, was escorted into the courtroom by marshals. He scanned the room as he entered and sat flanked by his lawyers.

Gupta invoked the teachings of Mahatma Gandhi, Mother Teresa, Nelson Mandela and Martin Luther King and said he had hoped to live by the ideals of these leaders.

Gupta apologised for his actions in a brief six-minute statement that he delivered in English in court.

“I cannot undo what I have done. I am sorry to Pannun, to the community and the fraternity. I’m sorry,” Gupta said, turning to look at Pannun, who was seated in the courtroom and had several members of the Sikh community accompanying him for the hearing.

Gupta said his family, wife, mother and children have suffered and are being punished for something that they did not do.

Gupta appeared to choke and get emotional as he addressed the court. He said he would accept whatever sentence the court accords him and would come out a “better” individual after he finishes his sentence.

Pannun made his statement claiming that he has not been able to do his regular legal practice for over 1200 days since the threat to his life was uncovered.

Also Read | U.S. govt seeks 24-year prison term for Nikhil Gupta in Pannun murder-for-hire plot

Pannun spoke for about 20 minutes, and at one point during his lengthy statement, the Judge asked him to “summarise” what he wants to say and wrap up his statement so the court can move ahead with the proceedings.

In imposing the 235-month sentence, the judge said it is “reasonable and appropriate” given the nature of the crime.

The defence lawyers, speaking after the verdict, expressed disappointment over the sentence, saying they would have wanted a lesser prison term for Gupta.

Several supporters of Pannun had gathered outside the courthouse in New York with effigies of Gupta and others ahead of the hearing.

World.title: Digital planetariums, education centres will be established in all divisions: Bihar Minister
World.content:
With a view to developing a scientific temperament among students and the general public, state-of-the-art “digital planetariums and education centres” will be established in all the divisions of the state, Bihar Science and Technology Minister Sheela Kumari said on Friday (November 20, 2026).

“The district magistrates of the districts concerned have been requested to provide a minimum of two acres of land for the purpose,” Ms. Kumari said while addressing a press conference in Patna.

These centres will provide children and young people with practical knowledge of astronomy and space research, she said, while praising Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary’s leadership for the initiative.

In reply to a query, she said that these planetariums will be ready in a year.

The Minister further stated that digital planetariums/space and astronomy education centres will also be established in three districts—East Champaran, Jamui, and Purnea—as part of the Union Ministry of Culture’s Scheme for Promotion of Culture and Science (SPOCS).

“The total estimated project cost is ₹39.00 crore, which will be funded with central assistance,” she said, adding that the target is to commence construction work during the current financial year, 2026-27.

A digital planetarium uses computer software and high-resolution digital projectors (or LED panels) to display 3D simulations of the night sky, space travel, and science visuals inside a dome theatre. Unlike traditional optical-mechanical projectors that only show fixed star positions, digital systems can fly viewers through galaxies, simulate different time periods, and play full-dome films.

Ms. Kumari was accompanied by Department Secretary Himanshu Sharma and a host of other senior officials during the press conference.

In order to generate public interest in science and technology, efforts are also being made to operate mobile science exhibition buses, observatory domes, and astro parks through the National Council of Science Museums.

Notably, the state currently has two functional planetariums—one each in Patna and Darbhanga. The planetarium in Darbhanga was established in 2023, while the renovation of the Patna planetarium has already been completed.

Appointments of faculty members

A total of 1,654 regular faculty members are currently working against 3,414 sanctioned posts in Government Engineering Colleges, she said, adding that requisitions for appointments against 1,061 posts have already been sent to the Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC).

Similarly, requisitions for the appointment of 354 posts for polytechnic colleges have already been sent to the BPSC, she said and added that a total of 997 regular faculty members are currently working against 2480 sanctioned posts in Polytechnic institutions across the state.

The Bihar Technical Service Commission, Patna, has published s for the recruitment of 723 Instructor posts and 1,093 Laboratory Assistant posts in Government Engineering Colleges and Government Polytechnic Institutes, the Minister said.

A steady increase has been observed in students’ enrolment against the sanctioned seats in Government Engineering Colleges and Government Polytechnic Institutes, the Minister said, adding that out of 15,183 sanctioned seats in Government Engineering Colleges, a total of 13,492 students have been enrolled, constituting 88.86 per cent of the total seats during the academic session 2026-27.

Similarly, out of a total of 17,227 sanctioned seats, 16,453 students have secured admission, thus representing 95.50 per cent of the total seats in Government Polytechnic Institutes.

NBA accreditation

The department is making systematic efforts to obtain NBA (National Board of Accreditation) accreditation for its academic programmes, she said and added that a total of 11 Government Polytechnic Institutions have so far received NBA accreditation for 20 programmes, while applications have been submitted for getting NBA accreditation for another 48 programmes.

The Minister also informed that the Chief Minister, Samrat Choudhary, has launched the Tech Connect Portal.

Through this portal, all Government Engineering Colleges and Polytechnic Institutes will be connected on a digital platform. Their rankings will be determined on the basis of academic performance, achievements, resources and prescribed standards.

This initiative will encourage healthy competition among institutions and help improve the overall quality of technical education.

World.title: BJP’s invitation to Pakistan’s Minister vindicates Abdullah’s stance: J&K Deputy Chief Minister
World.content:
J&K Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary on Friday (November 20, 2026) said that the BJP-led government’s move to invite Pakistan’s Minister Musadik Masood Malik to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisation Dialogue Forum “vindicated the stand of National Conference (NC) president Dr. Farooq Abdullah and vice president Omar Abdullah.”

Referring to the BJP’s stance after the 2025 Pahalgam attack, Mr. Choudhary said, “The BJP will say it will not talk to Pakistan. And when Dr. Abdullah and Omar Abdullah advocate dialogue, the BJP will call them Pakistani. I want to ask the BJP: hasn’t a Pakistani Minister been invited to India on their invitation?”

He said the invitation to the Pakistani Minister proved that “the stance of my leaders was right then and is right now.” “The NC’s stance is the same as the one articulated by former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, who would say, ‘You can choose your friends, but you cannot choose your neighbours.’ One must always maintain good relations with one’s neighbours,” said Mr. Choudhary.

Asking Pakistan to end terrorism, Mr. Choudhary said, “Both Dr. Abdullah and Omar Abdullah have been asking Pakistan to end terrorism and close terror camps if Pakistan wants better relations. We stand behind our leaders.”

People’s Democratic Party legislator Muntazir Mehdi termed the Pakistani Minister’s visit to India “a welcome development” and urged the resumption of dialogue between India and Pakistan.

“The two countries share a common history and several mutual concerns, including political issues, climate change, and water-related matters, which can only be addressed through engagement and dialogue. Hostility and non-engagement cannot resolve these issues. Both countries should come to the table and resume dialogue for peace and development in the subcontinent,” he said.

World.title: Transgender persons to be roped in for tax collection in West Bengal
World.content:
The West Bengal government will engage transgender persons to collect municipal tax and spread traffic awareness. Urban Development and Municipal Affairs Minister Agnimitra Paul said the initiative, called “Brihannala Brigade”, will provide an opportunity for a dignified livelihood for the transpersons.

“The CM wishes that they (transgender people no) longer have to resort to begging at traffic signals; instead, we want to offer them an alternative, respectable livelihood. We have decided that those among them who are interested will receive training from the police and be deployed at traffic signals. Their role will be to sensitise the public about traffic rules and safety measures,” Ms. Paul said on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

She further added that another group of transgender persons would be trained to collect outstanding taxes, which could help address the staff shortage that leads to delayed collections and large pending amounts.

The Minister also added that each of these transgender individuals will be provided with training to engage in this work so that they can conduct better public interaction and do their work seamlessly. They will receive a stipend for the work, Ms. Paul said.

The West Bengal government has started an initiative to offer relief in paying outstanding property taxes, including in the actual sums and interest, to encourage defaulters to pay their outstanding balances.

According to Kolkata Municipal Corporation estimates, they have around ₹6800 crore outstanding property tax pending, including personal properties, mixed-use properties, and commercial properties.

In 2022, the previous Mamata Banerjee government decided to allow transgender persons to apply for government jobs under the general category to help them have better opportunities in employment. A Transgender Development Board was set up in 2017, but the board could not undertake many activities for the welfare of members of the community. The last census carried out in the state in 2011 put the number of transgender people in the state at 30,349. The actual number of people of the third gender may be higher, several groups working for the community say.

World.title: Trinamool supporters attacked outside the police station as police questioned Abhishek
World.content:
Supporters of Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) were allegedly attacked on Friday (November 20, 2026) by supporters of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) outside a police station while party leader Abhishek Banerjee was being questioned by Kolkata Police at the Girish Park police station.

Videos of the scuffle and the assault on women supporters of the Trinamool were shared on social media and by the Mamata AITC. In the videos, groups of women alleged to be BJP supporters were seen chasing another group of women. Supporters of the Trinamool had gathered outside the police station in support of Abhishek Banerjee. The BJP leaders denied allegations of the assault but claimed that Trinamool supporters were trying to incite tensions by gathering outside the police station.

“@BJP4Bengal workers gathered outside Girish Park Police Station today, seemingly intent on harassing, heckling and assaulting our workers, did not even spare ordinary citizens and parents who had come to pick up their children from school,” the party shared on social media. The Mamata AITC leader raised questions on the role of politics.

The police complaint against the Diamond Harbour MP was filed in connection with remarks reportedly made by him on 29 October, in which he criticised sections of the police administration, alleging that officers were acting under political pressure. Mr. Banerjee took to social media to share videos of BJP leaders, including Suvendu Adhikari, alleging threats to the police when they were in the Opposition.

After the BJP came to power, several FIRs were registered against Abhishek Banerjee. He has been summoned to appear before the police on numerous occasions. Later in the day, the Trinamool leader filed a Zero FIR at Girish Park Police Station, highlighting how Suvendu Adhikari, Dilip Ghosh, and other BJP leaders threatened the Kolkata Police and the West Bengal Police on multiple occasions.

“The expertise and urgency shown by Girish Park PS in connection with Abhishek Banerjee’s matter—we hope the same expertise and urgency will be shown by them in connection with this Zero FIR, and that they will investigate the matter,” Arka Nag, an advocate representing Trinamool Congress leader, said.

World.title: Chandel district official issues advisory after spurious liquor kills 11 in Manipur
World.content:
Manipur’s Chandel district administration on Friday (November 20, 2026) issued an advisory, urging people to report suspected manufacturing, storage, sale or distribution of adulterated liquor.

The public advisory followed the death of 11 people due to consumption of spurious liquor in the district’s Chakpikarong Sub-Division. The deaths have been reported since Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

According to a statement from the Chief Minister’s Office, 180 others are undergoing treatment at two private hospitals in Imphal. Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited these hospitals on Friday and took stock of the treatment being provided to the patients.

Advising the general public to exercise utmost caution, the district administration said the cause of the deaths was yet to be “medically and scientifically established”. It asked people to refrain from consuming locally brewed liquor or alcoholic beverages of doubtful origin, particularly from suspected sources in the affected areas.

“Any person experiencing vomiting, abdominal pain, headache, dizziness, blurred vision, breathing difficulty or other unusual symptoms following alcohol consumption should immediately seek medical attention at the nearest facility,” the advisory read.

It also advised people who may have consumed liquor from the same suspected source to seek medical evaluation even if they are not experiencing symptoms.

“The public is requested to report suspected manufacturing, storage, sale or distribution of adulterated liquor to the nearest police station or the concerned authorities,” the advisory further read, requesting village authorities, civil society organisations, women’s organisations and youth clubs to assist in spreading awareness.

The Manipur government partially lifted 30 years of alcohol prohibition in December 2023, although extremist groups in the State continue to target liquor businesses. Years of prohibition led to certain areas turning into local liquor dens, selling alcoholic beverages of suspect quality.

Spurious liquor has claimed lives in other northeastern States where prohibition is enforced. For instance, 23 people were killed in Nagaland’s Mokokchung and Tuensang districts about two months ago.

World.title: PM to visit Bihar to inaugurate a six-lane bridge named after ex-CM Nitish
World.content:
On the completion of one year of NDA government rule in Bihar, Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit the Vaishali district on November 21 to inaugurate a six-lane bridge and lay the foundation stone for several other projects. PM Modi is also likely to address a public meeting after the scheduled ceremonies in the district.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to inaugurate a 9.76 km long ₹5,500 crore six-lane bridge on the River Ganga, connecting Kacchi Dargah in Patna district to Bidupur in the neighbouring Vaishali district. The government has named the bridge after former Chief Minister and ruling NDA ally Nitish Kumar as “Nitish Setu.”

The Opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal recently raised objections, claiming that the bridge was conceived in 2015 when the Mahagathbandhan (grand alliance) government was in power in the State, and the party has also demanded that the bridge be named after RJD chief Lalu Prasad.

RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav, who is also the leader of the Opposition in the State Assembly, and his parents Lalu Prasad and Rabri Devi, have been representing the flood-prone Raghopur for several terms in the Assembly and the constituency has been a bastion of the Other Backward Class “Yadav” caste for long.

“Nitish Setu will make travel between north and south Bihar smoother and faster, offering significant benefits to the people of Patna, Vaishali, and surrounding districts,” Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary said. However, RJD national working president Tejashwi Yadav took a dig at this, expressing wonder: “I’ve heard that such bridges or monuments are only named after people who are no more. I guess the BJP, by naming the bridge as Nitish Setu, has gobbled up Nitish Kumar, and he doesn’t exist for them.”

However, JD(U) working president Sanjay Kumar Jha said that “the decision of Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary to name the bridge as Nitish Setu symbolises the immense affection, respect, and gratitude that the people of Bihar have for our leader Nitish Kumar ji.”

For the first time in the state, senior BJP leader Samrat Choudhary became Chief Minister in April 2026, replacing the ruling alliance leader of JD(U), Nitish Kumar. Mr. Kumar’s son, Nishant Kumar, is the Health Minister in Mr. Choudhary’s cabinet. Following in the footsteps of his predecessor and former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary is likely to embark on his statewide tour on November 26, 2026, from the West Champaran district.

Meanwhile, BJP sources in Bihar said that Union Home Minister and senior party leader Amit Shah might visit Bihar next month, though “the place and exact date of his visit have not been confirmed yet”.

World.title: Minister insists referendum on new provinces 'will happen'
World.content:
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry on Friday insisted that a referendum on the formation of new provinces “will happen”.

The remarks come after PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari delivered a no-holds-barred speech on Tuesday that covered the question of new provinces.

Bilawal had expressed his opposition to the creation of provinces and the idea of holding a referendum for such a move in his speech. He cautioned that any “forced” attempt to divide provinces, particularly in Sindh, could lead to bloodshed.

However, the federal government maintains that a referendum is a legal and constitutional method of gauging public opinion on new provinces and that no political party should have reservations regarding it.

Speaking to the Geo News programme ‘Naya Pakistan’ on Friday, Chaudhry, when asked about the referendum, insisted that developing consensus on the matter should be a priority for the ruling coalition.

“National consensus is very important on the issue of new provinces,” the minister said, highlighting that the PTI-led opposition was also in favour of it.

Chaudhry said that the process of taking the public’s opinion cannot be stopped if a single party opposes it.

“The referendum will happen,” the minister insisted, adding that the PML-N would undertake “every last effort” to convince the PPP.

“A referendum is neither non-constitutional nor undemocratic; the public’s opinion can be sought on any important matter,” he remarked.

Asked about the timeline for the proposed move, Chaudhry said it was premature to talk about it. However, he added that “things will be clarified soon”.

Asked if PML-N supremo Nawaz Sharif was on board with the referendum, Chaudhry answered in the affirmative.

“One hundred per cent. The prime minister does not make any major decisions without his opinion,” he added.

On being asked if the PPP may join the opposition with the PTI and the Jamiat-Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F), Chaudhry maintained that the party included “mature and seasoned politicians”, expressing hope that it would continue in its role as a coalition partner.

“I believe matters will not reach a point where they might have to exit the coalition, as we will make sure to onboard them on the decision and vice versa,” he added.

In response to a question over Bilawal’s recent remarks and whether they were “justified”, he said that the PPP chairman had the right to present the party’s perspective on the formation of new provinces. However, he warned Bilawal against invoking other matters and targeting the PML-N.

“Attacking us [PML-N] or invoking other matters that have nothing to do with the debate related to the provinces was uncalled for.”

Chaudhry was also asked whether the government’s stance on the creation of provinces and the proposed referendum had been delivered to President Asif Ali Zardari in his meeting with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi a day earlier.

To this, he said that various matters had been discussed during the meeting in Islamabad. However, the main topic was the recent verbal confrontation between the coalition partners, he added.

Chaudhry said that during the meeting, both President Zardari and PM Shehbaz decided to resolve all the differences through dialogue. He added that the matters between the allied parties had returned to “usual”.

“Most of the matters have backtracked,” the minister remarked.

The PML-N leader said the party leadership would decide when to bring the party’s perspective on new provinces to the media.

Chaudhry also said that before making the remarks publicly, Bilawal should have taken PM Shehbaz into confidence.

“It is clear that the PPP will not exit the coalition,” he reiterated, referring to Bilawal’s comments about the prime minister completing his five-year term in office.

Over the past few months, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has whipped up a political storm since he called for the formation of new administrative units in the country, saying the current “system” of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”.

On November 12, Naqvi also floated the idea of holding a referendum to gauge public opinion on the issue, saying the exercise could settle the contentious debate once and for all.

However, Bilawal, in his hard-hitting speech on Tuesday, termed the referendum an “unconstitutional move”, vowing that his party would stand against any such measure.

Bilawal, as well as Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah and other senior party leaders, has repeatedly declared that the division of Sindh was neither legally nor politically acceptable to the party.

Soon after Bilawal’s remarks, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar defended the move, saying it was a legal and constitutional method of gauging public opinion.

Meanwhile, the JUI-F voiced its support for Bilawal’s opposition to a referendum, warning that it could be misused. The party termed Bilawal’s statements “realistic” and viewed them in high regard.

Against this backdrop, the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan has also called for a nationwide referendum on the creation of new administrative units, proposing that the exercise be held before the start of 2027 to allow people to decide the future administrative structure of the country.

Asif hopes ‘resolution will soon be reached’

Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, speaking to Geo News show ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Sath’, expressed hope that “some resolution will be reached” between the coalition partners on the issue of creating new provinces; however, he warned that certain politicians, without naming anyone, wanted to maintain “personal fiefdoms” over provinces.

“We have to drop this idea that a certain province in its current form is a personal fiefdom [..] I don’t want to take any names, but this is unacceptable,” he remarked, urging politicians to avoid pursuing personal agendas.

“I don’t want to sabotage any evolving situation, but the personal agendas of politicians have been brought to the surface,” he said, pointing out that the PPP had been pushing for a province in South Punjab for a long time.

Asif maintained that the creation of provinces was “not a political, but rather an administrative division for improved service delivery”.

However, Asif expressed confidence that a resolution will soon be found.

At the same time, referring to Bilawal’s comments warning of bloodshed in case of division of Sindh, Asif warned, “When you warn of bloodshed, you are attacking the state [..] they (PPP) should have clarity on this.”

On being asked if PM Shehbaz was making efforts towards the creation of fresh administrative units and if it meant that he had the “blessing” of Nawaz, Asif said, “Can anyone advance independently without Nawaz Sharif’s blessing [..] he is our leader [..] we want to pursue a solution where all stakeholders are on the same page.”

Asif also called on president Zardari to “intervene” so matters may be resolved.

World.title: Petrol price reduced by Re1 per litre; diesel increased by Rs2 per litre
World.content:
The government on Friday reduced the price of petrol by Re1 per litre while raising that of diesel by Rs2 per litre, after snapping a 12-day streak of consecutive reductions in the rate of petrol the previous day.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs322 per litre and HSD at Rs357 on Nov 21 (Saturday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

Following Tuesday’s reduction of the petrol price to Rs325 per litre, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar highlighted the government’s “proactive measures including policy changes and structural reforms in petroleum policy” that had brought prices back down from their April 3 peak and provided relief through a fuel subsidy scheme.

“The government of Pakistan remains committed to continue making all possible efforts to ease the financial burden on the common man amid global challenges,” he said.

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation.

The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

Since July 17 , the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: CTD says 3 terrorists, including mastermind of Kohat police lines attack, killed in IBO
World.content:
PESHAWAR: The Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) on Friday claimed to have killed three terrorists of the banned Ittehadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), including the mastermind of the Kohat Police Lines attack in September.

The three were killed in an intelligence-based operation (IBO) carried out in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Kohat, following information about presence of the group members in the area, a CTD statement said.

According to an official statement, the Kohat CTD received intelligence that armed terrorists of the banned IMP had set up a checkpoint on Bazeed Khel Road in Kohat. Following the lead, the CTD and district police launched a joint IBO at around 6:30pm.

“When police and CTD teams reached the location, the terrorists opened indiscriminate fire. The teams effectively retaliated in self-defence,” the statement said.

After the exchange of fire, a search operation was conducted in the area where the teams found the bodies of the suspected terrorists, while some of their associates escaped.

The statement read that according to preliminary information, two of the suspected terrorists killed had been identified as Abdul Hai and Abdul Rashid.

Hai belonged to Kohat and was the mastermind of the Kohat Police Lines suicide attack, in which at least 21 people, including 15 police officials, were martyred and over 100 were wounded.
